crunchbase.full_description:
ChowNow is an ordering platform dedicated to helping local restaurants grow and compete in a sustainable way. ChowNow helps local restaurants thrive. By helping diners discover the restaurants' delicious creations and helping restaurants connect with customers. ChowNow powers branded online ordering systems for independent restaurants via the restaurants’ own websites, on Facebook and Google pages, through ChowNow-created apps, and via ChowNow’s website, while also providing the restaurant partners key customer insights and marketing support.

The company does its services for a reasonable monthly fee, without the predatory third-party commissions charged by competitors. It also enables diners to connect with independent restaurants in communities to order takeout and in some cases delivery, in a way that’s sustainable and fair to restaurants.

ChowNow was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Playa Vista, California.

updates.text: Sometimes the message you need to hear comes when you least expect it. Last week, I had the opportunity to attend the HPSI National Conference in Salt Lake City. I met wonderful people, had great conversations, made new connections, and came away with plenty of insights. But one message in particular stayed with me. Our motivational speaker was José Hernández, a former NASA astronaut whose incredible story was portrayed in the movie A Million Miles Away. His story is remarkable, but it was his journey that really stuck with me: Anything is possible when you have a goal, create a roadmap, and stay persistent. He shared a simple three-part strategy for pursuing your goals. I've been thinking about it ever since: 1️⃣ Do we know the minimum requirements necessary to get where we want to go? Understand what it takes to reach the goal and make sure we're willing to do the work required to get there. 2️⃣ Are we studying the people we want to become? Look at the people who have already achieved what we're working toward. What are they doing? What can we learn from them? 3️⃣ Do we know what differentiates us from our competition? Understand what makes us unique and figure out how to use that difference to our advantage. Simple? Yes. Easy? Not necessarily. But incredibly actionable. No matter what stage of life or our career we're in, we always have an opportunity to change our trajectory. Set the goal. Visualize it. Create the roadmap. Stay the course. José's message has me revisiting my own goals, not just where I want to go, but what I'm willing to do to get there. If you're interested in learning more about José's journey, his book Reaching for the Stars is a great place to start. It is now on my reading list! What goal are you working toward right now and what's on your roadmap to get there? P.S. Check out Arin Perrott and I attending the HPSI Afternoon Food Show! #Leadership #ProfessionalDevelopment #Persistence #Foodservice

updates.text_html: Sometimes the message you need to hear comes when you least expect it. Last week, I had the opportunity to attend the HPSI National Conference in Salt Lake City. I met wonderful people, had great conversations, made new connections, and came away with plenty of insights. But one message in particular stayed with me. Our motivational speaker was José Hernández, a former NASA astronaut whose incredible story was portrayed in the movie A Million Miles Away. His story is remarkable, but it was his journey that really stuck with me: Anything is possible when you have a goal, create a roadmap, and stay persistent. He shared a simple three-part strategy for pursuing your goals. I've been thinking about it ever since: 1️⃣ Do we know the minimum requirements necessary to get where we want to go? Understand what it takes to reach the goal and make sure we're willing to do the work required to get there. 2️⃣ Are we studying the people we want to become? Look at the people who have already achieved what we're working toward. What are they doing? What can we learn from them? 3️⃣ Do we know what differentiates us from our competition? Understand what makes us unique and figure out how to use that difference to our advantage. Simple? Yes. Easy? Not necessarily. But incredibly actionable. No matter what stage of life or our career we're in, we always have an opportunity to change our trajectory. Set the goal. Visualize it. Create the roadmap. Stay the course. José's message has me revisiting my own goals, not just where I want to go, but what I'm willing to do to get there. If you're interested in learning more about José's journey, his book Reaching for the Stars is a great place to start. It is now on my reading list! What goal are you working toward right now and what's on your roadmap to get there? P.S. Check out Arin Perrott and I attending the HPSI Afternoon Food Show! #Leadership #ProfessionalDevelopment #Persistence #Foodservice

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
We’ve grown to become the largest family-operated broadline food service distributor in North America by upholding the same business approach since 1897—being passionately committed to the people we serve. We believe in the power of good food—to bring people together and make moments special. Every product, every order, and every decision we make is inspired by the people on the other side of the plate.

We distribute to foodservice operators throughout the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast  and Southwest regions of the U.S. and coast to coast in Canada. 

Our company also operates more than 170 Gordon Food Service Stores, which are open to the public and provide the benefits of restaurant-quality products and friendly, knowledgeable service. Gordon Food Service Stores do not charge a membership fee. 

Gordon Food Service Stores are the primary supplier for many small foodservice operators, including: restaurants, churches, daycare providers, caterers, event planners, and other small businesses. 

We offer a broad range of employment opportunities throughout our corporate offices, distribution centers, and retail stores. We have a strong commitment to our employees and foster an environment that promotes internal growth, training, and career development opportunities. 

Gordon Food Service is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any person on the basis of age, sex, race, religion, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

linkedin_company.about: ABOUT LITTLE CAESARS® Little Caesars, the Best Value in Pizza*, was founded by Mike and Marian Ilitch as a single, family-owned restaurant in 1959 and is headquartered in downtown Detroit, Michigan. It is the third-largest pizza chain in the world, with restaurants in each of the 50 U.S. states and 31 countries and territories. Known for its HOT-N-READY® pizza, Crazy Puffs®, and famed Crazy Bread®, Little Caesars uses quality ingredients, like fresh, never-frozen mozzarella and Muenster cheese and sauce made from fresh-packed, vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. The brand is known for innovation and is home to the exclusive Pizza Portal® pickup, a heated, self-service mobile order pickup station. Little Caesars is also the Official Pizza Sponsor of the NFL. A high-growth company with over 65 years in the $150 billion worldwide pizza industry, Little Caesars continually looks for franchisee candidates to join the team in markets worldwide. In addition to providing the opportunity for entrepreneurial independence in a franchise system, Little Caesars offers a simple operating system, a reputation for taste and value, and strong brand awareness with one of the most recognized characters in the country, Little Caesar. Little Caesars is proud to be part of the Ilitch Companies family of businesses. For more, visit LittleCaesars.com and follow Little Caesars on TikTok, Instagram, and X. *Limited to top 4 national pizza chains

updates.text: Last September 8, the Little Caesars Love Kitchen rolled into Byrd Barr Place, bringing hot pizza, connection, and a whole lot of community spirit to Seattle. We are grateful to everyone who joined us and helped make the day memorable. A special thank you to Little Caesars, the NFL, and the Seattle Seahawks for choosing Byrd Barr Place as a host site for this community celebration. We are also deeply grateful for the generous $50,000 donation, an investment that helps strengthen the work happening here every day. Partnerships like these create opportunities to come together, celebrate community, and build a stronger foundation for what comes next. Thank you for showing up for Byrd Barr Place and the people we serve. Keep showing up for community. As the nation’s leading natural cheese packager, Great Lakes Cheese serves grocery, club and super stores, as well as restaurant chains and foodservice distributors. Family- and employee-owned, Great Lakes Cheese celebrated their 60th year of business in 2018. Since then, Great Lakes Cheese has grown to a multi-billion dollar revenue company. The company remains privately owned by the Epprecht Family and over 4,000 dedicated employee-owners. In 1998, the Epprecht Family established an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), which gives all employee-owners a shared 20% stake in the company.

updates.text: Happy #NationalCheeseDay ! 🧀💛 It takes time, tradition, and an incredible amount of dedication to produce your savory favorites—and at Great Lakes Cheese, our family of employee-owners puts that dedication into practice every single day with every package we produce. As the nation’s leading natural cheese packager, we are proud to provide an affordable, nutritious staple that fuels families across the country. In fact, you’ve likely enjoyed our cheese without even knowing it! From the melted perfection on top of a slice from your local pizza shop to the packs you grab off the shelf at your go-to grocer, our hands help craft the products that bring people together. According to the International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA), the American cheese industry has grown into a phenomenal powerhouse, with more than one-third of all U.S. milk production dedicated to cheese. We are honored to lead the way, growing alongside consumer appetites while staying true to the craft and quality behind every single block. From our plants to your plate, thank you for making what we do possible!

updates.text: At Casey’s, great customer service is about more than completing a transaction. It's about creating meaningful connections that make guests feel welcomed, valued, and appreciated every time they visit. Recently, guests took the time to recognize two team members who exemplify that commitment to service: Charles from our Mount Enterprise, Texas store and Delanoe from one of our Oklahoma City stores. One guest shared that whenever Charles is working, they know their visit will be a great one. From remembering names and favorite orders to greeting guests with a smile, Charles creates memorable experiences that make guests feel more like family than customers. Another guest reached out to recognize Delanoe for the way he consistently treats everyone with calm, respect, and dignity. Whether it's a regular guest, a first-time visitor, or someone having a tough day, he makes people feel seen, heard, and valued. Every guest interaction is an opportunity to make a lasting impression, and that's exactly what Charles and Delanoe do each day. Through their dedication to serving others and creating welcoming experiences, they help turn everyday visits into meaningful connections. Charles and Delanoe, thank you for showing what outstanding service looks like and for making such a positive impact on our guests. We're proud to have you on the Casey's team. 👇 Help us celebrate Charles, Delanoe, and the many Casey's team members who create memorable experiences for our guests every day in the comments! #CaseysCARES #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys #TeamCaseys #CustomerServiceWeek

updates.text: 🏈 College football is back! And with more than 30 noon kickoffs in the first three weeks of the season, we set out to find the earliest-rising fanbase in Casey's Country. 🏆 The winner? Ohio State. Our all-new Casey's Tailgate Tracker also found that 9 in 10 college football fans eat pizza on gameday, with half of them grabbing their first slice before noon kickoffs. From breakfast pizza at the early-morning tailgate to fan favorites through the final whistle, Casey's is built to fuel football fans all gameday long. updates.text: For more than two decades, Domino’s® and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital - ALSAC ® have shared a belief in the power of hope. St. Jude has been Domino’s national charity partner since our first Thanks & Giving® campaign in 2004, and we are continually inspired by the generosity of our customers, franchisees and team members who help bring its lifesaving mission to life. Through this year’s campaign, customers can support children and families facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases by choosing the St. Jude Giving Combo, with $1 from each combo going to St. Jude, or by rounding up their order. Because of generous donors, families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing or food, so they can focus on what matters most: helping their child live, celebrate milestones and make memories together. Together, we can help St. Jude continue its mission: Finding cures. Saving children. ® Since the beginning of our partnership, Domino’s has raised more than $165 million for the kids of St. Jude, with a commitment to raise a total of $300 million by 2034. Join us in helping St. Jude give more children the greatest gift of all...time.

updates.text: Fire Prevention Month is here, and some Domino’s customers may get more than pizza at their door. 🚒👀 Throughout this month, participating franchise-owned stores across the U.S. are teaming up with local fire departments for surprise pizza deliveries via fire engine and free smoke alarm checks. If the customer’s smoke alarms work, the order is free. If not, firefighters will replace the batteries or install working alarms at no cost. Either way, it’s a win! For 19 years, we’ve proudly partnered with the National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ) and local fire departments to promote fire safety. Thank you to the NFPA and firefighters nationwide for helping keep our customers and communities safe.

updates.text: RUN. SLICE. REPEAT. 🍕🏃♀️ En agosto con Sbarro , realizamos una colaboración juanto a adidas en el marco de la Media Maratón de Buenos Aires, uno de los eventos deportivos más importantes del año, llevando The Original NY Pizza XXL a la comunidad de adidas Runners. Fui parte de la acción desde un lugar que disfruto mucho: la creación y cobertura de contenido en tiempo real, buscando capturar esos momentos que hacen a la experiencia: la alegría de cada runner al cruzar la meta y luego, por supuesto, disfrutar una slice de Sbarro. También trabajamos en el desarrollo de una cápsula especial de comunicación, junto a Lucia Cosimanoy Romina Ormazabal . Una colaboración que nos permitió descubrir un punto de conexión entre dos marcas con mundos diferentes y construir una experiencia relevante para sus comunidades. Mención especial al equipo de Cinco Yardas por acompañarnos en esta acción. 🤝

Pratt was founded in the USA some 20 years ago and, since then, has shown dramatic growth with sophisticated manufacturing facilities in more than 25 states.

updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

updates.text: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. updates.text_html: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. linkedin_company.about: We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now. The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

crunchbase.full_description:
At Round Table, we’ve enjoyed a heritage of creating high quality, innovative pizzas for over 57 years. From our founder Bill Larson’s first little Round Table Pizza Parlor in Menlo Park, California in 1959 to 450 thriving restaurants today, Round Table has always stood for freshness, innovation and craveable flavors in everything we serve.
Most pizza chains use primarily frozen dough, and often skimp on both the quality and quantity of their toppings and ingredients to cut costs. Not at Round Table. We roll our dough fresh, from scratch, every day, in every restaurant. That dough is made from wheat grown for us on family farms in Idaho. Our cheddar cheese is aged to perfection, and combined with whole milk mozzarella and provolone in our famous three–cheese blend. We use only premium meats for our toppings, which we spread lavishly on every pizza, all the way to the edge of the crust. And our vegetable toppings are freshly cut at each restaurant, including our juicy, selectively–picked tomatoes. This commitment to quality and authenticity is why we say we’re “The Last Honest Pizza.”
While we’re proud of the ingredients we use, Round Table is more than just freshness and quality. We’re the place where you’ll find unique, innovative pizza creations that expertly combine flavors no one else can match. Over the years we’ve introduced more than 30 successful new products, including many that are mainstays of our menu today. There’s the legendary King Arthur’s Supreme, with pepperoni, Italian sausage, Italian dry salami, linguica, mushrooms, green peppers, yellow onions, black olives, three cheeses and our Zesty Red Sauce. And the Wombo Combo, featuring primo pepperoni, linguica, Italian sausage, crisp bacon, mushrooms, Roma tomatoes, artichoke hearts and green onions. There are many more delightful combinations to choose from, or you can select your crust, sauce and toppings and create your own masterpiece. With appetizers like our Garlic Parmesan Twists, and salad bars offering an array of fresh selections, Round Table presents a feast of flavors that bring our guests back again and again, whether they choose to dine in, carry out or have us deliver.
There are a lot of places that serve pizza. But there’s no one else with the freshness and flavors you’ll always find at the best place for pizza: your neighborhood Round Table — The Last Honest Pizza.

updates.text: So we're back from NACS 2026, and honestly, we were surprised by what we heard on the show floor. It wasn't the sound of pitching, buzzwords, or typical conference chatter. It was the hum of skepticism. Customers had more questions this year than we've ever experienced before. Not because innovation has stalled, but because the stakes feel higher. AI was at the center of many of those conversations. Retailers recognize the opportunity, just as they once recognized the value of SEO. They know it has the potential to drive discovery, efficiency, and growth. What they're still trying to understand is how to capture that value without introducing unnecessary risk. One concern came up repeatedly: Will adding new value cost us the value we've already built? It's a challenge we understand because it's one we face ourselves. Large organizations can't afford to disrupt operations, customer experiences, or business continuity in pursuit of the next trend. That's why we've designed our solutions around a simple belief: innovation shouldn't require a tradeoff. Retailers shouldn't have to choose between what's working today and what will help them compete tomorrow. If you're asking the same questions, let's talk. Our team works with retailers every day to navigate these decisions and identify opportunities that support innovation without disrupting the experiences, operations, and outcomes that already drive success. Book a conversation with our team here: https://lnkd.in/gvFfcYyH

updates.text: Throughout history, every breakthrough has arrived with the same promise: Electricity. The internet. Mobile. Cloud. And now, AI. Each changed the world. But none created value simply because someone bought it. The winners weren't the organizations that adopted the technology first. They were the organizations that understood why they were adopting it. That's what stood out in Nick and Andy's conversation at NACS. Before AI. Before automation. Before modernization. Comes insight. What problem are you solving? What friction are you removing? What customer need are you addressing? Because ROI isn't just Return on Investment. It's the Result of Insight. Technology can accelerate almost anything. The question is whether it's accelerating a clear strategy or simply speeding up confusion. The investment comes after the insight. Not before it. crunchbase.full_description: Restaurant Depot is a members-only wholesale cash and carry foodservice supplier, catering to the needs of the foodservice industry, including restaurants, caterers, and bakers. It offers a wide range of products from bakery supplies to fresh and frozen meats. The company operates large warehouse-style stores designed to offer a wide selection of products at low prices by eliminating traditional distribution costs. Its model allows customers to purchase items in bulk or by individual units with no minimum purchase requirement, helping businesses manage costs efficiently. Restaurant Depot emphasizes one-stop shopping, offering categories such as fresh produce, meat, seafood, dairy, dry groceries, and kitchen equipment under one roof. The company also provides free membership, enabling eligible businesses to access discounted pricing and convenient in-store purchasing seven days a week.

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

Everything you see (and hear) is the real deal. The score is built entirely from the sounds of a working restaurant. The ticket printer became a synth. The fryer became a cymbal. Card taps and clanking dishes became the drums. And we dropped, dunked, and splashed the Handheld right along with it. Available now. See it at https://lnkd.in/eyUVWTSR Shoutout to Dan Mufson, the incredible composer who turned real restaurant sounds into a beat. 👏 #RestaurantTech #Hospitality #RestaurantOperators #SpotOn

updates.text: "It doesn't matter if we have two tables or 20. Crush it. Create something for a guest. They're gonna remember that forever." That's the standard at Port Union, a modern American restaurant in Chicago's Wicker Park from Chef Rodolfo Cuadros. Switching to a new POS wasn't an easy sell for the team. After a long time on one system, the comfort zone was real. SpotOn’s support is what won them over. With brunch about to launch and a whole new menu to build, one call to SpotOn got this answer: "Send me the menu and I'll do it for you." A simple tool to drive reviews mattered too, especially for a new restaurant still building its reputation. With SpotOn Mobile Pay & Review, guests leave a review right as they pay. That helps search visibility and builds trust with the next guest. Hit play for the full story 👇 #ShiftStories #RestaurantTech #RestaurantOwner #Hospitality #ChicagoRestaurants

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

SpotOn’s mission is to give small and midsize businesses a fighting chance, providing innovative software and payment solutions, supported by local and personal service, and delivered at a fair price. A leader in fully integrated restaurant management systems and small business technology, SpotOn offers end-to-end solutions which include marketing, website development, reservations, online ordering, appointments, eCommerce, digital loyalty, review management, as well as retail and restaurant point-of-sale (POS) solutions.

Doron Friedman, Matt Hyman, and Zach Hyman co-founded SpotOn in 2017 and its headquarters is located in San Francisco, California.

products_and_services.product_description: A cloud-based point-of-sale and restaurant management system for processing payments, managing menus and tables, handling orders, and viewing sales and labor reports.
Integrated payment processing for in-person, online, virtual-terminal, and invoicing transactions through SpotOn’s restaurant and small-business systems.
A commission-free online ordering and delivery solution that connects restaurant websites, guest ordering apps, delivery services, menus, payments, and the SpotOn POS.
A POS-integrated labor management platform for scheduling, labor forecasting, employee coordination, tip management, and payroll preparation.
Proprietary restaurant POS hardware including countertop stations, handheld POS devices, guest-facing displays, card readers, printers, cash drawers, and connectivity equipment.
A restaurant reservation and front-of-house management system for online bookings, waitlists, table layouts, guest information, reminders, and POS synchronization.

updates.text: The People Behind the Product: Meet Cory Behind every Grande product is a dedicated Associate who takes pride in getting the details right. For Cory, being a cheesemaker means never taking shortcuts. From monitoring the precision of the cheesemaking process to knowing when a batch meets Grande's standards, his role combines experience, skill, and attention to detail. "What surprises people most is how precise cheesemaking really is," says Cory. "If one parameter is off by even a little bit, it affects the cheese." After working hard to become a cheesemaker, Cory has developed a genuine passion for the craft and takes pride in knowing every batch is made with quality, care, and consistency. When asked what he wants consumers to know, his answer is simple: "Every single batch is made with pride and passion." #Grande #ManufacturingMonth
updates.title: Grande Cheese Company

updates.text: Simple ingredients. High standards. Our cheese starts with just four simple ingredients: milk, proprietary cultures, salt, and enzymes. No fillers. No artificial ingredients. No whiteners. And while the ingredient list is simple, the dedication, expertise, and attention to detail required to transform those ingredients into the quality our customers trust is anything but. It's a commitment Grande Associates uphold every day, because excellence doesn't come from adding more. It comes from doing things the right way.

updates.text: The People Behind the Product: Meet Val Behind every Grande product is a dedicated Associate who takes pride in making it the best it can be. For Valerie, every piece of hand-tied cheese represents a commitment to craftsmanship, quality, and tradition. After 13 years at Grande, her passion for learning and taking on new challenges led her to become an expert at the hand-tying process. Hand-tying is a traditional artisan process where each cheese is individually rope-tied, smoked, and cured. It's work that requires patience and attention to detail, something Val enjoys most about the role. When asked what makes her proud of the work she does, her answer is simple: "Great team, great cheese, and great pride.” #Grande #ManufacturingMonth

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

linkedin_company.about: We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now. The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

Blaze Pizza leads in the fast-casual artisan pizza category that uses an assembly line format to create pizzas at lightning fast speed.

Each Blaze Pizza restaurant makes its own dough from scratch using a recipe that requires a 24-hour fermentation period to produce its signature light-as-air, crisp crust. Guests watch as each perfectly proofed dough ball is pressed into a generous 12-inch crust. Pizzas are made in front of the customer using an assembly line format and are ready in two minutes. Blaze Pizza's menu also features signature salads, fresh lemonades, craft beer and wine and house-made S'more Pies, and also offers gluten-free dough and vegan cheese.

updates.text: A POS without built-in text marketing is like a margarita without tequila. It's basically just a glass full of lime juice and salt. Long gone are the days when a restaurant POS was a sleek cash register. Nearly every customer interaction passes through a modern POS in some form, accumulating a continuous record of guest behavior. When guest communication tools like text marketing are built in to that environment to create a unified marketing engine, marketing messages can be defined by what guests have actually done rather than by static assumptions. If marketing tools need to be bolted on to that environment...lime juice and salt. And did you know that text messages have a 95-99% read rate? For more delicious stats and more about how a modern POS can take advantage of customer behavior data to drive growth, check out this article on SourceForge .

updates.text: "We consistently see that the biggest drivers of guest dissatisfaction aren't price alone." "According to HungerRush data, it's things like long wait times, inaccurate orders, or poor customer service. Fixing those issues can have just as much impact on how guests perceive value as a discount could." — Shannon Chirone, SVP of Marketing, HungerRush A new era of value wars in QSR is heating up, but slashing prices isn't the only answer. updates.text: Is it time to renew your POS contract? Before you do, here are a few questions worth asking. Does your POS scale? Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

updates.text: Film photography is more than 150 years old, yet modern technology has allowed it to thrive to this day. Sound familiar? For more than a century, our cooperative has been built and strengthened by the hard work of generations of member-owners. This National Farmer's Day, we're celebrating what it means to be Rooted In Tomorrow through a unique lens: specifically, the lens of a Houghton Ensign-Cupid film camera that's just one year younger than our 105-year-old cooperative. updates.text: Film photography -- an art form that’s more than 150 years old -- has been able to evolve and adapt, enabling it to thrive in a modern era. Land O'Lakes, Inc. has lasted more than 100 years because of the durability of the cooperative model, the resiliency of our member-owners and their willingness to evolve and adapt. With traditions rooted in generations of family farming, they’re able to augment age-old farming methods with cutting-edge technology to keep up with the demands of a modern, global food system. “I think of it often when I’m working in the field. I know that field has been worked by someone in my family for the last 150 years, and I’ve got a grandkid riding with me in the tractor. That’s what American agriculture is all about. It’s more than an occupation. It’s a lifestyle and commitment to feeding the planet.” Sift through more photos of a modern farm captured through a 100-year-old camera right here: https://lnkd.in/gSYAWabz

updates.text: A POS without built-in text marketing is like a margarita without tequila. It's basically just a glass full of lime juice and salt. Long gone are the days when a restaurant POS was a sleek cash register. Nearly every customer interaction passes through a modern POS in some form, accumulating a continuous record of guest behavior. When guest communication tools like text marketing are built in to that environment to create a unified marketing engine, marketing messages can be defined by what guests have actually done rather than by static assumptions. If marketing tools need to be bolted on to that environment...lime juice and salt. And did you know that text messages have a 95-99% read rate? For more delicious stats and more about how a modern POS can take advantage of customer behavior data to drive growth, check out this article on SourceForge .

Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? HungerRush is the POS partner behind every great guest experience. Get in touch.

updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

updates.text: A POS without built-in text marketing is like a margarita without tequila. It's basically just a glass full of lime juice and salt. Long gone are the days when a restaurant POS was a sleek cash register. Nearly every customer interaction passes through a modern POS in some form, accumulating a continuous record of guest behavior. When guest communication tools like text marketing are built in to that environment to create a unified marketing engine, marketing messages can be defined by what guests have actually done rather than by static assumptions. If marketing tools need to be bolted on to that environment...lime juice and salt. And did you know that text messages have a 95-99% read rate? For more delicious stats and more about how a modern POS can take advantage of customer behavior data to drive growth, check out this article on SourceForge .

updates.text: "We consistently see that the biggest drivers of guest dissatisfaction aren't price alone." "According to HungerRush data, it's things like long wait times, inaccurate orders, or poor customer service. Fixing those issues can have just as much impact on how guests perceive value as a discount could." — Shannon Chirone, SVP of Marketing, HungerRush A new era of value wars in QSR is heating up, but slashing prices isn't the only answer. As The Food Institute reports, fast-food chains are navigating one of the most complex economic environments in recent memory, with lower-income consumers pulling back and even middle-class diners spending more intentionally. According to HungerRush data, 51% of guests choose QSRs for convenience. The brands that come out ahead won't just be the ones with the cheapest menu items. They'll be the ones that get the fundamentals right: fast, accurate orders and great guest experiences, every time. Many thanks to The Food Institute and Kelly Beaton for including us in her research! Read the full article from The Food Institute: https://hubs.li/Q04d5qx_0

"According to HungerRush data, it's things like long wait times, inaccurate orders, or poor customer service. Fixing those issues can have just as much impact on how guests perceive value as a discount could." — Shannon Chirone, SVP of Marketing, HungerRush A new era of value wars in QSR is heating up, but slashing prices isn't the only answer. As The Food Institute reports, fast-food chains are navigating one of the most complex economic environments in recent memory, with lower-income consumers pulling back and even middle-class diners spending more intentionally. According to HungerRush data, 51% of guests choose QSRs for convenience. The brands that come out ahead won't just be the ones with the cheapest menu items. They'll be the ones that get the fundamentals right: fast, accurate orders and great guest experiences, every time. Many thanks to The Food Institute and Kelly Beaton for including us in her research! Read the full article from The Food Institute: https://hubs.li/Q04d5qx_0

updates.text: Is it time to renew your POS contract? Before you do, here are a few questions worth asking. Does your POS scale? Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? HungerRush is the POS partner behind every great guest experience. Get in touch.

Yet it remains cheese, milk's leap toward immortality." — Clifton Fadiman If you believe you are what you eat, then National Grilled Cheese Day is the perfect moment to shave off (...or unwrap...) a slice of immortality, melt it between two pieces of bread, and digest the divine. And tomato soup? Like Batman and Robin, Lucy and Ethel, Mario and Luigi, Frodo and Samwise, Han and Chewy, Michael and Dwight, Penny and Brain, Wayne and Garth, Rumi Mira Zoey and Bobby, The Dude and Walter, Pooh and Piglet, Jay and Silent Bob, Fry and Bender, or Wallace and Gromit ( — who were, yes, highly attuned to the lunar immortality of cheese)... While not officially "required" for a proper National Grilled Cheese Day celebration, that steady bowl of tomato soup is the classic lawful-good force multiplier. The OG 10xer. And is now a good time to talk about sourdough being bread's own leap toward immortality as well? Making a grilled cheese on sourdough and dipping it in tomato soup is basically like discovering Mario's infinite lives staircase. If you're reading this on April 12th, today is the day to make an Artemis-like leap toward your own immortality. Looking for other days to celebrate your favorite foods? updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

A leader in fully integrated restaurant management systems and small business technology, SpotOn offers end-to-end solutions which include marketing, website development, reservations, online ordering, appointments, eCommerce, digital loyalty, review management, as well as retail and restaurant point-of-sale (POS) solutions.

Doron Friedman, Matt Hyman, and Zach Hyman co-founded SpotOn in 2017 and its headquarters is located in San Francisco, California.

But it's our drivers who make the final connection, delivering for customers, building relationships and representing PFG in the communities we serve. Their commitment to safety, service and excellence helps keep our business moving every day and ensures our customers have what they need to serve theirs. To all of our drivers and transportation associates: thank you for the miles you drive, the early mornings, the long days and the dedication you bring to every route. We're proud to celebrate you this week and every week. #ProudToBePFG #NTDAW26 #ThankADriver #TruckDriverAppreciationWeek

linkedin_company.about: Considered the oldest family name in Chicago pizza, Lou Malnati's is as rich in history as its pizza is in flavor. Lou Malnati got his start in the 1940's working in Chicago's first deep dish pizzeria. He took his pizza expertise to Lincolnwood, a northern suburb of Chicago, where he and his wife Jean opened the first Lou Malnati's Pizzeria on March 17, 1971. Lou was known for his fun-loving character as well as making Chicago's best pizza. Loyal patrons lined the streets on opening day for a taste of his delicious deep dish creations. Lou always thought it was funny that an Italian should open a pizzeria in a Jewish neighborhood on an Irish holiday. But that was Lou's style; he loved all types of people and didn't care much about what people thought. Today, we have 70+ locations across Illinois, Arizona, Wisconsin, and Indiana. We also ship over a million pizzas a year through our e-commerce business, Tastes of Chicago. Malnati’s success comes from our commitment to quality. Every Lou Malnati’s pizza is handmade from scratch using the finest and freshest ingredients. Every year, the Malnati team hand selects California vine-ripened tomatoes for the perfect sweet and tangy taste. The exclusive sausage blend is seasoned to our exact specifications. The fresh mozzarella cheese comes from the same small dairy that has supplied Lou Malnati’s for over 45 years. And our family’s secret recipe for flaky, buttery crust has been passed down from generation to generation. You’ll know with every bite that each pizza was made with care and special attention. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Lou Malnati’s is proud to be ranked a top Chicago workplace 15 years in a row!

updates.text: Today, we would like to spotlight our very own Alex Weaver and her Lou’s journey. Alex, our newest District Manager in Training (DMIT), first started with Lou’s as a 16-year-old PHC team member at our Lincolnwood location. After graduating college, she decided to continue building her career with Lou’s and pursue a path in leadership. Over the past 13 years, Alex has served in management roles across six different Lou’s locations. She credits each location, team, and challenge for shaping her into the leader she is today. “Growth has always been one of my core values,” Alex said. "Whether I was stepping into a new restaurant, taking on additional responsibilities, or navigating significant change, I've always embraced opportunities that pushed me outside of my comfort zone. I’m excited to step into the DMIT role because it represents the next chapter in my growth journey. Lou Malnati's has invested so much in my growth over the years, and I'm excited for the opportunity to give back by positively impacting even more teams and people throughout the organization, including our next generation of leaders.” Congratulations on this exciting next step, Alex! We’re excited to see you continue your growth.

updates.text: We are excited to kick off fundraising efforts for our 54th Annual Lou Malnati's Cancer Research Benefit, which will take place on September 26. This incredible event brings our team members, guests, and communities together with one shared goal: making a meaningful difference in the fight against cancer. Last year, thanks in part to the generosity of our guests and dedication of our teams, we raised more than $470,000 to support cancer research and support programs. As we build toward this year's event, our stores will participate in a friendly competition to see who can sell the most Cancer Donation Circles. Guests can purchase these circles or donate through round-up opportunities in-store throughout August and September. Most importantly, 100% of funds raised support the Lou and Jean Malnati Brain Tumor Institute at Northwestern Memorial Hospital , Gilda's Club Chicago , and Pickles Group . Let's work together to make this our biggest year yet and help bring us one step closer to a cure.

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
Sysco is the global leader in selling, marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. This includes restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments, entertainment venues, and more. Sysco operates almost 340 distribution centers, in over 10 countries, with 76,000 colleagues serving approximately 730,000 customer locations. The company generated sales of more than $81 billion in fiscal year 2025 that ended June 28, 2025.

As the world’s largest food-away-from-home distributor, Sysco offers customized supply chain solutions, bespoke specialty product offerings, and culinary support to drive customers to innovate and optimize their operations. We act as a trusted business partner to our customers, helping them grow through our industry-leading portfolio that includes fresh produce, premium proteins, specialty products, sustainably focused items, equipment and supplies, and innovative culinary solutions. 

For more information, visit www.sysco.com. For important news and key information for Sysco investors, visit the Investor Relations section of the company’s website at investors.sysco.com.

updates.text: RUN. SLICE. REPEAT. 🍕🏃♀️ En agosto con Sbarro , realizamos una colaboración juanto a adidas en el marco de la Media Maratón de Buenos Aires, uno de los eventos deportivos más importantes del año, llevando The Original NY Pizza XXL a la comunidad de adidas Runners. Fui parte de la acción desde un lugar que disfruto mucho: la creación y cobertura de contenido en tiempo real, buscando capturar esos momentos que hacen a la experiencia: la alegría de cada runner al cruzar la meta y luego, por supuesto, disfrutar una slice de Sbarro. También trabajamos en el desarrollo de una cápsula especial de comunicación, junto a Lucia Cosimanoy Romina Ormazabal . Una colaboración que nos permitió descubrir un punto de conexión entre dos marcas con mundos diferentes y construir una experiencia relevante para sus comunidades. Mención especial al equipo de Cinco Yardas por acompañarnos en esta acción. 🤝

linkedin_company.about: There are some unique qualities of LEDO Pizza that come from its long history. People often ask why LEDO Pizza is rectangular. The round pizza pans commonly seen today were very new in the fifties. Rectangular baking pans were readily available, hence the square pizza. Since that time, round pans have become the rage as pizza operators are able to cut costs by giving the appearance of more, while actually offering less. Our thick pepperoni is also a LEDO trademark. Its unique size resulted from the cooks cutting the pepperoni by hand. The thicker the slice, the faster the work was finished. The customers loved it so much we kept doing it that way. While our entrees and subs have a somewhat shorter history, they have become famous as well. All of our subs are made with freshly baked bread and stuffed with our favorite items. Our Italian salad is large enough for a meal and comes with our famous LEDO salad dressing. Other delicious entrees include lasagna, spaghetti, soup, salad, and breadsticks.

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby
