updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

updates.text: As we continue to pursue our long-term ambition of engineering trailblazing cooking product, we are proud to announce a new chapter in our leadership. To steer our 10-year strategy and next phase of global growth, we are thrilled to welcome former Volvo Cars CEO and Dyson CEO Jim Rowan , as our new Chair of the Board, effective 1st August 2026. Jim brings decades of international leadership from some of the world’s most innovative, design-led businesses. Throughout his career, he has successfully scaled premium, engineering-led consumer brands across complex global markets. He joins the Board alongside formalised Non-Executive Directors, Ruth Chandler (Board Advisor at Skyscanner and executive coach) and Scott Maguire (President and Chief Operating Officer of On). Together, they bring extensive global experience across innovation, people and commercial success. Darina Garland , Co-Founder of Ooni, shared: “Since the early days of Ooni we made the strategic decision to have a board of advisors, to bring together world-class experience that would challenge, support and steer us into the next level. Today we are so excited to bring this group of global stars into Ooni. We leaned into our value of ambition and had a rigorous process to find these board advisors and our new Chair. Jim is an exceptional leader, and we’re delighted to have him as Chair.” Jim succeeds Paul Ross who is stepping down after eight years in the position. During his tenure, Paul has played an important role in guiding growth and development, leaving a strong foundation for the future. We are immensely grateful for everything he has done for the business. #Ooni #Leadership #ExecutiveLeadership #BoardOfDirectors

updates.text: We’re rewriting how home kitchens mix dough. Introducing Ooni Halo Core - a compact spiral mixer engineered to outperform the stand mixers that have dominated home kitchens for decades. Following the sell-out success of our first spiral mixer, Halo Pro, we are taking the next significant step in our category expansion, adding another fantastic product to our indoor kitchen line-up. We are proud to introduce Ooni Halo Core Spiral Mixer which brings professional-grade, dual-kneading spiral engineering into a compact, countertop-friendly design that handles over 6 lbs of high-hydration dough with ease. Our Founder Kristian Tapaninaho notes: “Traditional stand mixers aren’t designed for kneading dough; they stall, overheat, and fail to develop gluten properly. With Halo Core, we’ve engineered a solution that fits on your counter but refuses to compromise on performance. We are making professional-grade spiral mixing technology the new domestic standard, giving home bakers the exact mechanical advantage used by the world’s best commercial bakeries.” Halo Core goes well beyond dough. With advanced, patent-pending removable breaker bar plus attachments for whipping and beating, this powerhouse transitions seamlessly from a heavy-duty kneader to a delicate kitchen powerhouse. Halo Core officially launches on August 4th at Ooni.com , and will be available with select retail partners globally. updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. updates.text: So excited to share that Owner.com has closed a $240M Series D led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a $2.3B valuation. Everyone is debating how many jobs AI can cut. That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? I eat at Ashley’s Cafe (pictured) multiple times a week, and seeing the impact of our technology on Ashley’s business has been pure joy. It’s a front-row-seat to a movement that Owner is building - over 100 million guests that we’ve been able to bring to small businesses across the country. I really believe local business owners are the most inspiring people on earth, and it’s a privilege to build for them. Today we celebrate a fun milestone, and then we get right back to building for these amazing entrepreneurs. If you want to come build AI for (not against) people - we’re hiring. updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby

updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

Ventless commercial cooking equipment that enables cooking without traditional exhaust infrastructure, including rapid-cook ovens, combi ovens, fryers, griddles, and conveyor ovens.

Beverage equipment for coffee, espresso, frozen drinks, ice, water, dispensing, beverage control, and related commercial beverage programs.
Equipment for commercial pizza preparation and baking, including deck, conveyor, wood-fired, stone-hearth, and ventless pizza ovens plus mixers, sheeters, proofers, slicers, and holding systems.

updates.text: Hungry Howie's has landed on QSR Magazine's list of the 20 Best Franchise Deals for 2026! 🍕 Every decision we make at Hungry Howie's comes back to one core question...does this set our franchisees up to win? Flavored Crust has been ours for more than 40 years, and it's still driving results for our operators today. Rotating limited-time offers, Secret Menu selections, products like Howie Bread, and the introduction of our new Flavor Experience platform give franchisees new ways to engage guests, all without losing our core identity. updates.text: As back-to-school, Labor Day and football season all converge, pizza chains are balancing menu innovation with value and familiar favorites. Hungry Howie's is leading the charge, because for us, value isn't something we manufacture during a select moment - it's ingrained in the brand. Our VP of Public Relations Jennifer Jackson spoke with Pizza Marketplace about how we're approaching this stretch. Instead of chasing pricier limited-time offers, we're leaning into our Flavored Crust roots (40+ years and counting), our new Tajín partnership, and our Flavor Experience platform, which brought back the Coney Pizza after more than 20 years off the menu. From how we're staying ahead in an increasingly competitive pizza category to what's next for Hungry Howie's, it's a great look at why value has always been part of who we are. Read the full story: https://lnkd.in/g9ixWKCV #PizzaIndustry #QSR #Franchising

updates.text: At just 24 years old, Kylee Bird is proving that leadership has no age limit. After starting at Hungry Howie’s as a high school employee in 2017, Kylee chose a career in franchising over a traditional college path. Today, she serves as the operating partner for three Northern Michigan locations, including the newly opened Traverse City restaurant at Chums Corner. From training team members and preparing fresh dough to supporting community events and school fundraisers, Kylee leads by example while developing the next generation of restaurant professionals. Kylee’s commitment extends beyond great pizza. Her stores have been recognized as a Recovery-Friendly Workplace by 217 Recovery in Traverse City, MI, reflecting her passion for creating opportunities and providing supportive employment for individuals rebuilding their lives. With another Northern Michigan location already planned, Kylee continues to demonstrate that hard work, compassion, and community involvement are the foundation of lasting success at Hungry Howie’s. According to Bill Bee of Traverse City’s The Daily Bee, “she isn’t just managing spreadsheets from a distant office, she is on the floor, in the flour, teaching high schoolers how to look a customer in the eye, and quietly building a business model rooted in radical empathy.” #HungryHowies #Franchising #FranchiseLeadership #NextGenLeadership #FranchiseSuccess #WomenInBusiness #CareerGrowth #CommunityImpact #WorkplaceCulture

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

Months of preparation come down to what reaches the judges. That is the environment our partners help make possible. As we prepare for Indianapolis, I want to recognize Sysco, alongside Buckhead, FreshPoint and European Imports, for their involvement in this year’s World Food Championships and the Taste of Indiana stage. linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
Sysco is the global leader in selling, marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. This includes restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments, entertainment venues, and more. Sysco operates almost 340 distribution centers, in over 10 countries, with 76,000 colleagues serving approximately 730,000 customer locations. The company generated sales of more than $81 billion in fiscal year 2025 that ended June 28, 2025.

As the world’s largest food-away-from-home distributor, Sysco offers customized supply chain solutions, bespoke specialty product offerings, and culinary support to drive customers to innovate and optimize their operations. We act as a trusted business partner to our customers, helping them grow through our industry-leading portfolio that includes fresh produce, premium proteins, specialty products, sustainably focused items, equipment and supplies, and innovative culinary solutions. 

For more information, visit www.sysco.com. For important news and key information for Sysco investors, visit the Investor Relations section of the company’s website at investors.sysco.com.

updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. Authors Haochen W. , Yi H. , and Ryan Xie share the engineering behind this deployment. The work was also presented at the ICML 2026 RLxF workshop. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

updates.text: DoorDash 🤝 Dispatch Goods 🤝 The Story of Stuff Project We ran a really special pilot in City of Half Moon Bay this year: a dozen restaurants swapped single-use containers for ones that get washed, sanitized, returned, and reused. Thousands fewer containers ended up in the trash. The program’s still running, and we’re still tuning it. But reusable packaging is new enough that half the work is just explaining what it is! Thanks Story of Stuff for helping with that. I hope it gets other cities and restaurants excited to try it too.

- Nearly 30 million pizza orders were placed on DoorDash in 2025

From neighborhood institutions to local favorites putting their own spin on a classic, meet the pizza spots customers are loving across America. Full list in the comments.

updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. Authors Haochen W. , Yi H. , and Ryan Xie share the engineering behind this deployment. The work was also presented at the ICML 2026 RLxF workshop. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

updates.text: DoorDash 🤝 Dispatch Goods 🤝 The Story of Stuff Project We ran a really special pilot in City of Half Moon Bay this year: a dozen restaurants swapped single-use containers for ones that get washed, sanitized, returned, and reused. updates.text: We were proud to join Northside Economic Opportunity Network (NEON) for its 20th Anniversary Celebration and be among the inaugural recipients of its Angel Awards, recognizing the companies and civic leaders whose partnership and investment have helped advance NEON’s mission to build wealth for low- to moderate-income entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis. Since 2016, General Mills has supported NEON through philanthropy, food-industry expertise and GoodWorks pro-bono projects, where our employees lend their skills and knowledge to help local business owners grow their operations. This support contributes to NEON’s work through programs like its Food Business Incubator and Collective Kitchens, which help food entrepreneurs access the resources they need to grow. We’re grateful to celebrate this milestone alongside NEON’s entrepreneurs, team, community partners and fellow supporters — and a special thank you to our General Mills Community Impact team for the leadership and dedication they bring to this work and to the North Minneapolis community. #GStandsForGood #CommunityImpact #Philanthropy

updates.text: We’re shaking up the soup aisle, and Progresso Pitmaster is leading the way. Since its debut last summer, Progresso Pitmaster, the BBQ-inspired soup line, has become the brand’s most successful product launch in four years.* Now, we're building on that momentum with two new fan-favorite flavors, available at retailers nationwide. Made with juicy meats, roasted vegetables and 14-20g of protein per can, Progresso Pitmaster soups brings the bold, smoky flavors of a backyard cookout to the table in just five minutes. No grill required. It’s an example of how we’re reimagining familiar flavors and making them easy to enjoy in one convenient bowl. #Progresso #Innovation #Soup *According to Nielsen Retail Measurement Database, as of August 26, 2026

updates.text: This morning, General Mills’ board of directors announced that Dana McNabb, current chief operating officer, will become our next CEO, succeeding Jeff Harmening, who will become executive chair of the board of directors, effective January 1, 2027. Dana has made significant contributions across her 27 years at General Mills, having led in senior positions across the company and around the world. As current COO, she leads all four operating segments and key functions, with a focus on our consumers and delivering growth. She is a proven, results-driven leader with a deep understanding of our business, our brands and our industry. We’re incredibly grateful to Jeff for his 32 years of impact at General Mills and the strong foundation he laid for our next chapter. Learn more here: https://lnkd.in/e7uW3tyu

updates.text: September was full of moments that brought our people and communities together. 💙 As part of Familia Heritage Month, employees volunteered with CLUES (Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio), to put together school-supply kits for local students. We also celebrated 20 years of the Mill City Farmers Market, where General Mills has been a founding funder and longtime supporter. At our World Headquarters, employees, families and friends laced up for our annual Run of the Mills, while current and former Pillsbury colleagues came together for the Funster event to share stories and celebrate the brand’s legacy. Meanwhile, the Edgard & Cooper team brought sustainability and a shared love of pets to life at Upcycled & Unleashed, where adoptable pups took the runway in upcycled designs. We also connected with fellow Minnesota leaders at the Minnesota Business Partnership event to talk about the future of our state. From giving back to celebrating the connections that bring us together, these are a few of the moments that made September special. #MillsMonthlyMoments #GeneralMillsLife

updates.text: Did you know that only 2% of people aged 2+ in the U.S. get enough whole grains daily?* That means most Americans are missing out on the benefits whole grains provide. For nearly 20 years, General Mills has made whole grain the first ingredient in our Big G cereals. Today, our Big G cereals deliver 39 million whole-grain servings each day – making a nutrient-dense breakfast more accessible to families. This #NationalWholeGrainMonth , we’re sharing simple ways to get more whole grains into your day. View our whole grains guide here: https://lnkd.in/eFy6rmWX #WholeGrains #Nutrition * Source: NHANES 2017-18

linkedin_company.about: We’ve grown to become the largest family-operated broadline food service distributor in North America by upholding the same business approach since 1897—being passionately committed to the people we serve. We believe in the power of good food—to bring people together and make moments special. Every product, every order, and every decision we make is inspired by the people on the other side of the plate. We distribute to foodservice operators throughout the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast and Southwest regions of the U.S. and coast to coast in Canada. Our company also operates more than 170 Gordon Food Service Stores, which are open to the public and provide the benefits of restaurant-quality products and friendly, knowledgeable service. Gordon Food Service Stores do not charge a membership fee. Gordon Food Service Stores are the primary supplier for many small foodservice operators, including: restaurants, churches, daycare providers, caterers, event planners, and other small businesses. We offer a broad range of employment opportunities throughout our corporate offices, distribution centers, and retail stores. We have a strong commitment to our employees and foster an environment that promotes internal growth, training, and career development opportunities. Gordon Food Service is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any person on the basis of age, sex, race, religion, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

By integrating high-quality, pre-seasoned ingredients from our exclusive Gran Sazón® product line, these three operators deliver unforgettable Latin flavor profiles while keeping back-of-house prep lean and consistent: 🥩 Papa Julio’s Bar and Grill (Seneca, SC) anchors their signature Bistec a la Tampiqueña with tender Gran Sazón Arrachera Steak, saving valuable prep labor on trimming and marinating. 🥘 Puerto Nuevo Mexican and Seafood brings families together with their Authentic Parrillada, featuring sizzling Gran Sazón Chorizo to drive shareable check sizes. 🌯 Taco Riendo maximizes drive-thru throughput with speed-scratch assembly, utilizing uniform Gran Sazón Chorizo for fast, consistent morning service. We’ve grown to become the largest family-operated broadline food service distributor in North America by upholding the same business approach since 1897—being passionately committed to the people we serve. We believe in the power of good food—to bring people together and make moments special. Every product, every order, and every decision we make is inspired by the people on the other side of the plate.

We distribute to foodservice operators throughout the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast  and Southwest regions of the U.S. and coast to coast in Canada. 

Our company also operates more than 170 Gordon Food Service Stores, which are open to the public and provide the benefits of restaurant-quality products and friendly, knowledgeable service. Gordon Food Service Stores do not charge a membership fee. 

Gordon Food Service Stores are the primary supplier for many small foodservice operators, including: restaurants, churches, daycare providers, caterers, event planners, and other small businesses. 

We offer a broad range of employment opportunities throughout our corporate offices, distribution centers, and retail stores. We have a strong commitment to our employees and foster an environment that promotes internal growth, training, and career development opportunities. 

Gordon Food Service is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any person on the basis of age, sex, race, religion, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

updates.text: As more brands seek out strategies for benefit stacking their products, they are turning to the power of whole grains. Whole grains can help you formulate products that get you closer to the claims consumers are prioritizing today so that you can win on shelf and consumers can get more of what they want from their favorite foods, like protein and fiber that come from trusted, whole ingredients. In this issue of The Stack™ we’re talking about whole grains and how they can help you optimize your portfolios with protein, fiber and other benefits. In this issue, we’re breaking down: · What consumers think of whole grains and how they turn to these familiar favorites to help them reach their wellness goals · The role whole grains can play in your efforts to reduce ultra-processed foods in your offerings · Key whole grain ingredients that deliver on multiple benefits · Strategies for integrating whole grains into your products without sacrificing taste or product consistency Be sure to follow The Stack™ to connect with what’s driving today’s consumers and shaping the products and trends of tomorrow. #TheStack #ArdentMills #FoodTrends #ConsumerInsights #FoodInnovation #BenefitStacking

updates.text: Foodservice organizations are starting to benefit stack their menus to include options full of the nutritional benefits consumers are seeking. From protein-powered coffees to gluten-free buns, high-protein pizza crust and more, now is the time to seek out the benefit-stacked foods you want from the fast food and quick-serve restaurants you love. If you’re a foodservice organization ready to get started, Ardent Mills is here to help. In the August edition of The Stack™, we’re breaking down what we’re seeing in foodservice and sharing the insights that are driving real change across menus. We’re also offering strategies to help you take that first step toward benefit stacking. Whether it’s more protein, whole grains or gluten-free choices, there are solutions available today that can help you stand out and gain consumer loyalty. In this issue you can: • Learn more about the data driving consumer choices • Connect with strategies for integrating more of the benefits consumers want into your menus • Take a look at brands who are leading the way in foodservice benefit stacking Be sure to subscribe to The Stack™ to connect with what’s driving today’s consumers and shaping the products and trends of tomorrow. #TheStack #ArdentMills #FoodTrends #ConsumerInsights #FoodserviceInnovation #FoodserviceIngredients

updates.text: Our team came away from IFT First full of ideas and inspiration for brands who want to benefit stack their portfolios to deliver more of what consumers want from their favorite foods. From added protein and fiber to whole grain nutrition and trusted ingredients, in this issue of The Stack, we’re breaking down the opportunities, watch-outs and key questions to consider when you develop strategies for innovating the products today’s consumers are seeking. We’ve delving into: • What benefit stacking means for customers that want to deliver what consumers demand while staying true to their brand • How to capitalize on the benefit stacking mindset by focusing on what matters today and will continue to matter tomorrow • The key questions to ask your organization as you begin to formulate your innovation strategies • The three most important considerations when benefit stacking It’s about giving consumers more of what they expect, from each and every bite.

updates.text: Are whole grains and pulses factoring into your brand’s innovation strategy? If not, you may be missing a key opportunity to outpace the competition. As more consumers continue to benefit stack – prioritizing foods that deliver multiple nutritional benefits at once – whole grains and pulses are showing up as foundational ingredients for delivering protein, fiber, cleaner labels and affordability. This month in The Stack™, we’re talking with two industry leaders—Ardent Mills Chief Growth Officer Angie Goldberg and Grain Foods Foundation Executive Director Erin E. Ball. They’re breaking down: • The rising momentum of the benefit-stacking trend • The key benefits consumers continue to prioritize • How whole grains and pulses can help connect your portfolio to consumer expectations • What’s next for brands who want to lead in today’s dynamic landscape Be sure to follow The Stack™ to connect with what’s driving today’s consumers and shaping the products of tomorrow. #TheStack #ArdentMills #FoodTrends #ConsumerInsights #CPGInnovation #CPGIngredients

updates.text: Introducing The Stack™— your new LinkedIn newsletter from Ardent Mills, sharing insights and information on benefit stacking. Today’s consumers aren’t choosing a single benefit anymore. They’re stacking them. High protein. High fiber. Whole grains. Transparent ingredient lists. Consider: • 43% of US adults now follow a high protein diet (+6 pts YoY), with another 29% growth expected through mid-2026 • 37% of US adults are focused on high fiber (+4 pts YoY), with 30% growth expected through mid-2026 • 41% of US adults now prioritize whole grain foods (+10 pts YoY), with 17% growth expected through mid-2026 This is more than a trend. It’s a mindset shift. In Issue One, we break down the who, what and why of benefit stacking — and how it’s reshaping decisions at the shelf. If you’re creating new products, reformulating classics or extending your lines, this is for you. updates.text: Is it time to renew your POS contract? Before you do, here are a few questions worth asking. Does your POS scale? Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? HungerRush is the POS partner behind every great guest experience. Get in touch.

updates.text: "A cheese may disappoint. It may be dull, it may be naive, it may be oversophisticated. Yet it remains cheese, milk's leap toward immortality." — Clifton Fadiman If you believe you are what you eat, then National Grilled Cheese Day is the perfect moment to shave off (...or unwrap...) a slice of immortality, melt it between two pieces of bread, and digest the divine. And tomato soup? Like Batman and Robin, Lucy and Ethel, Mario and Luigi, Frodo and Samwise, Han and Chewy, Michael and Dwight, Penny and Brain, Wayne and Garth, Rumi Mira Zoey and Bobby, The Dude and Walter, Pooh and Piglet, Jay and Silent Bob, Fry and Bender, or Wallace and Gromit ( — who were, yes, highly attuned to the lunar immortality of cheese)... While not officially "required" for a proper National Grilled Cheese Day celebration, that steady bowl of tomato soup is the classic lawful-good force multiplier. The OG 10xer. updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

The fresh mozzarella cheese comes from the same small dairy that has supplied Lou Malnati’s for over 45 years. And our family’s secret recipe for flaky, buttery crust has been passed down from generation to generation. updates.text: Today, we would like to spotlight our very own Alex Weaver and her Lou’s journey. Alex, our newest District Manager in Training (DMIT), first started with Lou’s as a 16-year-old PHC team member at our Lincolnwood location. After graduating college, she decided to continue building her career with Lou’s and pursue a path in leadership. Over the past 13 years, Alex has served in management roles across six different Lou’s locations. She credits each location, team, and challenge for shaping her into the leader she is today. “Growth has always been one of my core values,” Alex said. "Whether I was stepping into a new restaurant, taking on additional responsibilities, or navigating significant change, I've always embraced opportunities that pushed me outside of my comfort zone. I’m excited to step into the DMIT role because it represents the next chapter in my growth journey. Lou Malnati's has invested so much in my growth over the years, and I'm excited for the opportunity to give back by positively impacting even more teams and people throughout the organization, including our next generation of leaders.” Congratulations on this exciting next step, Alex! We’re excited to see you continue your growth.

updates.text: The best way to start a new semester? Ice-cold Coke®, great food, and even better company. 🥤📚 Last night, we brought students from across Hong Kong's universities together for a Joint-U "Semester Kick-Off Feast (開Sem飯)” — a local tradition of universities in Hong Kong — because the start of term isn't just about lectures and deadlines. It's about the moments of connection that make university life unforgettable. From a joint-university rhythmic group chants (Dem Beat) to sharing a meal with friends old and new, the night was all about togetherness. And no gathering is complete without that signature Coca-Cola® fizz to make every toast just a little more special. Thanks to sica Ho and Freeeboyzzzz for bringing the energy, and to our partner restaurant Ladies' Street Sik Faan Co. for proving that the best meals are the ones shared. Because when Coca-Cola® meets local flavours and student spirit, that's an experience only we can bring. ✨ Here's to new friends, good times, and a semester to remember. #TheCocaColaCompany #CocaColaHK #RefreshTheWorld #MakeADifference #UniversityLife #Togetherness

updates.text: Today in Atlanta, our CEO Henrique Braun joined LA28 and the City of Atlanta to announce that our hometown will serve as the first stop on the LA28 Olympic Torch Relay. The Coca-Cola Company was also named a Presenting Partner of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Torch Relays, helping bring one of the Movement’s most enduring traditions to communities across the country. The Relay is planning to travel through all 50 states — the longest Olympic Torch Relay ever — bringing the spirit of the Olympic Games closer to more people on the road to Los Angeles. In 2028, Coca-Cola will mark 100 years as a partner of the Olympic Movement, making us the longest continuous partner of the Olympic Games. As the journey to the LA28 Games begins, we’re proud to help carry the spirit of the Olympic Games forward.

products_and_services.product_description: A carbonated soft drink sold globally in regular and reduced- or no-sugar variants. It is distributed in bottles, cans and fountain formats for retail, foodservice and hospitality consumption.

A portfolio of carbonated beverages including Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, Fanta, Sprite, Fresca, Schweppes and Thums Up. Products are offered in regular, diet and zero-sugar formulations across retail and foodservice channels.
A portfolio of bottled water, enhanced water, sports drinks and functional hydration beverages, including Dasani, smartwater, Powerade, BODYARMOR, Topo Chico, vitaminwater and Aquarius.

A portfolio of packaged and served coffee and tea beverages, including Costa Coffee, Gold Peak, Fuze Tea, Peace Tea and Georgia. Offerings cover hot and cold consumption occasions across retail and foodservice channels.
A portfolio of fruit juices, juice drinks, dairy beverages and plant-based drinks, including Minute Maid, Simply, fairlife, innocent, Del Valle and Maaza.
A portfolio of pre-mixed alcoholic beverages, including Simply Spiked, Topo Chico Hard, Fresca Mixed and Jack Daniel's & Coca-Cola. Availability and alcohol regulations vary by market.

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

linkedin_company.about: For over 100 years, Shamrock Foods Company has worked to ensure people come first – our 5,000+ associates, our customers, and the families we serve across the nation. A privately held, family-owned and -operated Forbes 500 company, Shamrock is an innovator in the food industry and has been since its founding in Arizona in 1922. Shamrock specializes in the manufacturing and distribution of quality food and food-related products through a family of companies, including Shamrock Foods foodservice distribution and Shamrock Farms dairy manufacturing, among others. Now led by the third generation of McClelland family leadership, Shamrock’s success is built upon three unwavering principles set forth by our founder, W.T. McClelland: An unwavering commitment to quality people, products, and service; innovation in everything we do; and commitment to the communities we are privileged to serve. Our unique company culture is guided by the motto to “treat associates as family, and customers and suppliers as friends.” Learn more about our products, philosophy, and current job openings at https://jobs.shamrockfoods.com.

updates.text: Arizona’s Hometown Dairy We're excited to kick off another season of the Shamrock Farms Farm Tour! As a family-owned company with more than 100 years rooted in dairy farming, we're proud to welcome thousands of students, families and community members each year to experience agriculture firsthand. Since opening our farm to the public in 2005, we've welcomed more than 150,000 visitors to learn how we care for our cows and where the pure, fresh milk in Shamrock Farms' delicious dairy products comes from. Located in Stanfield, Arizona, our milk travels less than an hour to our Phoenix production facility. It's a local farm-to-table story we're proud to share. Ready to see it for yourself? crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

Its menu includes a variety of pizza options with different crust styles and toppings, along with baked pasta, chicken wings, fried chicken, and snack items. The company also offers meal bundles and group-sharing combinations designed for individual, family, and larger dining occasions. Customers can place orders through its website, mobile platforms, and restaurant locations, with options for pickup or delivery. In addition to its core pizza offerings, Pizza Hut provides complementary menu categories such as appetizers, desserts, and drinks, allowing customers to order complete meals from a single restaurant brand. Based on its Philippine operations, the company serves a broad selection of food products that cater to everyday meals, gatherings, and special occasions.

updates.text: As back-to-school, Labor Day and football season all converge, pizza chains are balancing menu innovation with value and familiar favorites. Hungry Howie's is leading the charge, because for us, value isn't something we manufacture during a select moment - it's ingrained in the brand. Our VP of Public Relations Jennifer Jackson spoke with Pizza Marketplace about how we're approaching this stretch. Instead of chasing pricier limited-time offers, we're leaning into our Flavored Crust roots (40+ years and counting), our new Tajín partnership, and our Flavor Experience platform, which brought back the Coney Pizza after more than 20 years off the menu. From how we're staying ahead in an increasingly competitive pizza category to what's next for Hungry Howie's, it's a great look at why value has always been part of who we are. Read the full story: https://lnkd.in/g9ixWKCV #PizzaIndustry #QSR #Franchising

updates.text: At just 24 years old, Kylee Bird is proving that leadership has no age limit. After starting at Hungry Howie’s as a high school employee in 2017, Kylee chose a career in franchising over a traditional college path. Today, she serves as the operating partner for three Northern Michigan locations, including the newly opened Traverse City restaurant at Chums Corner. From training team members and preparing fresh dough to supporting community events and school fundraisers, Kylee leads by example while developing the next generation of restaurant professionals. Kylee’s commitment extends beyond great pizza. Her stores have been recognized as a Recovery-Friendly Workplace by 217 Recovery in Traverse City, MI, reflecting her passion for creating opportunities and providing supportive employment for individuals rebuilding their lives. With another Northern Michigan location already planned, Kylee continues to demonstrate that hard work, compassion, and community involvement are the foundation of lasting success at Hungry Howie’s. According to Bill Bee of Traverse City’s The Daily Bee, “she isn’t just managing spreadsheets from a distant office, she is on the floor, in the flour, teaching high schoolers how to look a customer in the eye, and quietly building a business model rooted in radical empathy.” #HungryHowies #Franchising #FranchiseLeadership #NextGenLeadership #FranchiseSuccess #WomenInBusiness #CareerGrowth #CommunityImpact #WorkplaceCulture

linkedin_company.about: Headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Marco’s Pizza is one of the fastest-growing pizza brands in the United States. Marco’s was founded in 1978 by Italian-born Pasquale (“Pat”) Giammarco and thrives to deliver a high-quality pizza experience, known for its dough made from scratch and its three fresh signature cheeses. The company has grown from its roots as a beloved Ohio brand to operate and franchise over 1,200 stores in 35 states with locations in Puerto Rico, the Bahamas, and Mexico. Most recently, Marco’s was recognized as America’s Favorite Restaurant in the Limited-Service Pizza category by Nation’s Restaurant News using Technomic Ignite Consumer 2024 dataꝉꝉ. Other recent accolades include ranking No. 48 on Entrepreneur Magazine’s 2024 “Franchise 500” ranking, earning a coveted spot as the only top 5 pizza chain to rank on Newsweek’s 2025 “America’s Best Customer Service” in pizza chains list, earning a spot on QSR’s Top 50, and being featured on Nation’s Restaurant News’ prestigious “Top 500” ranking. ꝉꝉAccording to Technomic’s 2024 America’s Favorite Restaurants data, Marco’s Pizza secured the top spot in the Limited-Service Pizza category with a 53.4% composite top-box rating, indicating the share of recent guests who gave the brand the highest possible rating for each of the guest experience attributes. Data for America’s Favorite Chains comes from Technomic Ignite Consumer, which collects information about how brands impact consumers and how consumers interact with those brands via online surveys. For more information: www.technomic.com/ignite-consumer.

updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Margherita Magnifico is BACK for a limited time only! When we introduce new pizzas, we hold ourselves to high standards for quality AND convenience. This Margherita Magnifico is no exception. Our Director of Culinary Innovation Kathleen Kennedy tried 20 different recipes before landing the perfect bite. When crafting this simple yet delicious pizza, she had three principles: 🍕Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor 🍕Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications 🍕Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s She wanted to make sure she would be proud to serve this to her friends and family. We’re proud to have her on our team, adding another layer to our franchisees' key differentiators! The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. Our Chief Marketing Officer Steve Kennedy said it best: “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach.” Check out the hand-stretched crust, thick slices of mozzarella, and a shredded three-cheese blend topped with our signature basil drizzle…while supplies last! 😉

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. updates.text: A common assumption in the restaurant industry is that success starts with what's on the menu. But consumers don't come back because a product was great once. They come back because they know exactly what to expect. The order will be accurate. The wait won't be excessive. The experience will be familiar. The food will taste the same regardless of which location they visit or who's working that day. That's not just great operations. That's a system. The brands that scale aren't always the ones with the most innovative menu items. They're the ones that consistently deliver convenience and consistency at every touchpoint. Technology doesn't create great restaurants. It creates the operational foundation that makes great experiences repeatable. What do you think drives long-term restaurant loyalty more: product quality or operational consistency? Unsure? Learn more: https://lnkd.in/ekbx_KgU

updates.text: So we're back from NACS 2026, and honestly, we were surprised by what we heard on the show floor. It wasn't the sound of pitching, buzzwords, or typical conference chatter. It was the hum of skepticism. Customers had more questions this year than we've ever experienced before. Not because innovation has stalled, but because the stakes feel higher. AI was at the center of many of those conversations. Retailers recognize the opportunity, just as they once recognized the value of SEO. They know it has the potential to drive discovery, efficiency, and growth. What they're still trying to understand is how to capture that value without introducing unnecessary risk. One concern came up repeatedly: Will adding new value cost us the value we've already built? It's a challenge we understand because it's one we face ourselves. Large organizations can't afford to disrupt operations, customer experiences, or business continuity in pursuit of the next trend. That's why we've designed our solutions around a simple belief: innovation shouldn't require a tradeoff. Retailers shouldn't have to choose between what's working today and what will help them compete tomorrow. If you're asking the same questions, let's talk. updates.text: We love the message from this FSR Magazine piece on Postino and Upward Projects | Postino • Federal Pizza • Lado A Lado • Windsor • Churn • Joyride . Hospitality tech only works if the people delivering the hospitality want to use it. Instead of managing guests through a handful of disconnected systems, they built an integrated tech stack with one central view of the guest. Then they launched the Postino Pass with their own teams first. Employees got training and time to try it, and they didn't launch until servers felt ready. Brittany Baldwin , CMO of Upward Projects, put it simply: “The data isn’t the goal. Better hospitality is the goal.” It reminds us of something Joshua Sharkey of meez said on our podcast: "The question you always have to ask is... will this be a tool that will require my team in order to be successful, or will this be something that my team will require to be successful? Does the tool rely on the team, or does the team rely on the tool?" The takeaway? Restaurant teams succeed when their tools are simple to access and easy to use. Read the full story: https://lnkd.in/gA2AXecy

updates.text: Yesterday, we hosted Women in Tech Sales (WITS) in our Toronto office for an honest conversation about what separates top sellers from everyone else. 40 women showed up to hear from Katarina R. , Kathrine Orlowski , and Shikha Bindra. A few things that stood out: → Politeness isn't pipeline. A prospect who loved the demo isn't necessarily a qualified deal. Did the conversation create enough value for them to actually act? → Top sellers aren't necessarily working the hardest. They're intentional about where they spend their time and which accounts deserve their attention. → AI is becoming a seller's job, too. The question isn't whether your company is building workflows for you. The sellers getting ahead are figuring out how to build and use them themselves. 🤖 From there, we broke into mentoring circles - smaller groups, experienced mentors, and candid conversations about what's actually hard right now. 💬 The event sold out weeks in advance, with the waitlist moving right up until the event. A pretty great reminder of what happens when women create space to learn from and support each other. We're proud to continue our partnership with WITS as a Silver Hiring Partner and connect with the next cohort of women building careers in tech sales. 🤝 🚀 What's next? The WITS Bootcamp is coming up next week, bringing together women looking to break into B2B SaaS sales, build their networks, and connect with tech employers. Applications are open now! 🔗 Apply here: bit.ly/3OTOicI

For others, an opportunity to prove they had been hiding a secret talent. 🏐 SickKids Volleyball Tournament: From battling it out on the court to battling wasps, the Toronto team hit the beach for the annual SickKids fundraiser. What we loved most was seeing people get out of their usual routines, try something new, and spend time together outside of the usual workday. And along the way, a few hidden talents made an appearance. We’ll take that as a pretty successful summer ☀️

updates.text: You're driving across the city for the third time today because someone forgot to order lettuce. Your phone buzzes at 6 a.m. with a text that an employee didn't show up, so you don't even make it out of the city limits before you're called back. This was Andrew R. Scott 's life for years. 100-hour weeks, running between multiple locations, making solid money on the P&L while his life disappeared. The turning point came after a near-disastrous expansion. He opened a fifth location next to his best-performing store, assuming it would perform the same way. Instead, it cannibalized 30% of his top store's customers and left him with heavy debt on short-term financing. That's when Andrew started rebuilding. He went from restaurant owner to founder of Ownershift - Restaurant Training, Coaching and Consulting , where he's now helped over 1,000 operators add an average of $100,000 back to their bottom line. Here's what he learned: 📊 Most people problems are actually system problems. If multiple staff don't know how to do something, the procedure isn't documented, trained, or clear enough. 📈 Track your food cost and labor weekly, not monthly. Andrew missed a 47% food-cost spike because his P&L was three weeks late. Weekly spot-checks can catch problems early. 🔗 You're the bottleneck when only you can do something. Write it down, train it, delegate to someone who can do it 80% as well as you. 💰 Higher wages can actually lower your labor percentage. Better pay reduces turnover. Higher productivity per person improves the wage-to-productivity ratio. Hear the full story on The Pre-Shift Podcast 🎙️ Spotify https://lnkd.in/g2GUvf2T Apple podcasts https://lnkd.in/gT97zVw8

updates.text: For more than two decades, Domino’s® and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital - ALSAC ® have shared a belief in the power of hope. St. Jude has been Domino’s national charity partner since our first Thanks & Giving® campaign in 2004, and we are continually inspired by the generosity of our customers, franchisees and team members who help bring its lifesaving mission to life. Through this year’s campaign, customers can support children and families facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases by choosing the St. Jude Giving Combo, with $1 from each combo going to St. Jude, or by rounding up their order. Because of generous donors, families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing or food, so they can focus on what matters most: helping their child live, celebrate milestones and make memories together. Together, we can help St. Jude continue its mission: Finding cures. Saving children. ® Since the beginning of our partnership, Domino’s has raised more than $165 million for the kids of St. Jude, with a commitment to raise a total of $300 million by 2034. Join us in helping St. Jude give more children the greatest gift of all...time.

updates.text: Fire Prevention Month is here, and some Domino’s customers may get more than pizza at their door. 🚒👀 Throughout this month, participating franchise-owned stores across the U.S. are teaming up with local fire departments for surprise pizza deliveries via fire engine and free smoke alarm checks. If the customer’s smoke alarms work, the order is free. If not, firefighters will replace the batteries or install working alarms at no cost. Either way, it’s a win! For 19 years, we’ve proudly partnered with the National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ) and local fire departments to promote fire safety. Thank you to the NFPA and firefighters nationwide for helping keep our customers and communities safe.

updates.text: For almost a decade, Darin Thacker spent his free time as a Yelp Elite — discovering and championing small businesses. So when he found a company built around helping those same businesses thrive, it felt less like a job opportunity and more like a full-circle moment. Meet Darin, our Senior Manager of Lifecycle Marketing — and a marketer who spent 15 years waiting for a company that truly meant it when they said AI-first. Before joining, he was already experimenting with AI on his own time — coding, home automation, and figuring out what was possible. But professionally, that curiosity had nowhere to go. “𝘈𝘵 𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘰𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘱𝘢𝘯𝘪𝘦𝘴, 𝘈𝘐 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘢𝘷𝘢𝘪𝘭𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦, 𝘣𝘶𝘵 𝘪𝘵 𝘧𝘦𝘭𝘵 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘢 𝘥𝘪𝘳𝘵𝘺 𝘴𝘦𝘤𝘳𝘦𝘵.” Then MCPs changed what was possible. Suddenly, he could connect an LLM to the tools he already used and bring context, recommendations, and next steps into one conversation. 𝗧𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗰𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱. Darin’s lean Lifecycle team launches nearly a campaign every day. But understanding historical performance meant reconstructing the story each time — briefs in Google Drive, creative in the campaign platform, and benchmarks dependent on tribal knowledge. And a payroll campaign and newsletter shouldn’t share the same benchmark.
