updates.text: At Homebase, we talk a lot about being “Customer Obsessed", one of our 5 operating principles that laser-focuses all of our efforts on the small businesses we serve. But here's something we don't say enough: most of us got our start at one. In our San Francisco office, on your first day as a new Homie, you’re given a sign. On it, you jot down your very first job. Here are a few of the stories behind ours: Kate Botler Kodesh worked her summers at a marina on Peaks Island — a small community where the owners treated her like their own, and she learned that the best workplaces don't just give you a job; they give you a sense of belonging. Keyvan Rahmatian spent his teenage years at a car dealership that employed people nobody else would. It was then that he realized what small businesses have always known (& the rest of us are still learning): the widest doors build the strongest cultures. Linda Darling served as a hostess at a local pizza place. She’ll never forget her manager jumping in to wash dishes after someone called in sick. She learned you don't need a title to make a difference. They didn't end up at Homebase by accident. Every Homie has a version of these stories — a small business that gave them their start and taught them something real about people, work, and what it means to show up. This wall isn't decoration. It's a daily reminder of whom we're doing this for. Your story might belong on this wall too 👉 https://lnkd.in/gi6YBDwg #Homebase #JoinHomebase #LifeAtHomebase #Hiring #SaaS

updates.text: AI is reaching Main Street. But the smallest businesses are still playing catch-up. Homebase’s 2026 Main Street AI Gap Report surveyed 750 U.S. small business decision-makers. A few findings stood out: • 74% are using or piloting AI. • Adoption is 54% at businesses under $500K in annual revenue, compared with 81% at $5M or more—a 27-point gap. • 89% of adopters report a positive overall business impact. • Owners using AI for both scheduling and payroll estimate savings of 7.7 hours and $343 per month. • 62% of non-adopters are interested, but data privacy and fear of mistakes remain the leading barriers. My takeaway: making AI useful for small businesses means earning trust, showing clear value, and making it easy to get started. Read the full report: https://lnkd.in/gkimySqP #SmallBusiness #AI #FutureOfWork

updates.text: Turnover on Main Street jumped sharply in August, and we think the World Cup is why. Our August Main Street Health Report, covering 100,000+ small businesses and 2 million hourly employees, shows turnover up nearly 20% month-over-month, largely reflecting event-driven staff who came on for the tournament and have since moved on. Meanwhile, hiring's year-over-year decline kept narrowing, a sign the labor market may be stabilizing after a difficult 2025. Hours and headcount have been easing since 2024, a pattern that increasingly looks structural and consistent with immigration policy tightening labor supply. For business leaders, the takeaway is to separate the noise from the signal. A one-time event can move a headline number without changing the underlying trends. Full report linked in the comments.

updates.text: It’s jobs data week, and the August Homebase Main Street Health Report is out. Link: https://lnkd.in/ghiaRbbF Some key trends: 1. Hiring is still cooling for hourly workers - it was down 2.1% Y/Y in August. However, the pace of declines is slowing - a year ago, the decline was 3.1%. 2. Turnover spiked in August; it was up 7.2% Y/Y. Our hunch is that it is a one-time surge that reflects the end of the World Cup; turnover increased more in the 11 game-hosting metro areas than elsewhere in the US. 3. Wage growth was 6.2% Y/Y in August. That’s a little slower than a year ago (6.8%), but as with hiring, the deceleration is slowing. 4. August is typically an interesting month from a seasonal perspective. Along with April and January, it’s one of the few months of the year in which both directions of hourly employee churn (hiring and turnover) both increase month-over-month. Presumably, many high school and college enrollees return back to their studies (turnover), and employers need to hire their replacements.

Meet Tai Wong & Allen Liao — our AI Engineering summer interns and two builders who made the most of every single day. Their paths to Homebase are different. Tai found us on LinkedIn and felt an immediate pull to the mission — his dad runs a small business, so the mission was personal. Allen came through Emerson Collective and was drawn to something he doesn't take for granted: the freedom to build. That freedom showed up immediately. Within weeks of joining, they were embedded in real projects with real stakeholders building something that hadn’t existed in quite this way before. So they got to work — alongside a cross-functional team spanning Product, People Ops, and Engineering." 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺: new employees were learning our product through training that couldn't keep up with how fast the product itself was evolving. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: reimagine it. Make it interactive, immersive, and always up to date. They took Homebasics, our existing product training experience, and upleveled it. Click by click, workflow by workflow, new hires can now walk through our product in a way they never could before. And because it lives inside Homebase's sandbox environment, it updates alongside the product itself. No manual refreshes. Just a living, breathing part of the onboarding experience. New hires are now walking into Homebase with a richer, more interactive understanding of the product they're here to support and build. And the product team? They saw the build at our companywide Show & Tell, and came straight to Allen and Tai to talk about what's next. And that was just one of three projects they shipped this summer. But what made it all possible was something both of them kept coming back to independently: access. Access to paid AI tools with minimal restrictions. The freedom to try things. And a team that trusted them to do it. Allen put it best: "𝘉𝘦𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘣𝘢𝘴𝘦, 𝘐 𝘸𝘢𝘴 𝘶𝘴𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘈𝘐. 𝘕𝘰𝘸 𝘐'𝘮 𝘣𝘶𝘪𝘭𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘈𝘐 — 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘨𝘦𝘵𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘴𝘮𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘪𝘵 𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺 𝘥𝘢𝘺." updates.text: Who should have a voice in how packaging is evaluated? The answer may be broader than you think. Manufacturing sees how packaging affects line performance, while supply chain considers freight and fulfillment. Procurement is focused on total cost, sales and marketing on the customer experience, and finance on the broader impact to the business. Each team has a different stake in how well packaging performs, which is why evaluating it through a single lens can leave important considerations out of the conversation. → Before your next packaging review, consider how packaging performance affects different parts of your business — and whether the people closest to those impacts have a voice in how it’s evaluated. Understanding packaging’s impact across the business is the focus of our own Scott Sauer’s recent article, where he explores the questions manufacturers can ask to make more informed packaging decisions. Read “Why Packaging Performance Is Business Performance” at the link. #SustainablePackaging #InternationalPaper #BeyondTheBoxAdvantage #Packaging https://lnkd.in/e8HcaBd9

updates.text: Price, spec, and quality tell you a lot about a box. But do they tell you how it will perform in your operation? Supply reliability, technical expertise, and a clear understanding of your operation all play a role in the answer. At International Paper, that belief shapes how we approach every customer relationship. We call it the Beyond the Box Advantage — our commitment to bringing more to the partnership than the package itself. It’s a broader way of looking at packaging, asking not just What are we buying?, but: What does our operation need from the people and capabilities behind it? The next time you evaluate your packaging strategy, consider: → How resilient is our packaging supply? → What expertise is available when something changes? → Where could packaging help improve our operation? A strong box matters. So does everything behind it. #SustainablePackaging #InternationalPaper #BeyondTheBoxAdvantage #Packaging https://lnkd.in/ei_iQv-W

updates.text: Technology and forestry expertise can work together to protect what matters most. In Oklahoma, International Paper’s proprietary ForSite® mapping system identified a sourcing location as potential habitat for Blair’s Fencing Crawfish, a species of conservation interest native to Arkansas, Oklahoma, and Texas. That early insight helped our Fiber Supply team and the managing forester adjust the harvest plan to limit disturbance to sensitive aquatic habitat and support water quality. It’s a powerful example of how data, planning and on-the-ground expertise can support biodiversity, protect water resources and promote the long-term sustainability of working forests. Read more at https://bit.ly/4h60GAA #SustainableForestry #ResponsibleSourcing #Biodiversity #WaterStewardship #InternationalPaper

Sysco operates almost 340 distribution centers, in over 10 countries, with 76,000 colleagues serving approximately 730,000 customer locations. The company generated sales of more than $81 billion in fiscal year 2025 that ended June 28, 2025. As the world’s largest food-away-from-home distributor, Sysco offers customized supply chain solutions, bespoke specialty product offerings, and culinary support to drive customers to innovate and optimize their operations. We act as a trusted business partner to our customers, helping them grow through our industry-leading portfolio that includes fresh produce, premium proteins, specialty products, sustainably focused items, equipment and supplies, and innovative culinary solutions. Sysco is the global leader in selling, marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. The company generated sales of more than $81 billion in fiscal year 2025 that ended June 28, 2025.

As the world’s largest food-away-from-home distributor, Sysco offers customized supply chain solutions, bespoke specialty product offerings, and culinary support to drive customers to innovate and optimize their operations. We act as a trusted business partner to our customers, helping them grow through our industry-leading portfolio that includes fresh produce, premium proteins, specialty products, sustainably focused items, equipment and supplies, and innovative culinary solutions.

linkedin_company.about: A TRADITION OF QUALITY for FIVE GENERATIONS. "Give the people what they want." Saverio (Sam) Rosati Nearly a century ago these were the simple words Sam Rosati lived by; little did he know this humble philosophy helped shape the foundation on which Rosati’s Pizza was built. Sam’s father began the family’s rich tradition of serving delicious Italian food to customers in his New York restaurant back in the late 1890’s. After the turn of the century, the family moved to Chicago and opened yet another fine ltalian restaurant featuring “Italian Style Pizza”, a tasty appetizer consisting of homemade tomato sauce served on a crispy piece of bread. In 1927, following in his father’s footsteps, Sam opened his own Italian restaurant in downtown Chicago. When Sam retired, his sons were ready to continue the family tradition. The year was 1964 and pizza in America had evolved and was starting to take off. The first Rosati’s Pizza opened its doors in a suburb of Chicago. In 1970, Rick Rosati, great grandson of Fred Sr., continued the family tradition and opened his own Rosati’s Pizza in Arlington Heights, Illinois. By 1978, a total of ten individual Rosati family members owned Rosati’s Pizza locations. In 1979 the family decided to expand the business and began franchising the Rosati’s Pizza concept. In 1996 Sam Rosati, great great grandson of Fred Sr. opened his first Rosati’s Pizza location in Belvidere, Illinois marking the fifth generation of Rosati family members serving delicious Italian food. Other locations soon followed and Rosati’s Pizza was on the map.

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

updates.text: "It doesn't matter if we have two tables or 20. Crush it. Create something for a guest. They're gonna remember that forever." That's the standard at Port Union, a modern American restaurant in Chicago's Wicker Park from Chef Rodolfo Cuadros. Switching to a new POS wasn't an easy sell for the team. After a long time on one system, the comfort zone was real. SpotOn’s support is what won them over. With brunch about to launch and a whole new menu to build, one call to SpotOn got this answer: "Send me the menu and I'll do it for you." A simple tool to drive reviews mattered too, especially for a new restaurant still building its reputation. With SpotOn Mobile Pay & Review, guests leave a review right as they pay. That helps search visibility and builds trust with the next guest. Hit play for the full story 👇 #ShiftStories #RestaurantTech #RestaurantOwner #Hospitality #ChicagoRestaurants

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. Lemkin , Alex Bard , Dylan Field , Fidji Simo , Max Mullen , Shalini Rao , Alex Kurland , Naval Ravikant, Jonathan Neman , Claire Hughes Johnson , Dharmesh Shah , Cory Levy , John Andrew Entwistle, Andrew Steele , Joshua Browder , Sean Rad , Scott Belsky , Brett Schulman , Mike Vichich , Andy Pforzheimer , Harris Pollack , Stephen Kerns, Kimbal Musk , Max Altman , Ben Braverman , Geoff Donaker , Nick Bunick , Alexis Ohanian Sr. , Kipp Bodnar , Ankur Nagpal , Henry Schuck , Parker Conrad , Justin Mateen , Marcus Lemonis , Shaan Puri , Sam Parr , Tanay Tandon , Josh R. on, Josh R. , Immad Akhund , Garrett Langley , Guillermo Rauch . Dean Bloembergen , the team, and I are deeply grateful for everyone who has supported us, including those not tagged here. Owner exists to close the gap between small businesses and huge corporations. We’re starting with restaurant owners. They represent the American dream. 80% start as cooks or servers, then become first-time business owners. But they’re forced to compete with massive corporations, which spend billions on tech & marketing and hire entire teams of experts. We don't want local businesses to get crushed. Owner gives AI superpowers to small businesses, doing work they could never afford before, so they can do more than compete. They can win.

updates.text: So excited to share that Owner.com has closed a $240M Series D led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a $2.3B valuation. Everyone is debating how many jobs AI can cut. That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

linkedin_company.about: We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now. The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

updates.text: Great full-service restaurants are hospitality businesses first. For our latest campaign, the most compelling story we could tell was already happening inside these restaurants. Rather than tell it ourselves, we let their words and experiences lead. We partnered with three of LA's most iconic full-service restaurants: Ètra, Bar Étoile, and Stir Crazy. These are restaurants the hospitality industry looks to, places that have helped shape what modern full-service looks like. We went in without a script and asked them one question: what does it take to run a great restaurant? Those conversations became our latest film - a story about the business of hospitality, told by the people living it every day. Thanks to Evan Algorri , Andrew Lawson , Jill Bernheimer , Julian Kurland , and Mackenzie Hoffman for sharing their stories.

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby

updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

updates.text: Happy #NationalCheeseDay ! 🧀💛 It takes time, tradition, and an incredible amount of dedication to produce your savory favorites—and at Great Lakes Cheese, our family of employee-owners puts that dedication into practice every single day with every package we produce. As the nation’s leading natural cheese packager, we are proud to provide an affordable, nutritious staple that fuels families across the country. In fact, you’ve likely enjoyed our cheese without even knowing it! From the melted perfection on top of a slice from your local pizza shop to the packs you grab off the shelf at your go-to grocer, our hands help craft the products that bring people together. According to the International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA), the American cheese industry has grown into a phenomenal powerhouse, with more than one-third of all U.S. milk production dedicated to cheese. We are honored to lead the way, growing alongside consumer appetites while staying true to the craft and quality behind every single block. From our plants to your plate, thank you for making what we do possible!

Their success is a great reflection of what can happen when experienced operators, strong teams and a scalable franchise model come together. Congratulations to the teams at Grube Inc., Hoogland Foods and Built Different Brands! We’re excited to see what’s ahead. Read the full press release: https://lnkd.in/gD-z45ad

updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Margherita Magnifico is BACK for a limited time only! When we introduce new pizzas, we hold ourselves to high standards for quality AND convenience. This Margherita Magnifico is no exception. Our Director of Culinary Innovation Kathleen Kennedy tried 20 different recipes before landing the perfect bite. When crafting this simple yet delicious pizza, she had three principles: 🍕Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor 🍕Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications 🍕Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s She wanted to make sure she would be proud to serve this to her friends and family. We’re proud to have her on our team, adding another layer to our franchisees' key differentiators! The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. Our Chief Marketing Officer Steve Kennedy said it best: “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach.” Check out the hand-stretched crust, thick slices of mozzarella, and a shredded three-cheese blend topped with our signature basil drizzle…while supplies last! 😉

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

updates.text: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. Read the full article in QSR Magazine: How Top Growing Franchise Brands Have Cracked the Code on Real Estate Development #Franchising #FranchiseDevelopment #RealEstate #RestaurantDevelopment #MarcosPizza

Headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Marco’s Pizza is one of the fastest-growing pizza brands in the United States. Marco’s was founded in 1978 by Italian-born Pasquale (“Pat”) Giammarco and thrives to deliver a high-quality pizza experience, known for its dough made from scratch and its three fresh signature cheeses. The company has grown from its roots as a beloved Ohio brand to operate and franchise over 1,200 stores in 35 states with locations in Puerto Rico, the Bahamas, and Mexico.
linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
Headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Marco’s Pizza is one of the fastest-growing pizza brands in the United States. Marco’s was founded in 1978 by Italian-born Pasquale (“Pat”) Giammarco and thrives to deliver a high-quality pizza experience, known for its dough made from scratch and its three fresh signature cheeses. The company has grown from its roots as a beloved Ohio brand to operate and franchise over 1,200 stores in 35 states with locations in Puerto Rico, the Bahamas, and Mexico. Most recently, Marco’s was recognized as America’s Favorite Restaurant in the Limited-Service Pizza category by Nation’s Restaurant News using Technomic Ignite Consumer 2024 dataꝉꝉ. Other recent accolades include ranking No. 48 on Entrepreneur Magazine’s 2024 “Franchise 500” ranking, earning a coveted spot as the only top 5 pizza chain to rank on Newsweek’s 2025 “America’s Best Customer Service” in pizza chains list, earning a spot on QSR’s Top 50, and being featured on Nation’s Restaurant News’ prestigious “Top 500” ranking.


ꝉꝉAccording to Technomic’s 2024 America’s Favorite Restaurants data, Marco’s Pizza secured the top spot in the Limited-Service Pizza category with a 53.4% composite top-box rating, indicating the share of recent guests who gave the brand the highest possible rating for each of the guest experience attributes. Data for America’s Favorite Chains comes from Technomic Ignite Consumer, which collects information about how brands impact consumers and how consumers interact with those brands via online surveys. For more information:  www.technomic.com/ignite-consumer.

linkedin_company.about: Leprino Foods Company’s history dates back over 70 years, when Jim Leprino first started making small batches of mozzarella for local markets and eateries in the Little Italy neighborhood of Denver. We’ve grown a bit since then. Today, Leprino is the world’s largest manufacturer of mozzarella and a leading producer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein and other high-quality dairy ingredients. Still owned by founder Jim Leprino’s family, we are committed to sustainably feeding and nourishing families around the world. We strive to be the “World’s Best Dairy Food and Ingredient Company.” We started in a small corner grocery store in the early 1950s, and today we employ over 5,000 employees across the globe.

We’ve grown a bit since then. Today, Leprino is the world’s largest manufacturer of mozzarella and a leading producer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein and other high-quality dairy ingredients. Still owned by founder Jim Leprino’s family, we are committed to sustainably feeding and nourishing families around the world. We strive to be the “World’s Best Dairy Food and Ingredient Company.” We started in a small corner grocery store in the early 1950s, and today we employ over 5,000 employees across the globe.

crunchbase.full_description:
Pratt was founded in the USA some 20 years ago and, since then, has shown dramatic growth with sophisticated manufacturing facilities in more than 25 states.

The Georgia-based company operates an extensive Recycling Company to supply four of the most modern, cost-effective 100% recycled paper mills in the country – at their Conyers’ Campus and in New York City, New York, Valparaiso, Indiana and Shreveport, Louisiana.

The company is dedicated to the sustainability of the environment, its customers and its people. The cornerstone of Pratt’s mission is to protect and nurture the planet’s natural resources while reducing their impact on the environment by “Harvesting the Urban Forest.” By doing so the company also seeks to help its customers meet their environmental goals.

Pratt has been honored by environmental leaders such as former Vice President Al Gore, former British Prime Minister Tony Blair, Ted Turner, the Climate Group and Global Green for spreading the word that recycling is an important weapon against climate change.

crunchbase.full_description:
At Round Table, we’ve enjoyed a heritage of creating high quality, innovative pizzas for over 57 years. From our founder Bill Larson’s first little Round Table Pizza Parlor in Menlo Park, California in 1959 to 450 thriving restaurants today, Round Table has always stood for freshness, innovation and craveable flavors in everything we serve.
Most pizza chains use primarily frozen dough, and often skimp on both the quality and quantity of their toppings and ingredients to cut costs. Not at Round Table. We roll our dough fresh, from scratch, every day, in every restaurant. That dough is made from wheat grown for us on family farms in Idaho. Our cheddar cheese is aged to perfection, and combined with whole milk mozzarella and provolone in our famous three–cheese blend. We use only premium meats for our toppings, which we spread lavishly on every pizza, all the way to the edge of the crust. And our vegetable toppings are freshly cut at each restaurant, including our juicy, selectively–picked tomatoes. This commitment to quality and authenticity is why we say we’re “The Last Honest Pizza.”
While we’re proud of the ingredients we use, Round Table is more than just freshness and quality. We’re the place where you’ll find unique, innovative pizza creations that expertly combine flavors no one else can match. Over the years we’ve introduced more than 30 successful new products, including many that are mainstays of our menu today. There’s the legendary King Arthur’s Supreme, with pepperoni, Italian sausage, Italian dry salami, linguica, mushrooms, green peppers, yellow onions, black olives, three cheeses and our Zesty Red Sauce. And the Wombo Combo, featuring primo pepperoni, linguica, Italian sausage, crisp bacon, mushrooms, Roma tomatoes, artichoke hearts and green onions. There are many more delightful combinations to choose from, or you can select your crust, sauce and toppings and create your own masterpiece. With appetizers like our Garlic Parmesan Twists, and salad bars offering an array of fresh selections, Round Table presents a feast of flavors that bring our guests back again and again, whether they choose to dine in, carry out or have us deliver.
There are a lot of places that serve pizza. But there’s no one else with the freshness and flavors you’ll always find at the best place for pizza: your neighborhood Round Table — The Last Honest Pizza.

Slice puts technology, marketing, buying power, and support to work for these shops, empowering owners to build profitable businesses and remain at the heart of our communities. products_and_services.product_description: A bundled service plan combining pizzeria ordering, marketing, delivery support, supplies, software, training, customer support, and owner resources.
A direct online ordering system that lets pizzerias accept pickup and delivery orders through websites, business listings, social channels, and ordering marketplaces.
A managed phone-ordering service in which Slice representatives answer pizzeria calls, take orders, provide customer assistance, and transmit orders to the shop.
A point-of-sale system for receiving orders, processing payments, managing order operations, and analyzing pizzeria data across in-store, online, and phone channels.
A pizzeria website created and managed by Slice to present menus, business information, and direct online ordering capabilities.
Managed marketing services for customer retention and demand generation, including email, text messaging, loyalty programs, paid advertising, and promotional materials.

updates.text: We were proud to join Northside Economic Opportunity Network (NEON) for its 20th Anniversary Celebration and be among the inaugural recipients of its Angel Awards, recognizing the companies and civic leaders whose partnership and investment have helped advance NEON’s mission to build wealth for low- to moderate-income entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis. Since 2016, General Mills has supported NEON through philanthropy, food-industry expertise and GoodWorks pro-bono projects, where our employees lend their skills and knowledge to help local business owners grow their operations. This support contributes to NEON’s work through programs like its Food Business Incubator and Collective Kitchens, which help food entrepreneurs access the resources they need to grow. We’re grateful to celebrate this milestone alongside NEON’s entrepreneurs, team, community partners and fellow supporters — and a special thank you to our General Mills Community Impact team for the leadership and dedication they bring to this work and to the North Minneapolis community. #GStandsForGood #CommunityImpact #Philanthropy

updates.text: This morning, General Mills’ board of directors announced that Dana McNabb, current chief operating officer, will become our next CEO, succeeding Jeff Harmening, who will become executive chair of the board of directors, effective January 1, 2027. Dana has made significant contributions across her 27 years at General Mills, having led in senior positions across the company and around the world. As current COO, she leads all four operating segments and key functions, with a focus on our consumers and delivering growth. She is a proven, results-driven leader with a deep understanding of our business, our brands and our industry. We’re incredibly grateful to Jeff for his 32 years of impact at General Mills and the strong foundation he laid for our next chapter. Learn more here: https://lnkd.in/e7uW3tyu

updates.text: September was full of moments that brought our people and communities together. 💙 As part of Familia Heritage Month, employees volunteered with CLUES (Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio), to put together school-supply kits for local students. We also celebrated 20 years of the Mill City Farmers Market, where General Mills has been a founding funder and longtime supporter. At our World Headquarters, employees, families and friends laced up for our annual Run of the Mills, while current and former Pillsbury colleagues came together for the Funster event to share stories and celebrate the brand’s legacy. Meanwhile, the Edgard & Cooper team brought sustainability and a shared love of pets to life at Upcycled & Unleashed, where adoptable pups took the runway in upcycled designs. We also connected with fellow Minnesota leaders at the Minnesota Business Partnership event to talk about the future of our state. From giving back to celebrating the connections that bring us together, these are a few of the moments that made September special. #MillsMonthlyMoments #GeneralMillsLife

updates.text: Did you know that only 2% of people aged 2+ in the U.S. get enough whole grains daily?* That means most Americans are missing out on the benefits whole grains provide. For nearly 20 years, General Mills has made whole grain the first ingredient in our Big G cereals. Today, our Big G cereals deliver 39 million whole-grain servings each day – making a nutrient-dense breakfast more accessible to families. This #NationalWholeGrainMonth , we’re sharing simple ways to get more whole grains into your day. View our whole grains guide here: https://lnkd.in/eFy6rmWX #WholeGrains #Nutrition * Source: NHANES 2017-18

crunchbase.full_description:
ChowNow is an ordering platform dedicated to helping local restaurants grow and compete in a sustainable way. ChowNow helps local restaurants thrive. By helping diners discover the restaurants' delicious creations and helping restaurants connect with customers. ChowNow powers branded online ordering systems for independent restaurants via the restaurants’ own websites, on Facebook and Google pages, through ChowNow-created apps, and via ChowNow’s website, while also providing the restaurant partners key customer insights and marketing support.

The company does its services for a reasonable monthly fee, without the predatory third-party commissions charged by competitors. It also enables diners to connect with independent restaurants in communities to order takeout and in some cases delivery, in a way that’s sustainable and fair to restaurants.

ChowNow was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Playa Vista, California.

updates.text: Sometimes the message you need to hear comes when you least expect it. Last week, I had the opportunity to attend the HPSI National Conference in Salt Lake City. I met wonderful people, had great conversations, made new connections, and came away with plenty of insights. But one message in particular stayed with me. Our motivational speaker was José Hernández, a former NASA astronaut whose incredible story was portrayed in the movie A Million Miles Away. His story is remarkable, but it was his journey that really stuck with me: Anything is possible when you have a goal, create a roadmap, and stay persistent. He shared a simple three-part strategy for pursuing your goals. I've been thinking about it ever since: 1️⃣ Do we know the minimum requirements necessary to get where we want to go? Understand what it takes to reach the goal and make sure we're willing to do the work required to get there. 2️⃣ Are we studying the people we want to become? Look at the people who have already achieved what we're working toward. What are they doing? What can we learn from them? 3️⃣ Do we know what differentiates us from our competition? Understand what makes us unique and figure out how to use that difference to our advantage. Simple? Yes. Easy? Not necessarily. But incredibly actionable. No matter what stage of life or our career we're in, we always have an opportunity to change our trajectory. Set the goal. Visualize it. Create the roadmap. Stay the course. José's message has me revisiting my own goals, not just where I want to go, but what I'm willing to do to get there. If you're interested in learning more about José's journey, his book Reaching for the Stars is a great place to start. It is now on my reading list! What goal are you working toward right now and what's on your roadmap to get there? P.S. Check out Arin Perrott and I attending the HPSI Afternoon Food Show! #Leadership #ProfessionalDevelopment #Persistence #Foodservice

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: Kyle McPhee started at Papa Murphy's International 's at 18, making $6 an hour. Twenty-five years later, he's the chain's largest owner in Utah with 15 locations –– plus two more in Wyoming –– and the eighth-largest brand owner in the country. This month, he opened his newest store in Eagle Mountain with a new business partner: his 20-year-old son, Aydon. What makes his operation work: 140 employees, mostly teens in their first jobs, with a low turnover rate. His approach is simple -- "I just manage the way I would want to be treated." McPhee's stores are embedded in their communities. They sponsor elementary school spirit nights, provide pizzas to local charter schools, support the Oakley Rodeo, and contribute to employees' own sports fundraisers. Now a second generation of employees is walking through his doors -- the kids of former workers are asking to be hired. "I always joke that they keep me young," he said. Full story from the Salt Lake Business Journal. https://lnkd.in/g9uiWMF6

updates.text: Are whole grains and pulses factoring into your brand’s innovation strategy? If not, you may be missing a key opportunity to outpace the competition. As more consumers continue to benefit stack – prioritizing foods that deliver multiple nutritional benefits at once – whole grains and pulses are showing up as foundational ingredients for delivering protein, fiber, cleaner labels and affordability. This month in The Stack™, we’re talking with two industry leaders—Ardent Mills Chief Growth Officer Angie Goldberg and Grain Foods Foundation Executive Director Erin E. Ball. They’re breaking down: • The rising momentum of the benefit-stacking trend • The key benefits consumers continue to prioritize • How whole grains and pulses can help connect your portfolio to consumer expectations • What’s next for brands who want to lead in today’s dynamic landscape Be sure to follow The Stack™ to connect with what’s driving today’s consumers and shaping the products of tomorrow. #TheStack #ArdentMills #FoodTrends #ConsumerInsights #CPGInnovation #CPGIngredients

updates.text: A POS without built-in text marketing is like a margarita without tequila. It's basically just a glass full of lime juice and salt. Long gone are the days when a restaurant POS was a sleek cash register. Nearly every customer interaction passes through a modern POS in some form, accumulating a continuous record of guest behavior. When guest communication tools like text marketing are built in to that environment to create a unified marketing engine, marketing messages can be defined by what guests have actually done rather than by static assumptions. If marketing tools need to be bolted on to that environment...lime juice and salt. And did you know that text messages have a 95-99% read rate? For more delicious stats and more about how a modern POS can take advantage of customer behavior data to drive growth, check out this article on SourceForge .

updates.text: Is it time to renew your POS contract? Before you do, here are a few questions worth asking. Does your POS scale? Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? HungerRush is the POS partner behind every great guest experience. Get in touch.

Yet it remains cheese, milk's leap toward immortality." — Clifton Fadiman If you believe you are what you eat, then National Grilled Cheese Day is the perfect moment to shave off (...or unwrap...) a slice of immortality, melt it between two pieces of bread, and digest the divine. And tomato soup? Like Batman and Robin, Lucy and Ethel, Mario and Luigi, Frodo and Samwise, Han and Chewy, Michael and Dwight, Penny and Brain, Wayne and Garth, Rumi Mira Zoey and Bobby, The Dude and Walter, Pooh and Piglet, Jay and Silent Bob, Fry and Bender, or Wallace and Gromit ( — who were, yes, highly attuned to the lunar immortality of cheese)... While not officially "required" for a proper National Grilled Cheese Day celebration, that steady bowl of tomato soup is the classic lawful-good force multiplier. The OG 10xer. And is now a good time to talk about sourdough being bread's own leap toward immortality as well? Making a grilled cheese on sourdough and dipping it in tomato soup is basically like discovering Mario's infinite lives staircase. If you're reading this on April 12th, today is the day to make an Artemis-like leap toward your own immortality. Looking for other days to celebrate your favorite foods? updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

updates.text: Now Open: The Marco’s Pizza Operations Center of Excellence in downtown Orlando! This past week, our Chief Operating Officer John Meyers and our executive team celebrated with a ribbon-cutting and ceremonial “first-slice,” with the Orlando Mayor Buddy Dyer . As we continue growing our franchise footprint, we want to ensure every store owner is ready on day one. This training center was designed for exactly that. The center will be home to in-person Discovery Days, where you can spend real time with our leadership teams, see how training works, and ask questions you would otherwise save until after you’ve signed. The Center will also host Marco’s University classes, where franchisees can receive advanced training! Just like our Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores said, “Growth only matters if our operators are set up to perform, and this Center is how we make sure they are.” A huge thank you to the Orlando Economic Partnership for coming out to support our team at the opening! updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Margherita Magnifico is BACK for a limited time only! When we introduce new pizzas, we hold ourselves to high standards for quality AND convenience. This Margherita Magnifico is no exception. Our Director of Culinary Innovation Kathleen Kennedy tried 20 different recipes before landing the perfect bite. When crafting this simple yet delicious pizza, she had three principles: 🍕Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor 🍕Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications 🍕Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s She wanted to make sure she would be proud to serve this to her friends and family. We’re proud to have her on our team, adding another layer to our franchisees' key differentiators! The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. Our Chief Marketing Officer Steve Kennedy said it best: “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach.” Check out the hand-stretched crust, thick slices of mozzarella, and a shredded three-cheese blend topped with our signature basil drizzle…while supplies last! 😉

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

updates.text: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. Read the full article in QSR Magazine: How Top Growing Franchise Brands Have Cracked the Code on Real Estate Development #Franchising #FranchiseDevelopment #RealEstate #RestaurantDevelopment #MarcosPizza

updates.text: We’re rewriting how home kitchens mix dough. Introducing Ooni Halo Core - a compact spiral mixer engineered to outperform the stand mixers that have dominated home kitchens for decades. Following the sell-out success of our first spiral mixer, Halo Pro, we are taking the next significant step in our category expansion, adding another fantastic product to our indoor kitchen line-up. We are proud to introduce Ooni Halo Core Spiral Mixer which brings professional-grade, dual-kneading spiral engineering into a compact, countertop-friendly design that handles over 6 lbs of high-hydration dough with ease. Our Founder Kristian Tapaninaho notes: “Traditional stand mixers aren’t designed for kneading dough; they stall, overheat, and fail to develop gluten properly. With Halo Core, we’ve engineered a solution that fits on your counter but refuses to compromise on performance. We are making professional-grade spiral mixing technology the new domestic standard, giving home bakers the exact mechanical advantage used by the world’s best commercial bakeries.” Halo Core goes well beyond dough. updates.text: I used the Olo app for the first time tonight and since everybody on planet earth feels the need to give their opinion on a company trying new things, I figured I’d join the crowd 🤣. There’s clearly something here. A marketplace style platform that doesn’t silo the customer into one single delivery service is good for users, and it’s good for restaurants. It means the cheapest delivery possible for the restaurant, and the fastest food possible for the customer. Win win. I’ve heard a lot of chatter around how this impacts restaurants and competing technology platforms, but I haven’t heard much about how it impacts the end user. Isn’t that who we should all be trying to help at the end of the day? Now obviously, there are going to be holes in the product on day one. As with any new product, you have to feel out your users and mold to features they’re asking for. That will come with time and if Noah Glass has shown us anything, it’s that his team will figure it out. That said, there are some features I already really enjoy. The live delivery screen is what I would consider “delightful”. It’s easy to understand and gives me all of the information I’m looking for without overloading my screen. One thing I think we all need to remember is that helping end customers helps restaurants. If a platform can deliver a better customer experience, the user will associate that experience with the brand, not only the platform. I’m excited to see where Olo takes the product next. And a reminder to some of the harsher critics out there, building things in this industry is hard. We should be supporting and learning from each other because the more we do, the better products our customers will get to enjoy. #RestaurantTech

updates.text: 48 hours ago, we launched the Olo App. Since then, I’ve read every comment, article, and DM. I’ve answered as many questions as I can. Here are the four I see most: “Isn’t this just another third-party marketplace?” No. It’s a network, not a marketplace, for good reason. Every order hits the restaurant’s kitchen exactly like a first-party order with zero commission. The brand keeps the guest relationship and the data. The Olo App brings restaurants together as a coalition. “Will people really download another app?” 40 million guests already have an Olo Account. Sign in with your email or mobile number, and your favorite brands, order history, delivery addresses, and payment details come with you. We built this for the big middle: guests who love variety and don’t want to pay 15-30% more for it. “Isn’t the 5% fee just a commission by another name?” No. The guest pays 5% on top of the product subtotal. The restaurant pays zero commission and keeps the full profit of a first-party order. We show the fee at the top of the menu and again at checkout. Want the absolute lowest price? Order direct from the brand—we tell you that in the fee breakdown at checkout. “Who delivers?” More than two dozen delivery service providers through Olo Dispatch. We built delivery-as-a-service over a decade ago and have scaled it ever since. Those years also gave us answers to the hard questions on driver accountability, handoffs, and reconciliation. The Olo App is not an all-encompassing solution today. Circle back with us in 2030. We have big plans we’re already working toward. Until then: feedback and iteration. Miles to go before we sleep! 🚀

updates.text: YESTERDAY we launched the OLO APP and you can download it now!! https://lnkd.in/gQY7tTAd For years restaurant brands have been (rightfully) pissed about the math on third-party marketplaces. updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby
