The Mutti Pasta Sauce UK Tour has come to an end.

From London to Birmingham, Leeds, Manchester, Liverpool, Edinburgh and Cardiff, our Van travelled across the UK, introducing the new Mutti Pasta Sauce range to chefs, consumers, partners and everyone who shares our passion for tomatoes.

A journey filled with meetings, tastings and conversations that gave us the opportunity to share what drives us every day: a passion for uncompromising quality and the authentic taste of tomatoes.

A heartfelt thank you to everyone who welcomed us along the way and to all those who stopped by to meet us. The tour may be over, but the story of Mutti Pasta Sauce in the United Kingdom is only just beginning!

updates.text: Per noi, il pomodoro è sempre stato molto più che pomodoro. È cultura, maestria, conoscenza agricola, pazienza, storie di famiglia, campi estivi e un profondo rispetto per le persone che li coltivano. Ecco perché è un grande piacere vedere questo spirito riconosciuto da The Guardian , che ha dedicato un articolo al percorso di Mutti, ai suoi valori e al posizionamento premium nel mercato britannico. L'articolo cattura ciò che ci ha guidati per oltre 125 anni: un'attenzione incondizionata alla qualità, rapporti solidi con i nostri agricoltori e la convinzione che anche l'ingrediente più semplice possa diventare straordinario se trattato con cura e passione. Siamo grati a tutti coloro che contribuiscono a questa storia ogni giorno. --- For us, tomatoes have always been much more than tomatoes. They are culture, craftsmanship, agricultural knowledge, patience, family stories, summer fields, and a deep respect for the people who grow them. That is why it is such a pleasure to see this spirit recognised by The Guardian , which dedicated a feature to Mutti’s journey, values and premium positioning in the UK market. The article captures what has guided us for over 125 years: an uncompromising focus on quality, strong relationships with our farmers, and the belief that even the simplest ingredient can become extraordinary when treated with care and passion. We are grateful to everyone who contributes to this story every day. Here's the full article 👉 https://lnkd.in/erB-PpvP

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
At Mutti, we believe in the importance of recognising the worth of what may seem ordinary, but never truly is - the soil, the tomatoes, and the small, daily gestures that, over time, make a real difference. Behind every product lies a long-term commitment, built with care and patience. Not to chase short-time success, but to leave something meaningful for the future. 

Mutti is currently the most beloved tomato brand in Europe, dedicated to the processing of 100% Italian tomatoes. For 125 years, the company has been a tomato specialist, always owned and run by the Mutti family. Now led by the fourth generation, it continues to uphold the values that have made the brand so well-loved. Today, Mutti is the leading group in the tomato-based products market in Italy and Europe, with operations in over 100 countries.

The Company has always focused on quality, investing in research and innovation. To ensure the quality of its tomatoes, Mutti upholds a procurement policy that pays a premium price to all suppliers capable of delivering superior quality tomatoes. In addition, for more than 25 years the Company has promoted the “Pomodorino d’Oro”, an incentive that goes far beyond a monetary reward – serving as a source of motivation and economical support that brings pride and new sources for investments to the farmers who are dedicated to producing this iconic excellence of Italian food. The Pomodorino d’Oro also stands as a testament to the strong bond Mutti shares with its farmers, reflecting a relationship built on trust and genuine human connection.

Working for Mutti means becoming part of a business experiencing a sustainable international growth – yet, at the heart of this expansion is steadfast commitment to what truly matters: the quality of our products, along with economic sustainability. We grow and broaden our reach because we are confident in our ability to do so responsibly, maintaining the same exceptional standards while pursuing a long-term vision.

updates.text: “Our founders were, quite frankly, just hippies...” That’s Ahsan Jiva , EVP of Strategy & Transformation at Mellow Mushroom . The brand came out of the counterculture in the early 70s, started by people who didn’t want to work for anyone. Fifty years on, it’s still family owned and has never taken outside money. He says that’s the thing he sells hardest to franchisees. Swipe to hear why. The takeaway: ask whoever owns your brand what clock they’re on. If their timeline is shorter than your franchise agreement, you’re the one carrying the risk. Thank you Ahsan, for joining us at On The Clock 2026 to share your stories and insights that make a real difference for fellow restaurant operators!

updates.text: Today - October 23 - marks 73 years since our company was founded in 1953. What began as a small family business has become a business family whose impact can be felt far beyond our hometown of Plymouth, Wisconsin. The visionary thinking of Leonard A. Gentine who married Dolores Becker and started a family in Plymouth, set into a motion an enterprise that would forever change how America enjoys natural cheese. Leonard's winning spirit, produced a long line of industry firsts. His earliest innovations included custom equipment for cutting and packaging cheese, adapting a pasta cutter to automate shredding and pioneering gas-flushed packaging to help preserve freshness. Over time, Sargento was the first company to successfully mass produce pre-packaged sliced and shredded natural cheese. Today Leonard's grandson, our Chairman and CEO Louie Gentine , continues his vision as we strive to be the most innovative, best-loved real food company. From our Ultra Thin® slices, to Balanced Breaks® snacks to Sargento®Natural American cheese slices, our goal has remained consistent: listen closely, solve real needs and add value to our stakeholder's lives. Thank you to everyone - past and present - who has helped us reach this milestone and be come one of Fast Company 's 'World's Most Innovative Companies' this year. See our History of Innovation at Sargento: https://lnkd.in/g7xRsVjc #SargentoFamily #innovation #CEO #cheese #anniversary

updates.text: We're proud to share that we've earned three prestigious workplace rankings: America’s Greatest Workplaces in Manufacturing 2026, America’s Greatest Workplaces, and America’s Greatest Workplaces by State 2026 (Wisconsin) by Newsweek. "National Manufacturing Month is the perfect occasion to celebrate our teams in operations and our history,” said Louie Gentine , 3rd generation Chairman and CEO of Sargento. "Manufacturing is how Sargento began with my grandfather, Leonard Gentine, who was a machinist by trade. He saw a need for consumer-sized packages of natural cheese, and he created processes and machinery that were ahead of their time to bring his vision to life. Being recognized by Newsweek across these three categories is a true testament to the foundation he laid for us and our culture. Today, our manufacturing teams continue that spirit of innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality natural cheese to families across the country." These three honors reflect our legacy of manufacturing excellence, culture of innovation, and commitment to employees across production, packaging, and technical facilities in Plymouth, Kiel, Hilbert, Elkhart Lake, and St. Cloud, Wis. Congratulations Sargento Family. Read our full press release: https://lnkd.in/gMYm8zUE

updates.text: Fun fact: Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers worked at Sargento many years ago. Today, the governor returned to our shared hometown of Plymouth to break ground with our Chairman and CEO Louie Gentine on new workforce housing: 102 single family homes in a new subdivision called Scholar’s Ridge. For several years, building more entry-level housing in Sheboygan County has been a key focus of ours alongside others in our business community. That’s why we invested $2 million to help create the Sheboygan County Economic Development Corporation ’s (SCEDC) ‘Forward Fund’ which made this moment possible. Scholar’s Ridge is the third subdivision developed through SCEDC’s housing Intitiative, geared toward Wisconsin’s workforce. Each home will be priced to provide affordable homeownership opportunities for working families. We’re excited for the future and look forward to welcoming more families and opportunity to Sheboygan County. https://lnkd.in/gDSRdG_F #SargentoFamily #housing #CEO #cheese

updates.text: We're feeling good this Friday, grateful for our community partners: Hunger Task Force and Pauls Pantry . Our 3rd annual 'Touchdowns for Hunger' Day of Action in partnership with the Green Bay Packers , brought us to Hunger Task Force's farm in Franklin, Wisconsin where we harvested more than 1,300 pounds of apples to feed families statewide. Hunger Task Force has operated this 200+ acre farm since 2012 to provide seasonal fresh produce to its hunger relief network across Wisconsin and our Tribal nations. It's not every day you have a member of the Packers team to show up in an orchard to pick apples with you, but that's what happened Tuesday as kicker Lenny C. Krieg joined our 'Day of Action. Thank you for your time, Lenny. As the Official Cheese of the Packers and a family-owned company, we strive to make a difference off the field in areas that matter most. #GoPackGo #SargentoFamily cc: Jon Murphy , Tyler McCune , Amanda Wery , Jonathan Hansen , Mardi Smirl , Robert Hornacek , Peggy Osthelder , Addison Lund , Phillip Bock, Portia Young

updates.text: Today we announce our acquisition of La Terra Fina , maker of premium dairy-based dips, spreads and quiches. The acquisition expands our portfolio into grocery and club deli departments, and creates a Deli Business Unit alongside Consumer Products and Food Service & Ingredients. We are honored to also welcome approximately 250 new employees in Union City, CA to the Sargento Family. “For three generations, Sargento has built our success through industry-leading innovation and a real commitment to our stakeholders,” said Louie Gentine , our 3rd generation Chairman and CEO. “Entering the Deli is an exciting opportunity for the Sargento Family, that expands our capabilities, builds on the strength of the La Terra Fina® brand and brings new consumers to Sargento.” The closing of the sale has sparked promotions and new leadership roles across our three business units: Consumer Products, Food Service & Ingredients and today, Deli. “The acquisition of La Terra Fina represents an important milestone and growth engine for Sargento. It will strengthen our ability to deliver value for our employees, customers, suppliers and shareholders,” said COO Michael Pellegrino . “I want to congratulate Erin, Jeremy and Joy on their new roles as we align our leadership structure to support this exciting venture. Their leadership and expertise will help us welcome La Terra Fina to the Sargento Family, serve our stakeholders and continue positioning our company for long-term growth.” cc: Erin Price , Jeremy Schellin , Joy Judski Read our full press release: https://lnkd.in/gUZyg2q4 #SargentoFamily | #businessnews | #leadership | #CEO | #cheese

updates.text: We're pleased to announce continued investments in the leadership, capabilities and operational excellence that support long-term growth. These actions include leadership appointments across Food Safety & Quality, Manufacturing and Strategic Sourcing, as well as a planned transition in the company’s Innovation. "At Sargento, our success has always been built on high quality, real food innovation, and a commitment to our stakeholders,” said Louie Gentine, third-generation Chairman and CEO of Sargento. “As we position our leadership team to guide us into the future, we are strengthening the values that have driven us for generations. I am confident they will lead Sargento with integrity and a commitment to the principles my grandfather, Leonard Gentine, instilled in our company from the very beginning.” As Gerard (Rod) Hogan prepares to retire in January 2027, we thank him for the incredible impact he's had on Sargento through his leadership, innovation, and commitment to developing others. His contributions were recently recognized with the Founder's Ring, our highest honor. Please read our full leadership announcement as we congratulate Holly Baumgart , Steve Cahoon in the new roles and welcome Jack Lindsay and Tim Finnerty to the Sargento Family: https://lnkd.in/eR53Uhyv

updates.text: As college students head back to campus, we're proud to announce that we have been named by Forbes as one of America's Best Employers for New Grads 2026. "Our success has always been driven by our employees: the Sargento Family. We are committed to welcoming new graduates and students into our workforce, where they contribute at a high level and bring new ideas and ways of working to Sargento," said Louie Gentine 3rd-generation Chairman and CEO. "Being recognized by Forbes as a top employer for both new graduates and midsize companies in America is an incredible honor. It shows that the culture we have built over generations continues to drive our success and makes Sargento a place where you can start and grow your career." The Forbes ranking was determined through an independent survey of over 100,000 U.S. young professionals (under 10 years of experience) working at companies employing at least 1,000 people. Out of 2 million evaluations, scores were based on direct employee nominations and public recommendations from industry peers. Thank you, #SargentoFamily , for demonstrating our values to build meaningful experiences and relationships across all career stages. linkedin_company.about: We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now. The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now.

The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

SpotOn’s mission is to give small and midsize businesses a fighting chance, providing innovative software and payment solutions, supported by local and personal service, and delivered at a fair price. A leader in fully integrated restaurant management systems and small business technology, SpotOn offers end-to-end solutions which include marketing, website development, reservations, online ordering, appointments, eCommerce, digital loyalty, review management, as well as retail and restaurant point-of-sale (POS) solutions.

Doron Friedman, Matt Hyman, and Zach Hyman co-founded SpotOn in 2017 and its headquarters is located in San Francisco, California.

products_and_services.product_description: A cloud-based point-of-sale and restaurant management system for processing payments, managing menus and tables, handling orders, and viewing sales and labor reports.
Integrated payment processing for in-person, online, virtual-terminal, and invoicing transactions through SpotOn’s restaurant and small-business systems.
A commission-free online ordering and delivery solution that connects restaurant websites, guest ordering apps, delivery services, menus, payments, and the SpotOn POS.
A POS-integrated labor management platform for scheduling, labor forecasting, employee coordination, tip management, and payroll preparation.
Proprietary restaurant POS hardware including countertop stations, handheld POS devices, guest-facing displays, card readers, printers, cash drawers, and connectivity equipment.
A restaurant reservation and front-of-house management system for online bookings, waitlists, table layouts, guest information, reminders, and POS synchronization.

updates.text: Our VP of Product, Kevin Rood , walks through MCP access to PAR OPS data in this video. Short version: any tool your team already uses can now query PAR OPS directly. Analysts, AI assistants, your BI tool. They connect through a standard interface, so there’s no custom integration project, and the answers come from current data instead of last night’s file drop. Ask Claude “What was food cost by store last week?” and it pulls the answer straight from PAR OPS. Permissions carry over from the product, so a franchisee only sees their own stores. PAR OPS has its own AI built in. But if your team prefers a different tool, that works too. Your data, your setup. https://lnkd.in/dsiNCXrP

updates.text: For more than two decades, Domino’s® and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital - ALSAC ® have shared a belief in the power of hope. St. Jude has been Domino’s national charity partner since our first Thanks & Giving® campaign in 2004, and we are continually inspired by the generosity of our customers, franchisees and team members who help bring its lifesaving mission to life. Through this year’s campaign, customers can support children and families facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases by choosing the St. Jude Giving Combo, with $1 from each combo going to St. Jude, or by rounding up their order. Because of generous donors, families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing or food, so they can focus on what matters most: helping their child live, celebrate milestones and make memories together. Together, we can help St. Jude continue its mission: Finding cures. Saving children. ® Since the beginning of our partnership, Domino’s has raised more than $165 million for the kids of St. Jude, with a commitment to raise a total of $300 million by 2034. Join us in helping St. Jude give more children the greatest gift of all...time.

updates.text: Fire Prevention Month is here, and some Domino’s customers may get more than pizza at their door. 🚒👀 Throughout this month, participating franchise-owned stores across the U.S. are teaming up with local fire departments for surprise pizza deliveries via fire engine and free smoke alarm checks. If the customer’s smoke alarms work, the order is free. If not, firefighters will replace the batteries or install working alarms at no cost. Either way, it’s a win! For 19 years, we’ve proudly partnered with the National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ) and local fire departments to promote fire safety. Thank you to the NFPA and firefighters nationwide for helping keep our customers and communities safe.

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
ABOUT LITTLE CAESARS®  

Little Caesars, the Best Value in Pizza*, was founded by Mike and Marian Ilitch as a single, family-owned restaurant in 1959 and is headquartered in downtown Detroit, Michigan. It is the third-largest pizza chain in the world, with restaurants in each of the 50 U.S. states and 31 countries and territories. 
 
Known for its HOT-N-READY® pizza, Crazy Puffs®, and famed Crazy Bread®, Little Caesars uses quality ingredients, like fresh, never-frozen mozzarella and Muenster cheese and sauce made from fresh-packed, vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. The brand is known for innovation and is home to the exclusive Pizza Portal® pickup, a heated, self-service mobile order pickup station. Little Caesars is also the Official Pizza Sponsor of the NFL. 
 
A high-growth company with over 65 years in the $150 billion worldwide pizza industry, Little Caesars continually looks for franchisee candidates to join the team in markets worldwide. In addition to providing the opportunity for entrepreneurial independence in a franchise system, Little Caesars offers a simple operating system, a reputation for taste and value, and strong brand awareness with one of the most recognized characters in the country, Little Caesar. Little Caesars is proud to be part of the Ilitch Companies family of businesses.
 
For more, visit LittleCaesars.com and follow Little Caesars on TikTok, Instagram, and X.
 
*Limited to top 4 national pizza chains

updates.text: A little Stanislaus lore from the plant floor. 🍅 Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. Just before the first tomato hits the line, members of our third-shift crew, many of whom were retired Navy service members, raise the Stanislaus flag beneath the American flag. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed. What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture. That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

updates.text_html:
A little Stanislaus lore from the plant floor. 🍅

Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. Just before the first tomato hits the line, members of our third-shift crew, many of whom were retired Navy service members, raise the Stanislaus flag beneath the American flag. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed.

What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture.

That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

updates.text: Precision. Speed. Teamwork. You'd think you were watching a Formula 1 pit crew. But this is the Stanislaus Distribution Center, and these are our incredibly skilled forklift drivers. Every movement has a purpose. Every second matters. And every driver knows their role, anticipating the movements of others and working in remarkable coordination to keep the unloading process running smoothly. What looks effortless in this timelapse is anything but. Just like an F1 pit crew, that level of precision doesn't happen by accident. updates.text: Our Fresh Pack tomato season wrapped up about a week ago. As the dust settles, I keep coming back to the reason we do what we do: you, the restaurateurs who count on the products we make. This year's pack ran from mid-July through the end of September. We harvest during the "Heart of the Season," when tomatoes are at their peak flavor and color. From choosing the right harvest time for each variety to moving with precision in the cannery, every decision was made with our customers in mind. We know the high standards you set for yourselves, and we are committed to producing and delivering tomato products that meet those expectations. The Fresh Pack tomato season is a true team effort. Through the summer heat and long hours, our team stayed focused on one goal: harvesting tomatoes at peak freshness and capturing their vibrant red color, fresh aroma, and vine-ripened flavor in every can. Thank you for trusting us to be part of your success. We are proud of the work accomplished this season, and even as we take a moment to reflect, we are already looking ahead to next year's harvest. Until next time, Tom Cortopassi

updates.text: Fall Harvest is Almost Here! Before the first olives make their way to the mill, there's something just as important to bring together, our team! Our seasonal and year-round employees recently came together for Fall Harvest orientation, reconnecting with familiar faces, welcoming teammates, and spending time at the mill and in the olive groves as we prepare for another harvest season. For many of our employees, this isn't their first Fall Harvest. They return season after season, bringing experience, knowledge, and pride in what they do. Some even go straight from tomato Fresh Pack to olive harvest, bringing their dedication from one harvest to the next! There's something exciting about seeing everyone come together again, knowing that soon the mill will be busy turning freshly harvested olives into the olive oil Corto is known for. To our Corto team, we're excited to have you back and grateful for the dedication you bring to every harvest. updates.text: There’s something special about getting to share Stanislaus with the people who support us outside of work. During our Family Tours, employees had the opportunity to bring a family member or friend along for a guided look through the plant. Our guests got to follow the tomato journey from start to finish, experience Fresh Pack up close, and see a little of what we do every day. But these tours are about more than showing our families where we work. Their support helps us do what we do, especially during Fresh Pack, and giving them a glimpse into something they’re a part of in their own way makes the experience that much more meaningful. After the tour, everyone gathered in the Cucina for a meal together and a chance to talk about everything they had just seen. To all the family members and friends who joined us, thank you for supporting our employees and for being part of the Stanislaus story, too. updates.text: Tomatoes are still flowing. 🍅 For roughly 70 days, our cannery runs around the clock as tomatoes move from the field to the can during our Fresh Pack season. It’s a time at our company that is built on endurance. The kind of perseverance that asks you to keep showing up, shift after shift, day after day. Our chefs and restaurateurs understand that rhythm. They know the work is a marathon, not a sprint, and their dedication to the craft inspires us to keep moving forward and bring our best energy to work every day. The season isn’t over yet. We’re still flowing.

Tomatoes are still flowing. 🍅

For roughly 70 days, our cannery runs around the clock as tomatoes move from the field to the can during our Fresh Pack season. It’s a time at our company that is built on endurance. The kind of perseverance that asks you to keep showing up, shift after shift, day after day.

Our chefs and restaurateurs understand that rhythm. They know the work is a marathon, not a sprint, and their dedication to the craft inspires us to keep moving forward and bring our best energy to work every day.

The season isn’t over yet. We’re still flowing.

updates.text: Next Stop: The Can! During Fresh Pack, our tomatoes go on quite the journey through the plant. We’ve shared a few stops along the way, and now we’re following them to our Filler Seamers. This is where our tomatoes make their way into the can. Across our Filler Seamers, team members keep an eye on proper fill levels as cans move through this part of the process before they are closed and continue on to their next stop. When you work in one area of the plant, you don't always get to see every step our tomatoes take along the way. From the field to sorting and now into the can, each stop has a team of people helping move Fresh Pack forward. These are just a few of the many team members working at our Filler Seamers this Fresh Pack. Thank you to everyone behind this step of the journey! #SFPLife #CortoLife #StanislausandCortoLife #StanislausTomatoes #FamilyOwnedandOperated #CaliforniaTomatoes #CaliforniaGrown #StanislausFamily #Modesto #ModestoJobs #Careers #Agriculture #Cortooliveoil #EmployeeSpotlight #TeamStanislaus #BehindTheScenes #MeetOurTeam #Stanislaus #WorkFamily #OurPeople #StanislausStories #EmployeeExcellence

updates.text: Technology has changed a lot about the restaurant business, but one thing will never change: what people remember is how you made them feel. In this interview with Freddy’s VP of Guest Experience, Tim Woodburn, he touched on the importance of human connection in hospitality. Speed and convenience alone aren’t what create loyal guests. People come back because they feel welcomed. They come back because someone remembered them, took care of them, or made their family feel comfortable spending time there. That’s the idea Happy Joe’s 🍕 was built on. That’s why “happy” is in the name. Great food gets people in the door, but happiness is what keeps them coming back.
updates.title: Happy Joe's Pizza
updates.text_html:
Technology has changed a lot about the restaurant business, but one thing will never change: what people remember is how you made them feel.

In this interview with Freddy’s VP of Guest Experience, Tim Woodburn, he touched on the importance of human connection in hospitality. Speed and convenience alone aren’t what create loyal guests.

People come back because they feel welcomed. They come back because someone remembered them, took care of them, or made their family feel comfortable spending time there.

That’s the idea Happy Joe’s 🍕 was built on. That’s why “happy” is in the name.

Great food gets people in the door, but happiness is what keeps them coming back.

updates.text: My favorite thing about the restaurant business is that you don’t have to wait very long to know if you’ve made someone happy. The restaurant business gives me something a lot of industries don’t: immediate feedback from every single guest, every single day. There’s nothing more satisfying than seeing families spend time together over a meal. The excitement on a child’s face during a birthday party celebration at Happy Joe's 🍕 is contagious, and the whole team lights up in those moments. I really enjoy watching guests leave knowing they had a magical memory-making experience. I’ve always believed a Servant’s Heart is so important. When you focus on taking care of your guests, team members, franchisees, and vendor partners, the impact is right in front of you. Seeing the experiences everyone enjoys sharing every day never gets old, and that’s what Happy Joe’s 🍕 has always been about. #RestaurantLeadership #Hospitality #ServantLeadership

updates.text: One of the advantages of a strong franchise system is the ability to reflect the local community while still delivering the experience and hospitality our guests expect from the brand. People should be able to count on the things that define the restaurant. The quality of the food. The experience. The standards that make it recognizable wherever they visit. The hospitality. At the same time, every community likes seeing a little of itself in the brand. I remember the excitement when Happy Joe’s 🍕 created a Chorizo omelet pizza specifically for our new Oro Valley, Arizona, location. It gave our new guests something that reflected their local tastes while still fitting naturally within our brand. You can maintain brand consistency while still giving each restaurant the opportunity to connect individually with the community it serves. This balance is one of the things that has made franchising so rewarding to me in my 40+ years living the dream.

updates.text: Guests aren’t going out to eat as often as they used to. NJ.com last month highlighted how families are dining out less and being more intentional about where they spend their money. That’s something happening all across the country. As visits become less frequent, expectations go up. Families need more from even a quick night out, and they’re choosing places they trust to deliver a consistent meal and an experience that justifies the time spent. There’s less room for trial and error now. Guests are more likely to return to places they trust rather than try something new. For brands like Happy Joe’s 🍕, that puts more weight on what we already concentrate on - earning that trust and keeping it. Consistent food. Teams that are attentive and responsive. A space that feels comfortable. Now more than ever, every visit has to count.

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
ABOUT HAPPY JOE'S PIZZA & ICE CREAM ®

Headquartered in Davenport, Iowa, Happy Joe's Pizza was founded in 1972 by Lawrence “Joe” Whitty, a professional baker by trade otherwise known to everyone simply as Happy Joe. Our company started as a small, single, family-owned pizza and ice cream restaurant in the Village of East Davenport and has since grown to become an Iconic Midwestern pizza chain. We're known for our signature specialty pizzas, ice cream, birthday parties, Happy the Dog mascot and of course creating fun lasting memories for generations of guests! We have approximately 50 restaurants throughout the United States with franchisee owned locations in Florida, Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota, Missouri, North Dakota, Texas, and Wisconsin. 

We are experiencing high growth and expansion Internationally as well, with our recently opened Roxy, Cairo, Egypt restaurant by Ahmed El Batran's family-owned franchise group HJ Happy Joe’s Middle East, LLC. Several more locations are under construction in Egypt that include Sodic, Mall of Arabia, Lotus, and Mall of Egypt. Additional development locations include 26th of July and New Cairo properties. HJ Happy Joe’s Middle East, LLC was awarded a master franchise agreement in 2022 for 10 countries and 25 units with expectations to expand the brand into other countries such as Abu Dhabi, Bahrain, Dubai, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Sharjah, and Saudi Arabia in the next seven years.

Our 2023 plans in the US market include new franchisee owned restaurants opening in Branson, Missouri; Navarre, Florida; and the Dallas, Texas metro area. Happy Joe's has been creating entrepreneurial self-confidence for existing and new franchisee owners through brand guidance, on-going training, and support within our franchise system for more than fifty years. We're always looking for minority, veteran, and female-owned franchise candidates to join our brand in expanding markets through multi-unit opportunities.

crunchbase.full_description:
Founded in 1972 in Bettendorf, Iowa, by a one-time Shakey's Pizza manager, Lawrence Joseph "Happy Joe" Whitty, the chain has, from its beginning, been known for innovation. Whitty was disciplined by his former employer for hosting a children's birthday party at the pizza restaurant. Once he opened the first Happy Joe's location, by contrast, such parties were not only encouraged but celebrated in epic fashion.

Whitty's unique vision fueled the company's expansion in the midwestern and southern United States, as well as opening a Happy Joe's boat-shaped restaurant on the Nile River in Egypt during the 1980s. He related that, in the early days, a couple who had had fun at a birthday party asked about investing in a franchise. At the time, he said, he knew nothing about how to make that happen and had never really intended to expand. But expand he did.

The chain took form as a combination pizza parlor and ice cream palace, known Whitty also claimed credit for inventing the chain's best-selling product -- The Taco Pizza. In 2005, Happy Joe's began serving breakfast pizza at select locations, and in 2013 it debuted a flatbread pizza.

Shortly after that, Whitty's company introduced a second concept restaurant known as Happy Joe's Pizza Grille, with a limited buffet format. In addition to signature pizzas, diners are able to order traditional American fare that now includes a selection of tasty appetizers, pasta, popular sandwiches, gourmet salads, dessert pizzas, hand-dipped ice cream cones, and other family favorites.

Happy Joe's continues to focus on fun and family connections and is committed to causes that benefit children, as it has been since its founding.
Today, Happy Joe's embraces new technology and has faced major challenges during the COVID pandemic, but still offers a family-friendly experience that emphasizes fun as well as good food.

Happy Joe's is one of only a handful of worldwide brands that connect emotionally with its guests. A very different type of pizza brand; at Happy Joe’s, pizza dough is a blank canvas. There are no restrictions to pizza toppings based on preconceived norms. 

Very few restaurant brands can celebrate 50 years in business. Even fewer are true to the vision held by their founders. But this pizza (and more) chain epitomizes the "can do" spirit that led to its initial success. A Happy Joe's location in Dubuque, Iowa, and the original Bettendorf location continue to lead the chain year in and year out in sales and guest counts.

They both offer consistently excellent food, great value for the dollar, are heavily involved in their local community, and operate with a Servant's Heart, Warrior Spirit, and are passionate about their business.

One of the founder's annual practices was to close each location one day a year and invite children with special needs for a party. He also encouraged his franchisees to hire workers with special needs or disabilities. And he established the Happy Joe's Kids Foundation, which focuses on outreach to children with special needs. Its work continues to this day.

Happy Joe’s focuses on family connections and being the place to celebrate any family event. Whether it’s a school or community group event, Happy Joe’s creates lifelong magical memories for its guests.

Happy Joe's has been serving America's two favorite foods -- pizza and ice cream -- for five decades, bringing smiles to the faces of countless families. Over the past 18 months, Happy Joe's has signed more franchise agreements and opened more new locations than during the past decade, pointing to the fact that Americans are hungry for good times in a family-friendly environment.

The chain has also attracted attention in the industry and has been named a QSR (Quick Service Restaurant) "Top 50" Contender, a FastCasual "Top 200" concept, a "Top 400" business by Franchise Times, and a "Top 500" restaurant by Nation's Restaurant News.

That's not a bad record for a chain begun on a shoestring budget by a man who just wanted to have some fun by serving unique pizzas and ice cream at children's birthday parties.

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

updates.text: Grubhub is proud to be recognized with the UserTesting Illumi Award for Emerging Innovator — and it came out of one of the biggest moments of our year. We recently made a bold move: removing delivery and service fees on restaurant orders over $50, supported by a campaign during the Big Game. As soon as the campaign launched, we ran three parallel research studies to capture real-time customer reactions. Within 48 hours, we had clear feedback. Customers were excited about the offer, but we identified opportunities to make the experience even stronger. Teams across the business moved quickly to update parts of the app and campaign creative while the campaign was still live. That fast feedback loop helped us improve the customer experience during a high-visibility moment — driving stronger AOV, better brand perception, and a campaign that delivered on its promise. The combination of customer insight, speed, and cross-functional execution helped turn a bold idea into meaningful business impact.

linkedin_company.about: For over 100 years, Shamrock Foods Company has worked to ensure people come first – our 5,000+ associates, our customers, and the families we serve across the nation. A privately held, family-owned and -operated Forbes 500 company, Shamrock is an innovator in the food industry and has been since its founding in Arizona in 1922. Shamrock specializes in the manufacturing and distribution of quality food and food-related products through a family of companies, including Shamrock Foods foodservice distribution and Shamrock Farms dairy manufacturing, among others. Now led by the third generation of McClelland family leadership, Shamrock’s success is built upon three unwavering principles set forth by our founder, W.T. McClelland: An unwavering commitment to quality people, products, and service; innovation in everything we do; and commitment to the communities we are privileged to serve. Our unique company culture is guided by the motto to “treat associates as family, and customers and suppliers as friends.” Learn more about our products, philosophy, and current job openings at https://jobs.shamrockfoods.com.

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

linkedin_company.about: Headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Marco’s Pizza is one of the fastest-growing pizza brands in the United States. Marco’s was founded in 1978 by Italian-born Pasquale (“Pat”) Giammarco and thrives to deliver a high-quality pizza experience, known for its dough made from scratch and its three fresh signature cheeses. The company has grown from its roots as a beloved Ohio brand to operate and franchise over 1,200 stores in 35 states with locations in Puerto Rico, the Bahamas, and Mexico. Most recently, Marco’s was recognized as America’s Favorite Restaurant in the Limited-Service Pizza category by Nation’s Restaurant News using Technomic Ignite Consumer 2024 dataꝉꝉ. Other recent accolades include ranking No. 48 on Entrepreneur Magazine’s 2024 “Franchise 500” ranking, earning a coveted spot as the only top 5 pizza chain to rank on Newsweek’s 2025 “America’s Best Customer Service” in pizza chains list, earning a spot on QSR’s Top 50, and being featured on Nation’s Restaurant News’ prestigious “Top 500” ranking. ꝉꝉAccording to Technomic’s 2024 America’s Favorite Restaurants data, Marco’s Pizza secured the top spot in the Limited-Service Pizza category with a 53.4% composite top-box rating, indicating the share of recent guests who gave the brand the highest possible rating for each of the guest experience attributes. Data for America’s Favorite Chains comes from Technomic Ignite Consumer, which collects information about how brands impact consumers and how consumers interact with those brands via online surveys. For more information: www.technomic.com/ignite-consumer.

updates.text: Now Open: The Marco’s Pizza Operations Center of Excellence in downtown Orlando! This past week, our Chief Operating Officer John Meyers and our executive team celebrated with a ribbon-cutting and ceremonial “first-slice,” with the Orlando Mayor Buddy Dyer . As we continue growing our franchise footprint, we want to ensure every store owner is ready on day one. This training center was designed for exactly that. The center will be home to in-person Discovery Days, where you can spend real time with our leadership teams, see how training works, and ask questions you would otherwise save until after you’ve signed. The Center will also host Marco’s University classes, where franchisees can receive advanced training! Just like our Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores said, “Growth only matters if our operators are set up to perform, and this Center is how we make sure they are.” A huge thank you to the Orlando Economic Partnership for coming out to support our team at the opening! If you’re thinking about a Marco’s franchise, the best way to evaluate us is to see the kitchen, meet the team, and ask your hardest questions in person. Learn more: https://lnkd.in/gdBUt3zU

updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Margherita Magnifico is BACK for a limited time only! When we introduce new pizzas, we hold ourselves to high standards for quality AND convenience. This Margherita Magnifico is no exception. Our Director of Culinary Innovation Kathleen Kennedy tried 20 different recipes before landing the perfect bite. When crafting this simple yet delicious pizza, she had three principles: 🍕Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor 🍕Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications 🍕Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s She wanted to make sure she would be proud to serve this to her friends and family. We’re proud to have her on our team, adding another layer to our franchisees' key differentiators! The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. Our Chief Marketing Officer Steve Kennedy said it best: “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach.” Check out the hand-stretched crust, thick slices of mozzarella, and a shredded three-cheese blend topped with our signature basil drizzle…while supplies last! 😉

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

updates.text: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. Read the full article in QSR Magazine: How Top Growing Franchise Brands Have Cracked the Code on Real Estate Development #Franchising #FranchiseDevelopment #RealEstate #RestaurantDevelopment #MarcosPizza

updates.text: At Casey’s, great customer service is about more than completing a transaction. It's about creating meaningful connections that make guests feel welcomed, valued, and appreciated every time they visit. Recently, guests took the time to recognize two team members who exemplify that commitment to service: Charles from our Mount Enterprise, Texas store and Delanoe from one of our Oklahoma City stores. One guest shared that whenever Charles is working, they know their visit will be a great one. From remembering names and favorite orders to greeting guests with a smile, Charles creates memorable experiences that make guests feel more like family than customers. Another guest reached out to recognize Delanoe for the way he consistently treats everyone with calm, respect, and dignity. Whether it's a regular guest, a first-time visitor, or someone having a tough day, he makes people feel seen, heard, and valued. Every guest interaction is an opportunity to make a lasting impression, and that's exactly what Charles and Delanoe do each day. Through their dedication to serving others and creating welcoming experiences, they help turn everyday visits into meaningful connections. Charles and Delanoe, thank you for showing what outstanding service looks like and for making such a positive impact on our guests. We're proud to have you on the Casey's team. 👇 Help us celebrate Charles, Delanoe, and the many Casey's team members who create memorable experiences for our guests every day in the comments! #CaseysCARES #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys #TeamCaseys #CustomerServiceWeek

updates.text: As we celebrate National 4-H Week, we're proud to continue our partnership with the National 4-H Council , helping young people build the confidence, leadership, and life skills they need to become #4HBeyondReady . Across Casey's 19-state footprint, nearly 3 million active 4-H members are gaining hands-on experiences that develop communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills while preparing them for future success. We invite our guests to join us in supporting the next generation of leaders by: 🍀 Rounding up in-store purchases through October 11 🍀 Adding a donation to online orders through October 31 🍀 Purchasing participating Pringles products, with contributions generated through qualifying purchases Casey's will match guest donations up to $150,000, and Pringles will contribute up to $20,000. Together, we're creating more opportunities for youth across Casey's Country. We're also bringing learning to life this fall through eight interactive events with local 4-H members, providing hands-on experiences focused on retail careers, teamwork, and workplace skills. Thank you to our guests, team members, partners, and the entire 4-H community for helping young people discover their potential and prepare for bright futures. #National4HWeek #4HBeyondReady #CaseysCountry #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys

Across Casey's 19-state footprint, nearly 3 million active 4-H members are gaining hands-on experiences that develop communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills while preparing them for future success. We invite our guests to join us in supporting the next generation of leaders by: 🍀 Rounding up in-store purchases through October 11 🍀 Adding a donation to online orders through October 31 🍀 Purchasing participating Pringles products, with contributions generated through qualifying purchases Casey's will match guest donations up to $150,000, and Pringles will contribute up to $20,000. Together, we're creating more opportunities for youth across Casey's Country. We're also bringing learning to life this fall through eight interactive events with local 4-H members, providing hands-on experiences focused on retail careers, teamwork, and workplace skills. Thank you to our guests, team members, partners, and the entire 4-H community for helping young people discover their potential and prepare for bright futures. #National4HWeek #4HBeyondReady #CaseysCountry #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys

updates.text: 🏈 College football is back! And with more than 30 noon kickoffs in the first three weeks of the season, we set out to find the earliest-rising fanbase in Casey's Country. 🏆 The winner? Ohio State. Our all-new Casey's Tailgate Tracker also found that 9 in 10 college football fans eat pizza on gameday, with half of them grabbing their first slice before noon kickoffs. From breakfast pizza at the early-morning tailgate to fan favorites through the final whistle, Casey's is built to fuel football fans all gameday long. That's why we're back as the Official Pizza of Noon Kickoffs. We're also introducing our First-Team All-Casey's Country roster featuring Trevor Lauck, Isaiah Sategna III and Dre'lon Miller to help rally fans all season. And because every great gameday deserves great pizza, we're bringing back 40% off any-size pizza every Saturday during college football season with promo code TOUCHDOWN. 👇 Where did your team rank? #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys

updates.text: 🏈 Friday night lights are back, and we're proud to kick off a new partnership with Dave Campbell's Texas Football. Community has always been at the heart of everything we do. Supporting local schools and organizations is about showing up, celebrating local traditions, and backing the people and places that bring communities together. That's why we're excited to partner with an organization that has been telling the stories of Texas football for generations. This season, you'll see Casey's and Dave Campbell's Texas Football hitting the road to highlight outstanding communities across the state and recognize the people who make Texas football special. Keep an eye out for our Team of the Week, Scholar-Athlete of the Week, and special stops at select football games throughout the season. We're just getting started, and we can't wait to be part of the traditions, pride, and passion that make Texas football unlike anything else. See you under the lights.

updates.text: Those who serve our communities leave a lasting impact. We're honored to support the Hermann community's efforts to create a mural recognizing Sgt. Mason Griffith and his legacy of service. The planned 3,000-square-foot mural will stand as a tribute not only to Sgt. Griffith, but also to the dedication, sacrifice and courage demonstrated by first responders and community servants every day. At Casey's, we believe supporting our communities means showing up in moments that matter. That's why we're proud to contribute $15,000 to this project and help bring this vision to life. ❤️ Together, the Hermann community, including residents, local leaders and supporters, are rallying together to create a meaningful space that will honor Sgt. Griffith's memory for generations to come. We're grateful to be part of this community and play a small role in helping recognize those who dedicate their lives to serving others. 👇 Read more about the project and the community behind it.

linkedin_company.about: In 1959, armed with savings of only $1,800, William R. Larson opened his first restaurant in Menlo Park, California. He wanted to create a place where families could go to relax, to experience a real sense of community, and to share a superb pizza. Bill called his little restaurant Round Table Pizza Parlor. By 1962, demand was extraordinary. With three locations already thriving, employees and customers saw an opportunity to expand Round Table through franchising. The hard work and dedication of these founding franchisees has driven our tremendous growth. After more than 50 years, we have expanded the Round Table family to more than 150 franchise groups operating some 500 restaurants. Today, Round Table continues to serve up great tasting pizzas that customers crave. We roll our dough from scratch, add our fresh blend of three cheeses, and lavishly top our pizzas with only premium meats and garden fresh vegetables. We are also known for our unique specialty pizzas. Over the last 15 years, Round Table has introduced more than 30 successful new products, and we are considered a pioneer in pizza innovation. The world has changed over the last 50 years since Bill Larson opened his first pizza parlor. The fast pace often leaves no time for a relaxing family meal. But like Bill, we still believe that serving families is Round Table’s most important role. Parents are looking for the chance to sit down as a family in a place that welcomes, respects and celebrates family meal time. By serving a superb pizza and nurturing family connections in a comfortable place to gather, we can all be a part of bringing families closer together at Round Table for years to come.

crunchbase.full_description:
At Round Table, we’ve enjoyed a heritage of creating high quality, innovative pizzas for over 57 years. From our founder Bill Larson’s first little Round Table Pizza Parlor in Menlo Park, California in 1959 to 450 thriving restaurants today, Round Table has always stood for freshness, innovation and craveable flavors in everything we serve.
Most pizza chains use primarily frozen dough, and often skimp on both the quality and quantity of their toppings and ingredients to cut costs. Not at Round Table. We roll our dough fresh, from scratch, every day, in every restaurant. That dough is made from wheat grown for us on family farms in Idaho. Our cheddar cheese is aged to perfection, and combined with whole milk mozzarella and provolone in our famous three–cheese blend. We use only premium meats for our toppings, which we spread lavishly on every pizza, all the way to the edge of the crust. And our vegetable toppings are freshly cut at each restaurant, including our juicy, selectively–picked tomatoes. This commitment to quality and authenticity is why we say we’re “The Last Honest Pizza.”
While we’re proud of the ingredients we use, Round Table is more than just freshness and quality. We’re the place where you’ll find unique, innovative pizza creations that expertly combine flavors no one else can match. Over the years we’ve introduced more than 30 successful new products, including many that are mainstays of our menu today. There’s the legendary King Arthur’s Supreme, with pepperoni, Italian sausage, Italian dry salami, linguica, mushrooms, green peppers, yellow onions, black olives, three cheeses and our Zesty Red Sauce. And the Wombo Combo, featuring primo pepperoni, linguica, Italian sausage, crisp bacon, mushrooms, Roma tomatoes, artichoke hearts and green onions. There are many more delightful combinations to choose from, or you can select your crust, sauce and toppings and create your own masterpiece. With appetizers like our Garlic Parmesan Twists, and salad bars offering an array of fresh selections, Round Table presents a feast of flavors that bring our guests back again and again, whether they choose to dine in, carry out or have us deliver.
There are a lot of places that serve pizza. But there’s no one else with the freshness and flavors you’ll always find at the best place for pizza: your neighborhood Round Table — The Last Honest Pizza.

linkedin_company.about: We are Uber. The go-getters. The kind of people who are relentless about our mission to help people go anywhere and get anything and earn their way. Movement is what we power. It’s our lifeblood. It runs through our veins. It’s what gets us out of bed each morning. It pushes us to constantly reimagine how we can move better. For you. For all the places you want to go. For all the things you want to get. For all the ways you want to earn. Across the entire world. In real time. At the incredible speed of now. The idea for Uber was born on a snowy night in Paris in 2008, and ever since then our DNA of reimagination and reinvention carries on. We’ve grown into a global platform powering flexible earnings and the movement of people and things in ever expanding ways. We’ve gone from connecting rides on 4 wheels to 2 wheels to 18-wheel freight deliveries. From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

From takeout meals to daily essentials to prescription drugs to just about anything you need at any time and earning your way. From drivers with background checks to real-time verification, safety is a top priority every single day. At Uber, the pursuit of reimagination is never finished, never stops, and is always just beginning.

updates.text: For more than two decades, Domino’s® and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital - ALSAC ® have shared a belief in the power of hope. St. Jude has been Domino’s national charity partner since our first Thanks & Giving® campaign in 2004, and we are continually inspired by the generosity of our customers, franchisees and team members who help bring its lifesaving mission to life. Through this year’s campaign, customers can support children and families facing cancer and other life-threatening diseases by choosing the St. Jude Giving Combo, with $1 from each combo going to St. Jude, or by rounding up their order. Because of generous donors, families never receive a bill from St. Jude for treatment, travel, housing or food, so they can focus on what matters most: helping their child live, celebrate milestones and make memories together. Together, we can help St. Jude continue its mission: Finding cures. Saving children. ® Since the beginning of our partnership, Domino’s has raised more than $165 million for the kids of St. Jude, with a commitment to raise a total of $300 million by 2034. Join us in helping St. Jude give more children the greatest gift of all...time.
