updates.text: Fire Prevention Month is here, and some Domino’s customers may get more than pizza at their door. 🚒👀 Throughout this month, participating franchise-owned stores across the U.S. are teaming up with local fire departments for surprise pizza deliveries via fire engine and free smoke alarm checks. If the customer’s smoke alarms work, the order is free. If not, firefighters will replace the batteries or install working alarms at no cost. Either way, it’s a win! For 19 years, we’ve proudly partnered with the National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ) and local fire departments to promote fire safety. Thank you to the NFPA and firefighters nationwide for helping keep our customers and communities safe.

linkedin_company.about: We’ve grown to become the largest family-operated broadline food service distributor in North America by upholding the same business approach since 1897—being passionately committed to the people we serve. We believe in the power of good food—to bring people together and make moments special. Every product, every order, and every decision we make is inspired by the people on the other side of the plate. We distribute to foodservice operators throughout the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast and Southwest regions of the U.S. and coast to coast in Canada. Our company also operates more than 170 Gordon Food Service Stores, which are open to the public and provide the benefits of restaurant-quality products and friendly, knowledgeable service. Gordon Food Service Stores do not charge a membership fee. Gordon Food Service Stores are the primary supplier for many small foodservice operators, including: restaurants, churches, daycare providers, caterers, event planners, and other small businesses. We offer a broad range of employment opportunities throughout our corporate offices, distribution centers, and retail stores. We have a strong commitment to our employees and foster an environment that promotes internal growth, training, and career development opportunities. Gordon Food Service is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any person on the basis of age, sex, race, religion, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

crunchbase.full_description:
Papa Gino's is a web and mobile-based online food ordering platform that provides a wide range of authentic Italian taste pizzas for individuals.

Papa Gino's uses ingredients such as locally-milled hard winter wheat flour, water, yeast, salt, and oil to make pizzas and the specially crafted tomato sauce is made from vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. Their signature blend of three premium cheeses for an authentic pizza is also used in the process. It offers its users with catering and delivery services as well as gluten free food for a healthy lifestyle. The company allows its users to send personalized eGift cards that individuals can select the layout of the card as well.

Papa Gino's was launched in 1961 by Michael Valerio and the company is based in the United States.

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. Thank you to: Jack Altman , Jason M. Lemkin , Alex Bard , Dylan Field , Fidji Simo , Max Mullen , Shalini Rao , Alex Kurland , Naval Ravikant, Jonathan Neman , Claire Hughes Johnson , Dharmesh Shah , Cory Levy , John Andrew Entwistle, Andrew Steele , Joshua Browder , Sean Rad , Scott Belsky , Brett Schulman , Mike Vichich , Andy Pforzheimer , Harris Pollack , Stephen Kerns, Kimbal Musk , Max Altman , Ben Braverman , Geoff Donaker , Nick Bunick , Alexis Ohanian Sr. , Kipp Bodnar , Ankur Nagpal , Henry Schuck , Parker Conrad , Justin Mateen , Marcus Lemonis , Shaan Puri , Sam Parr , Tanay Tandon , Josh R. on, Josh R. , Immad Akhund , Garrett Langley , Guillermo Rauch . Dean Bloembergen , the team, and I are deeply grateful for everyone who has supported us, including those not tagged here. Owner exists to close the gap between small businesses and huge corporations. We’re starting with restaurant owners. They represent the American dream. 80% start as cooks or servers, then become first-time business owners. But they’re forced to compete with massive corporations, which spend billions on tech & marketing and hire entire teams of experts. We don't want local businesses to get crushed. Owner gives AI superpowers to small businesses, doing work they could never afford before, so they can do more than compete. They can win.

updates.text: So excited to share that Owner.com has closed a $240M Series D led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a $2.3B valuation. Everyone is debating how many jobs AI can cut. That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? I eat at Ashley’s Cafe (pictured) multiple times a week, and seeing the impact of our technology on Ashley’s business has been pure joy. It’s a front-row-seat to a movement that Owner is building - over 100 million guests that we’ve been able to bring to small businesses across the country. I really believe local business owners are the most inspiring people on earth, and it’s a privilege to build for them. Today we celebrate a fun milestone, and then we get right back to building for these amazing entrepreneurs. If you want to come build AI for (not against) people - we’re hiring. Careers page in the comments.

Owner provides small businesses, starting with restaurants, with access to AI-powered technology and automation capabilities that have historically been accessible only to larger enterprises, helping local business owners manage and grow more efficiently. updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

updates.text: Great full-service restaurants are hospitality businesses first. For our latest campaign, the most compelling story we could tell was already happening inside these restaurants. Rather than tell it ourselves, we let their words and experiences lead. We partnered with three of LA's most iconic full-service restaurants: Ètra, Bar Étoile, and Stir Crazy. These are restaurants the hospitality industry looks to, places that have helped shape what modern full-service looks like. We went in without a script and asked them one question: what does it take to run a great restaurant? Those conversations became our latest film - a story about the business of hospitality, told by the people living it every day. Thanks to Evan Algorri , Andrew Lawson , Jill Bernheimer , Julian Kurland , and Mackenzie Hoffman for sharing their stories.

crunchbase.full_description:
California Pizza Kitchen opened their first restaurant In Beverly Hills in 1985. Former federal prosecutors Rick Rosenfield and Larry Flax combined their passion for food with fresh high-quality ingredients to create innovative, hearth-baked pizzas such as The Original BBQ Chicken, Thai Chicken, and Jamaican Jerk Chicken, cooked in an open kitchen. The restaurant gave California a place in the pizza pantheon alongside Chicago and New York. Their California twist on global flavors resonated with guests, and almost immediately, CPK became a bustling spot for business and family gatherings.

Almost immediately after the first location opened, they expanded from California to more than 250 locations in more than 30 states and 11 countries. But it doesn't stop there; you'll also find us bringing smiles to the pizza aisle in your grocer's freezer, taking the edge off travel fatigue in major airports all over the world, feeding eager fans at sports stadiums and students on college campuses.

California Pizza Kitchen completed an initial public offering in August 2000 and traded on the NASDAQ National Market under the ticker symbol CPKI. On July 7, 2011, Golden Gate Capital completed the acquisition of CPK and as a result of the acquisition, the company’s common stock is no longer publicly traded.

On August 18, 2011, G.J. Hart was named President, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman.

updates.text: Growth is important but responsible growth matters even more. In franchise development, knowing when to say “no” can be just as important as knowing when to say “yes.” In an article from Pizza Marketplace, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares why disciplined growth is at the heart of our development strategy. From evaluating market capacity and real estate analytics to franchisee readiness and cultural fit, every decision is made with the long-term health of the brand and our franchisees in mind. At Marco’s, we believe successful franchising isn’t simply about signing more deals or opening more locations. It’s about building the right markets, with the right partners, in the right locations and creating opportunities for long-term success. As Gerardo puts it, “Discipline, not velocity, is the real differentiator for a development strategy built to last.” Read the full article in Pizza Marketplace: https://lnkd.in/gU24pijh

updates.text: Margherita Magnifico is BACK for a limited time only! When we introduce new pizzas, we hold ourselves to high standards for quality AND convenience. This Margherita Magnifico is no exception. Our Director of Culinary Innovation Kathleen Kennedy tried 20 different recipes before landing the perfect bite. When crafting this simple yet delicious pizza, she had three principles: 🍕Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor 🍕Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications 🍕Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s She wanted to make sure she would be proud to serve this to her friends and family. We’re proud to have her on our team, adding another layer to our franchisees' key differentiators! The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. Our Chief Marketing Officer Steve Kennedy said it best: “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach.” Check out the hand-stretched crust, thick slices of mozzarella, and a shredded three-cheese blend topped with our signature basil drizzle…while supplies last! 😉

updates.text: Real impact starts with real people. Long before Brandon Hudson was a multi-unit Marco’s Pizza franchisee, he was a kid in a Junior Achievement USA classroom learning early lessons about money, business, and opportunity. Those lessons really took hold as Brandon became President of the Marco’s Pizza Foundation, where he helps ensure the next generation of kids gets the same shot. Brandon’s story is what makes our Foundation partnership with Junior Achievement so important. It’s the full-circle moment for someone who knows firsthand what that support can do for kids. To date, the Marco's Pizza Foundation has contributed more than $1 million to Junior Achievement USA, helping fund financial literacy, work readiness, and entrepreneurship programs for students across the country. The Foundation has also given $475,000 to No Kid Hungry, supporting meals and food programs for kids who need them, bringing our total charitable giving to more than $1.5 million across all partners! And through employee engagement programs like our We're Golden, we equip franchisees with the tools they need to cultivate a thriving store culture built on growth, recognition, hospitality, and opportunity at every level. We are so proud of our franchisees who carry on this giving spirit and the generosity of our guests. A huge thank you to everyone involved!

updates.text: Real estate development is one of the biggest challenges facing franchise growth today and franchisors have an important role to play in helping franchisees navigate it. In a new article for QSR Magazine, Marco’s Pizza Chief Development Officer Gerardo Flores shares how leading franchise brands are adapting their approach to real estate, from greater franchisor involvement and data-driven site selection to incentives and nontraditional development opportunities. “For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites,” said Flores. At Marco’s, we believe strong development is about more than finding a location. It’s about providing franchisees with the data, expertise, support and resources they need to make informed real estate decisions and build for long-term growth. As costs rise and prime real estate becomes more competitive, collaboration between franchisors and franchisees has never been more important. Read the full article in QSR Magazine: How Top Growing Franchise Brands Have Cracked the Code on Real Estate Development #Franchising #FranchiseDevelopment #RealEstate #RestaurantDevelopment #MarcosPizza

crunchbase.full_description: Slice believes that local pizzerias deserve all the advantages of big chains without compromising their independence. updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. Authors Haochen W. , Yi H. , and Ryan Xie share the engineering behind this deployment. The work was also presented at the ICML 2026 RLxF workshop. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

updates.text: DoorDash 🤝 Dispatch Goods 🤝 The Story of Stuff Project We ran a really special pilot in City of Half Moon Bay this year: a dozen restaurants swapped single-use containers for ones that get washed, sanitized, returned, and reused. Thousands fewer containers ended up in the trash. The program’s still running, and we’re still tuning it. But reusable packaging is new enough that half the work is just explaining what it is! Thanks Story of Stuff for helping with that. I hope it gets other cities and restaurants excited to try it too.

From neighborhood institutions to local favorites putting their own spin on a classic, meet the pizza spots customers are loving across America. Full list in the comments.

linkedin_company.about: From humble beginnings in a small Iowa town to 200 plus restaurant locations across the Midwest, Pizza Ranch has grown with loyal guests and hard-working franchise owners. Striving to uphold the company’s Mission and Vision, each Pizza Ranch location is a part of our lore and can trace its roots back to the very beginning of the story. Cultivating its mission “To give every guest a legendary experience” since its inception in 1981 as a single store in Hull, Iowa, Pizza Ranch connects with its communities in a way that provides bridges for friends, family and colleagues to come together. Pizza Ranch® prides itself in offering a unique array of dining options including a pizza/chicken/salad bar buffet, carry-out and delivery service of all menu items. What makes Pizza Ranch® different? The people. It's the owners, managers and employees of Pizza Ranch® that strive to make their customers feel special...and it shows. Each month, Pizza Ranch® locations throughout the country receive hundreds of letters and comment cards from satisfied customers relaying their excitement about the extraordinary hospitality. This friendly service has helped Pizza Ranch® become one of the largest regional pizza restaurant chains in the nation. Beyond the legendary buffet, Pizza Ranch® showcases a commitment to serving communities. Restaurants partner with schools, churches, non-profits and other organizations to host fundraisers and social functions. Additionally, Community Impact Nights feature members of participating organizations helping serve Pizza Ranch® guests while they earn tips and a portion of sales from that night. Pizza Ranch® prides itself on providing these opportunities to raise awareness and much needed funding for community groups and programs that represent and serve their hometowns. Find out more about Pizza Ranch at www.pizzaranch.com and follow us for the latest updates. To learn more about available franchise opportunities, visit http://www.pizzaranchfranchise.com.

updates.text: A little Stanislaus lore from the plant floor. 🍅 Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. Just before the first tomato hits the line, members of our third-shift crew, many of whom were retired Navy service members, raise the Stanislaus flag beneath the American flag. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed. What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture. That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed.

What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture.

That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

updates.text: Precision. Speed. Teamwork. You'd think you were watching a Formula 1 pit crew. But this is the Stanislaus Distribution Center, and these are our incredibly skilled forklift drivers. It's the result of years of experience, focus, trust, and teamwork. To our forklift drivers, thank you for the expertise and pride you bring to Stanislaus every day. updates.text: Our Fresh Pack tomato season wrapped up about a week ago. As the dust settles, I keep coming back to the reason we do what we do: you, the restaurateurs who count on the products we make. This year's pack ran from mid-July through the end of September. We harvest during the "Heart of the Season," when tomatoes are at their peak flavor and color. From choosing the right harvest time for each variety to moving with precision in the cannery, every decision was made with our customers in mind. We know the high standards you set for yourselves, and we are committed to producing and delivering tomato products that meet those expectations. The Fresh Pack tomato season is a true team effort. Through the summer heat and long hours, our team stayed focused on one goal: harvesting tomatoes at peak freshness and capturing their vibrant red color, fresh aroma, and vine-ripened flavor in every can. Thank you for trusting us to be part of your success. We are proud of the work accomplished this season, and even as we take a moment to reflect, we are already looking ahead to next year's harvest. Until next time, Tom Cortopassi

updates.text: Fall Harvest is Almost Here! Before the first olives make their way to the mill, there's something just as important to bring together, our team! Our seasonal and year-round employees recently came together for Fall Harvest orientation, reconnecting with familiar faces, welcoming teammates, and spending time at the mill and in the olive groves as we prepare for another harvest season. For many of our employees, this isn't their first Fall Harvest. They return season after season, bringing experience, knowledge, and pride in what they do. Some even go straight from tomato Fresh Pack to olive harvest, bringing their dedication from one harvest to the next! There's something exciting about seeing everyone come together again, knowing that soon the mill will be busy turning freshly harvested olives into the olive oil Corto is known for. To our Corto team, we're excited to have you back and grateful for the dedication you bring to every harvest. updates.text: There’s something special about getting to share Stanislaus with the people who support us outside of work. During our Family Tours, employees had the opportunity to bring a family member or friend along for a guided look through the plant. Our guests got to follow the tomato journey from start to finish, experience Fresh Pack up close, and see a little of what we do every day. But these tours are about more than showing our families where we work. Their support helps us do what we do, especially during Fresh Pack, and giving them a glimpse into something they’re a part of in their own way makes the experience that much more meaningful. After the tour, everyone gathered in the Cucina for a meal together and a chance to talk about everything they had just seen. To all the family members and friends who joined us, thank you for supporting our employees and for being part of the Stanislaus story, too. updates.text: Next Stop: The Can! During Fresh Pack, our tomatoes go on quite the journey through the plant. We’ve shared a few stops along the way, and now we’re following them to our Filler Seamers. This is where our tomatoes make their way into the can. Across our Filler Seamers, team members keep an eye on proper fill levels as cans move through this part of the process before they are closed and continue on to their next stop. When you work in one area of the plant, you don't always get to see every step our tomatoes take along the way. From the field to sorting and now into the can, each stop has a team of people helping move Fresh Pack forward. These are just a few of the many team members working at our Filler Seamers this Fresh Pack. After a long time on one system, the comfort zone was real. SpotOn’s support is what won them over. With brunch about to launch and a whole new menu to build, one call to SpotOn got this answer: "Send me the menu and I'll do it for you." A simple tool to drive reviews mattered too, especially for a new restaurant still building its reputation. With SpotOn Mobile Pay & Review, guests leave a review right as they pay. updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

updates.text: "It doesn't matter if we have two tables or 20. Crush it. Create something for a guest. They're gonna remember that forever." That's the standard at Port Union, a modern American restaurant in Chicago's Wicker Park from Chef Rodolfo Cuadros. Switching to a new POS wasn't an easy sell for the team. After a long time on one system, the comfort zone was real. SpotOn’s support is what won them over. With brunch about to launch and a whole new menu to build, one call to SpotOn got this answer: "Send me the menu and I'll do it for you." A simple tool to drive reviews mattered too, especially for a new restaurant still building its reputation. With SpotOn Mobile Pay & Review, guests leave a review right as they pay. That helps search visibility and builds trust with the next guest. Hit play for the full story 👇 #ShiftStories #RestaurantTech #RestaurantOwner #Hospitality #ChicagoRestaurants

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

SpotOn’s mission is to give small and midsize businesses a fighting chance, providing innovative software and payment solutions, supported by local and personal service, and delivered at a fair price. A leader in fully integrated restaurant management systems and small business technology, SpotOn offers end-to-end solutions which include marketing, website development, reservations, online ordering, appointments, eCommerce, digital loyalty, review management, as well as retail and restaurant point-of-sale (POS) solutions.

Doron Friedman, Matt Hyman, and Zach Hyman co-founded SpotOn in 2017 and its headquarters is located in San Francisco, California.

products_and_services.product_description: A cloud-based point-of-sale and restaurant management system for processing payments, managing menus and tables, handling orders, and viewing sales and labor reports.
Integrated payment processing for in-person, online, virtual-terminal, and invoicing transactions through SpotOn’s restaurant and small-business systems.
A commission-free online ordering and delivery solution that connects restaurant websites, guest ordering apps, delivery services, menus, payments, and the SpotOn POS.
A POS-integrated labor management platform for scheduling, labor forecasting, employee coordination, tip management, and payroll preparation.
Proprietary restaurant POS hardware including countertop stations, handheld POS devices, guest-facing displays, card readers, printers, cash drawers, and connectivity equipment.
A restaurant reservation and front-of-house management system for online bookings, waitlists, table layouts, guest information, reminders, and POS synchronization.

crunchbase.full_description:
ChowNow is an ordering platform dedicated to helping local restaurants grow and compete in a sustainable way. ChowNow helps local restaurants thrive. By helping diners discover the restaurants' delicious creations and helping restaurants connect with customers. ChowNow powers branded online ordering systems for independent restaurants via the restaurants’ own websites, on Facebook and Google pages, through ChowNow-created apps, and via ChowNow’s website, while also providing the restaurant partners key customer insights and marketing support.

The company does its services for a reasonable monthly fee, without the predatory third-party commissions charged by competitors. It also enables diners to connect with independent restaurants in communities to order takeout and in some cases delivery, in a way that’s sustainable and fair to restaurants.

ChowNow was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Playa Vista, California.

updates.text: Growth starts with people. In the latest episode of Food for Thought, Jane Wakely , Chief Consumer and Marketing Officer and Chief Growth Officer, International Foods at PepsiCo, shares what it takes to build enduring brands and drive growth in a world where consumer behavior is evolving faster than ever. From human insight and creativity to cultural relevance and commercial impact, great marketers do more than build brands. They architect growth. At PepsiCo, that means meeting people where they are, showing up in the moments that matter, and creating meaningful connections through the brands they love. One key takeaway from Jane: human-centricity will continue to matter most. And for the next generation of marketers, don't chase fads. Create trends.

updates.text: The People Behind the Product: Meet Cory Behind every Grande product is a dedicated Associate who takes pride in getting the details right. For Cory, being a cheesemaker means never taking shortcuts. From monitoring the precision of the cheesemaking process to knowing when a batch meets Grande's standards, his role combines experience, skill, and attention to detail. "What surprises people most is how precise cheesemaking really is," says Cory. "If one parameter is off by even a little bit, it affects the cheese." After working hard to become a cheesemaker, Cory has developed a genuine passion for the craft and takes pride in knowing every batch is made with quality, care, and consistency. When asked what he wants consumers to know, his answer is simple: "Every single batch is made with pride and passion." #Grande #ManufacturingMonth

updates.text: At Casey’s, great customer service is about more than completing a transaction. It's about creating meaningful connections that make guests feel welcomed, valued, and appreciated every time they visit. Recently, guests took the time to recognize two team members who exemplify that commitment to service: Charles from our Mount Enterprise, Texas store and Delanoe from one of our Oklahoma City stores. One guest shared that whenever Charles is working, they know their visit will be a great one. From remembering names and favorite orders to greeting guests with a smile, Charles creates memorable experiences that make guests feel more like family than customers. Another guest reached out to recognize Delanoe for the way he consistently treats everyone with calm, respect, and dignity. Whether it's a regular guest, a first-time visitor, or someone having a tough day, he makes people feel seen, heard, and valued. Every guest interaction is an opportunity to make a lasting impression, and that's exactly what Charles and Delanoe do each day. Through their dedication to serving others and creating welcoming experiences, they help turn everyday visits into meaningful connections. Charles and Delanoe, thank you for showing what outstanding service looks like and for making such a positive impact on our guests. We're proud to have you on the Casey's team. 👇 Help us celebrate Charles, Delanoe, and the many Casey's team members who create memorable experiences for our guests every day in the comments! #CaseysCARES #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys #TeamCaseys #CustomerServiceWeek

updates.text: As we celebrate National 4-H Week, we're proud to continue our partnership with the National 4-H Council , helping young people build the confidence, leadership, and life skills they need to become #4HBeyondReady . Across Casey's 19-state footprint, nearly 3 million active 4-H members are gaining hands-on experiences that develop communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills while preparing them for future success. We invite our guests to join us in supporting the next generation of leaders by: 🍀 Rounding up in-store purchases through October 11 🍀 Adding a donation to online orders through October 31 🍀 Purchasing participating Pringles products, with contributions generated through qualifying purchases Casey's will match guest donations up to $150,000, and Pringles will contribute up to $20,000. Together, we're creating more opportunities for youth across Casey's Country. We're also bringing learning to life this fall through eight interactive events with local 4-H members, providing hands-on experiences focused on retail careers, teamwork, and workplace skills. Thank you to our guests, team members, partners, and the entire 4-H community for helping young people discover their potential and prepare for bright futures. #National4HWeek #4HBeyondReady #CaseysCountry #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys

linkedin_company.about: For over 100 years, Shamrock Foods Company has worked to ensure people come first – our 5,000+ associates, our customers, and the families we serve across the nation. A privately held, family-owned and -operated Forbes 500 company, Shamrock is an innovator in the food industry and has been since its founding in Arizona in 1922. Shamrock specializes in the manufacturing and distribution of quality food and food-related products through a family of companies, including Shamrock Foods foodservice distribution and Shamrock Farms dairy manufacturing, among others. Now led by the third generation of McClelland family leadership, Shamrock’s success is built upon three unwavering principles set forth by our founder, W.T. McClelland: An unwavering commitment to quality people, products, and service; innovation in everything we do; and commitment to the communities we are privileged to serve. Our unique company culture is guided by the motto to “treat associates as family, and customers and suppliers as friends.” Learn more about our products, philosophy, and current job openings at https://jobs.shamrockfoods.com.

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: Kyle McPhee started at Papa Murphy's International 's at 18, making $6 an hour. Twenty-five years later, he's the chain's largest owner in Utah with 15 locations –– plus two more in Wyoming –– and the eighth-largest brand owner in the country. This month, he opened his newest store in Eagle Mountain with a new business partner: his 20-year-old son, Aydon. What makes his operation work: 140 employees, mostly teens in their first jobs, with a low turnover rate. His approach is simple -- "I just manage the way I would want to be treated." McPhee's stores are embedded in their communities. They sponsor elementary school spirit nights, provide pizzas to local charter schools, support the Oakley Rodeo, and contribute to employees' own sports fundraisers. Now a second generation of employees is walking through his doors -- the kids of former workers are asking to be hired. "I always joke that they keep me young," he said. Full story from the Salt Lake Business Journal. https://lnkd.in/g9uiWMF6

updates.text: The People Behind the Product: Meet Cory Behind every Grande product is a dedicated Associate who takes pride in getting the details right. For Cory, being a cheesemaker means never taking shortcuts. From monitoring the precision of the cheesemaking process to knowing when a batch meets Grande's standards, his role combines experience, skill, and attention to detail. "What surprises people most is how precise cheesemaking really is," says Cory. "If one parameter is off by even a little bit, it affects the cheese." After working hard to become a cheesemaker, Cory has developed a genuine passion for the craft and takes pride in knowing every batch is made with quality, care, and consistency. When asked what he wants consumers to know, his answer is simple: "Every single batch is made with pride and passion." #Grande #ManufacturingMonth

After 13 years at Grande, her passion for learning and taking on new challenges led her to become an expert at the hand-tying process. updates.text: Employee Spotlight: Chris Balis 🍕✨ From store-level operations to managing construction logistics, Chris Balis embodies what it means to grow with a brand. Today, Chris serves as our Procurement & Maintenance Manager in the Construction Department, but his story at Pizza Pizza started on the ground in Operations. Armed with a deep understanding of how our restaurants run day-to-day, he eventually transitioned his skills into managing store equipment, facilities, and critical maintenance infrastructure. That dual perspective, knowing what a store needs operationally while executing high-level construction strategy, makes Chris an irreplaceable part of our team. He ensures our locations aren't just built, but built to run seamlessly for our team members and customers. As he approaches his 20-year milestone with us, we’re proud to highlight Chris today and celebrate the incredible expertise, dedication, and internal career path he brings to Pizza Pizza every single day. 👏🎉 #EmployeeSpotlight #TeamHighlights #CareerPath

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Congratulations to our latest Middleby MVPs, Varun Rallabandi from Newton Beverage Solutions, and Steven Boyd from Doyon/NU-VU & Carter-Hoffmann! Varun has constantly shown a willingness to go above and beyond to find the best, most effective software solutions for customers. His attention to detail has resulted in completing some amazing software engineering projects. Varun has represented Middleby and Newton at multiple tradeshows, and his presence is known. When Varun is on the show floor he does a great job of teaching and engaging customers by listening to understand their needs and offering solutions. Our customers and leadership teams speak highly of Varun and remember him after meeting him. Steven has been with Doyon/NU-VU for eighteen years!! He recently earned a well-deserved promotion to Product Manager & International Sales Lead at Doyon/NU-VU & Carter-Hoffmann. Congrats on your new role, Steven! Recently he developed several apps that enable customers to input their baking or cooking needs to be matched with their ideal product. He quickly (within days!) led the project from conception to launch, giving customers and reps a streamlined approach to make product browsing and selection much more simplified. Congratulations again to both Varun and Steven who ensure Middleby customers get our best, every day, every interaction. Your achievements are propelling our brands forward, and you both bring a positive, can-do attitude that inspires us companywide to achieve your standard of excellence. Thank you, thank you for all you do for your brands and Middleby! To learn more about Middleby careers and our MVP program, visit: https://lnkd.in/gyawVGE6 #middleby #middlebymvp #mvp #teammiddleby

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby

updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together. So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality through Afterpay, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next-generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale. Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business and helping sellers worldwide do the same. updates.text: Great full-service restaurants are hospitality businesses first. For our latest campaign, the most compelling story we could tell was already happening inside these restaurants. Rather than tell it ourselves, we let their words and experiences lead. We partnered with three of LA's most iconic full-service restaurants: Ètra, Bar Étoile, and Stir Crazy. These are restaurants the hospitality industry looks to, places that have helped shape what modern full-service looks like. We went in without a script and asked them one question: what does it take to run a great restaurant? Those conversations became our latest film - a story about the business of hospitality, told by the people living it every day. Thanks to Evan Algorri , Andrew Lawson , Jill Bernheimer , Julian Kurland , and Mackenzie Hoffman for sharing their stories.

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality through Afterpay, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next-generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business and helping sellers worldwide do the same.

Square is part of Block, Inc. (NYSE: SQ), a global technology company with a focus on financial services.

updates.text: We love the message from this FSR Magazine piece on Postino and Upward Projects | Postino • Federal Pizza • Lado A Lado • Windsor • Churn • Joyride . Hospitality tech only works if the people delivering the hospitality want to use it. Instead of managing guests through a handful of disconnected systems, they built an integrated tech stack with one central view of the guest. Then they launched the Postino Pass with their own teams first. Employees got training and time to try it, and they didn't launch until servers felt ready. Brittany Baldwin , CMO of Upward Projects, put it simply: “The data isn’t the goal. Better hospitality is the goal.” It reminds us of something Joshua Sharkey of meez said on our podcast: "The question you always have to ask is... will this be a tool that will require my team in order to be successful, or will this be something that my team will require to be successful? Does the tool rely on the team, or does the team rely on the tool?" The takeaway? Restaurant teams succeed when their tools are simple to access and easy to use. Read the full story: https://lnkd.in/gA2AXecy

updates.text: Yesterday, we hosted Women in Tech Sales (WITS) in our Toronto office for an honest conversation about what separates top sellers from everyone else. 40 women showed up to hear from Katarina R. , Kathrine Orlowski , and Shikha Bindra. A few things that stood out: → Politeness isn't pipeline. A prospect who loved the demo isn't necessarily a qualified deal. Did the conversation create enough value for them to actually act? → Top sellers aren't necessarily working the hardest. They're intentional about where they spend their time and which accounts deserve their attention. → AI is becoming a seller's job, too. The question isn't whether your company is building workflows for you. The sellers getting ahead are figuring out how to build and use them themselves. 🤖 From there, we broke into mentoring circles - smaller groups, experienced mentors, and candid conversations about what's actually hard right now. 💬 The event sold out weeks in advance, with the waitlist moving right up until the event. A pretty great reminder of what happens when women create space to learn from and support each other. We're proud to continue our partnership with WITS as a Silver Hiring Partner and connect with the next cohort of women building careers in tech sales. 🤝 🚀 What's next? The WITS Bootcamp is coming up next week, bringing together women looking to break into B2B SaaS sales, build their networks, and connect with tech employers. Applications are open now! 🔗 Apply here: bit.ly/3OTOicI

updates.text: Our team is back from #FSTEC in Grapevine, Texas, and the energy was unmatched! 🤠✨ We packed a lot into the week: from speaking sessions and conversations on the conference floor to VIP dinners, a Texas Rangers box, and plenty of late-night lobby bar catch-ups. More importantly, we got to catch up with dozens of customers, prospects, and GTM partners. And two themes came up again and again: 1️⃣ Tech stack consolidation: Operators are actively looking for ways to cut down on the number of tools they’re juggling. Bringing hiring, training, scheduling, payroll, and retention together in one HR platform is exactly what we’re building at 7shifts . 2️⃣ Actionable AI: There is a strong, growing appetite for AI that drives real operational value. Operators want automation that goes beyond buzzwords to make day-to-day work easier and surface proactive, data-driven insights. Through our AI-driven reports, we're helping restaurants address labor challenges *before* they impact the bottom line. Huge thanks to everyone who made FSTEC such a great week. Justin Kaiser , Jeremy Terman , Aron Bariagabre , Priya Busfield Nep , and Jordan Boesch will be keeping the conversations going with customers, prospects, and partners in the weeks ahead. Did you attend FSTEC this year? What was your biggest takeaway from the floor? 👇 #FSTEC #RestaurantTech #RestaurantHR #LaborOptimization #AI #7shifts #HospitalityTech

What we loved most was seeing people get out of their usual routines, try something new, and spend time together outside of the usual workday. And along the way, a few hidden talents made an appearance. We’ll take that as a pretty successful summer ☀️

updates.text: You're driving across the city for the third time today because someone forgot to order lettuce. Your phone buzzes at 6 a.m. with a text that an employee didn't show up, so you don't even make it out of the city limits before you're called back. This was Andrew R. Scott 's life for years. 100-hour weeks, running between multiple locations, making solid money on the P&L while his life disappeared. The turning point came after a near-disastrous expansion. He opened a fifth location next to his best-performing store, assuming it would perform the same way. Instead, it cannibalized 30% of his top store's customers and left him with heavy debt on short-term financing. That's when Andrew started rebuilding. He went from restaurant owner to founder of Ownershift - Restaurant Training, Coaching and Consulting , where he's now helped over 1,000 operators add an average of $100,000 back to their bottom line. Here's what he learned: 📊 Most people problems are actually system problems. If multiple staff don't know how to do something, the procedure isn't documented, trained, or clear enough. 📈 Track your food cost and labor weekly, not monthly. Andrew missed a 47% food-cost spike because his P&L was three weeks late. Weekly spot-checks can catch problems early. 🔗 You're the bottleneck when only you can do something. Write it down, train it, delegate to someone who can do it 80% as well as you. 💰 Higher wages can actually lower your labor percentage. Better pay reduces turnover. Higher productivity per person improves the wage-to-productivity ratio. Hear the full story on The Pre-Shift Podcast 🎙️ Spotify https://lnkd.in/g2GUvf2T Apple podcasts https://lnkd.in/gT97zVw8

crunchbase.full_description:
California Pizza Kitchen opened their first restaurant In Beverly Hills in 1985. Former federal prosecutors Rick Rosenfield and Larry Flax combined their passion for food with fresh high-quality ingredients to create innovative, hearth-baked pizzas such as The Original BBQ Chicken, Thai Chicken, and Jamaican Jerk Chicken, cooked in an open kitchen. The restaurant gave California a place in the pizza pantheon alongside Chicago and New York. Their California twist on global flavors resonated with guests, and almost immediately, CPK became a bustling spot for business and family gatherings.

Almost immediately after the first location opened, they expanded from California to more than 250 locations in more than 30 states and 11 countries. But it doesn't stop there; you'll also find us bringing smiles to the pizza aisle in your grocer's freezer, taking the edge off travel fatigue in major airports all over the world, feeding eager fans at sports stadiums and students on college campuses.

California Pizza Kitchen completed an initial public offering in August 2000 and traded on the NASDAQ National Market under the ticker symbol CPKI. On July 7, 2011, Golden Gate Capital completed the acquisition of CPK and as a result of the acquisition, the company’s common stock is no longer publicly traded.

On August 18, 2011, G.J. Hart was named President, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman.

updates.text: The path to better food access looks different in every community. #sponsored In Guatemala, families are growing and preserving more of their own food. In Iowa, a local farmer is building the infrastructure behind a community farm that can last. And in communities across the U.S., meals and essentials are reaching families at home and through their schools. The PepsiCo Foundation is working with local partners on each of these, addressing barriers from how food is grown to how it reaches the people who need it. updates.text: Growth starts with people. In the latest episode of Food for Thought, Jane Wakely , Chief Consumer and Marketing Officer and Chief Growth Officer, International Foods at PepsiCo, shares what it takes to build enduring brands and drive growth in a world where consumer behavior is evolving faster than ever. From human insight and creativity to cultural relevance and commercial impact, great marketers do more than build brands. They architect growth. At PepsiCo, that means meeting people where they are, showing up in the moments that matter, and creating meaningful connections through the brands they love. One key takeaway from Jane: human-centricity will continue to matter most. And for the next generation of marketers, don't chase fads. Create trends.

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

updates.text: We were proud to join Northside Economic Opportunity Network (NEON) for its 20th Anniversary Celebration and be among the inaugural recipients of its Angel Awards, recognizing the companies and civic leaders whose partnership and investment have helped advance NEON’s mission to build wealth for low- to moderate-income entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis. Since 2016, General Mills has supported NEON through philanthropy, food-industry expertise and GoodWorks pro-bono projects, where our employees lend their skills and knowledge to help local business owners grow their operations. This support contributes to NEON’s work through programs like its Food Business Incubator and Collective Kitchens, which help food entrepreneurs access the resources they need to grow. We’re grateful to celebrate this milestone alongside NEON’s entrepreneurs, team, community partners and fellow supporters — and a special thank you to our General Mills Community Impact team for the leadership and dedication they bring to this work and to the North Minneapolis community. #GStandsForGood #CommunityImpact #Philanthropy

updates.text: September was full of moments that brought our people and communities together. 💙 As part of Familia Heritage Month, employees volunteered with CLUES (Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio), to put together school-supply kits for local students. We also celebrated 20 years of the Mill City Farmers Market, where General Mills has been a founding funder and longtime supporter. At our World Headquarters, employees, families and friends laced up for our annual Run of the Mills, while current and former Pillsbury colleagues came together for the Funster event to share stories and celebrate the brand’s legacy. Meanwhile, the Edgard & Cooper team brought sustainability and a shared love of pets to life at Upcycled & Unleashed, where adoptable pups took the runway in upcycled designs. We also connected with fellow Minnesota leaders at the Minnesota Business Partnership event to talk about the future of our state. From giving back to celebrating the connections that bring us together, these are a few of the moments that made September special. #MillsMonthlyMoments #GeneralMillsLife

updates.text: The best way to start a new semester? Ice-cold Coke®, great food, and even better company. 🥤📚 Last night, we brought students from across Hong Kong's universities together for a Joint-U "Semester Kick-Off Feast (開Sem飯)” — a local tradition of universities in Hong Kong — because the start of term isn't just about lectures and deadlines. It's about the moments of connection that make university life unforgettable. From a joint-university rhythmic group chants (Dem Beat) to sharing a meal with friends old and new, the night was all about togetherness. And no gathering is complete without that signature Coca-Cola® fizz to make every toast just a little more special. Thanks to sica Ho and Freeeboyzzzz for bringing the energy, and to our partner restaurant Ladies' Street Sik Faan Co. for proving that the best meals are the ones shared. Because when Coca-Cola® meets local flavours and student spirit, that's an experience only we can bring. ✨ Here's to new friends, good times, and a semester to remember. #TheCocaColaCompany #CocaColaHK #RefreshTheWorld #MakeADifference #UniversityLife #Togetherness

updates.text: Today in Atlanta, our CEO Henrique Braun joined LA28 and the City of Atlanta to announce that our hometown will serve as the first stop on the LA28 Olympic Torch Relay. The Coca-Cola Company was also named a Presenting Partner of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Torch Relays, helping bring one of the Movement’s most enduring traditions to communities across the country. The Relay is planning to travel through all 50 states — the longest Olympic Torch Relay ever — bringing the spirit of the Olympic Games closer to more people on the road to Los Angeles. In 2028, Coca-Cola will mark 100 years as a partner of the Olympic Movement, making us the longest continuous partner of the Olympic Games. As the journey to the LA28 Games begins, we’re proud to help carry the spirit of the Olympic Games forward.

products_and_services.product_description: A carbonated soft drink sold globally in regular and reduced- or no-sugar variants. It is distributed in bottles, cans and fountain formats for retail, foodservice and hospitality consumption.

A portfolio of carbonated beverages including Coca-Cola, Diet Coke, Fanta, Sprite, Fresca, Schweppes and Thums Up. Products are offered in regular, diet and zero-sugar formulations across retail and foodservice channels.
A portfolio of bottled water, enhanced water, sports drinks and functional hydration beverages, including Dasani, smartwater, Powerade, BODYARMOR, Topo Chico, vitaminwater and Aquarius.

A portfolio of packaged and served coffee and tea beverages, including Costa Coffee, Gold Peak, Fuze Tea, Peace Tea and Georgia. Offerings cover hot and cold consumption occasions across retail and foodservice channels.
A portfolio of fruit juices, juice drinks, dairy beverages and plant-based drinks, including Minute Maid, Simply, fairlife, innocent, Del Valle and Maaza.

updates.text: A common assumption in the restaurant industry is that success starts with what's on the menu. But consumers don't come back because a product was great once. They come back because they know exactly what to expect. The order will be accurate. The wait won't be excessive. The experience will be familiar. The food will taste the same regardless of which location they visit or who's working that day. That's not just great operations. That's a system. The brands that scale aren't always the ones with the most innovative menu items. They're the ones that consistently deliver convenience and consistency at every touchpoint. Technology doesn't create great restaurants. It creates the operational foundation that makes great experiences repeatable. What do you think drives long-term restaurant loyalty more: product quality or operational consistency? Unsure? Learn more: https://lnkd.in/ekbx_KgU

updates.text: So we're back from NACS 2026, and honestly, we were surprised by what we heard on the show floor. It wasn't the sound of pitching, buzzwords, or typical conference chatter. It was the hum of skepticism. Customers had more questions this year than we've ever experienced before. Not because innovation has stalled, but because the stakes feel higher. AI was at the center of many of those conversations. Retailers recognize the opportunity, just as they once recognized the value of SEO. They know it has the potential to drive discovery, efficiency, and growth. What they're still trying to understand is how to capture that value without introducing unnecessary risk. One concern came up repeatedly: Will adding new value cost us the value we've already built? It's a challenge we understand because it's one we face ourselves. Large organizations can't afford to disrupt operations, customer experiences, or business continuity in pursuit of the next trend. That's why we've designed our solutions around a simple belief: innovation shouldn't require a tradeoff. Retailers shouldn't have to choose between what's working today and what will help them compete tomorrow. If you're asking the same questions, let's talk. Our team works with retailers every day to navigate these decisions and identify opportunities that support innovation without disrupting the experiences, operations, and outcomes that already drive success. Book a conversation with our team here: https://lnkd.in/gvFfcYyH

It was the hum of skepticism. Customers had more questions this year than we've ever experienced before. Not because innovation has stalled, but because the stakes feel higher. AI was at the center of many of those conversations. Retailers recognize the opportunity, just as they once recognized the value of SEO. They know it has the potential to drive discovery, efficiency, and growth. What they're still trying to understand is how to capture that value without introducing unnecessary risk. One concern came up repeatedly: Will adding new value cost us the value we've already built? It's a challenge we understand because it's one we face ourselves. Large organizations can't afford to disrupt operations, customer experiences, or business continuity in pursuit of the next trend. That's why we've designed our solutions around a simple belief: innovation shouldn't require a tradeoff. Retailers shouldn't have to choose between what's working today and what will help them compete tomorrow. If you're asking the same questions, let's talk. Our team works with retailers every day to navigate these decisions and identify opportunities that support innovation without disrupting the experiences, operations, and outcomes that already drive success. Book a conversation with our team here: https://lnkd.in/gvFfcYyH

updates.text: “Will switching systems disrupt my business?” A retailer from NACS asked this of Amit Acharya, Head of Product, Retail at NCR Voyix. Then Omni Talk's Chris Walton put the same pain point to him on camera. His answer: retailers aren't afraid of technology, they're afraid of disruption. When business is thriving, the last thing they want is to lose momentum. That's why the NCR Voyix platform is built on modular microservices, so retailers can modernize without missing a beat. What's the biggest thing holding your business back from upgrading legacy systems?

updates.text: Throughout history, every breakthrough has arrived with the same promise: Electricity. The internet. Mobile. Cloud. And now, AI. Each changed the world. But none created value simply because someone bought it. The winners weren't the organizations that adopted the technology first. They were the organizations that understood why they were adopting it. That's what stood out in Nick and Andy's conversation at NACS. Before AI. Before automation. Before modernization. Comes insight. What problem are you solving? What friction are you removing? What customer need are you addressing? Because ROI isn't just Return on Investment. It's the Result of Insight. Technology can accelerate almost anything. The question is whether it's accelerating a clear strategy or simply speeding up confusion. The investment comes after the insight. Not before it. Stay connected to get access to the full conversation. #NCRVoyix #NACS #RetailTechnology #DigitalTransformation #CustomerExperience #AI

updates.text: A little Stanislaus lore from the plant floor. 🍅 Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. Just before the first tomato hits the line, members of our third-shift crew, many of whom were retired Navy service members, raise the Stanislaus flag beneath the American flag. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed. What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture. That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

A little Stanislaus lore from the plant floor. 🍅

Around 15 years ago, our production team started a tradition to mark the beginning and end of each canning season. Just before the first tomato hits the line, members of our third-shift crew, many of whom were retired Navy service members, raise the Stanislaus flag beneath the American flag. It stays there until the last can of the season is sealed.

What makes this tradition so special is that it was created by the people on our plant floor. It wasn't something the company planned or directed. It grew from the pride our team takes in their work and the opportunity they have to help shape our culture.

That sense of ownership, pride, and attention to detail is woven into everything we do at Stanislaus. And we couldn't be prouder of the people who bring it to life, season after season.

updates.text: Precision. Speed. Teamwork. You'd think you were watching a Formula 1 pit crew. But this is the Stanislaus Distribution Center, and these are our incredibly skilled forklift drivers. Every movement has a purpose. Every second matters. And every driver knows their role, anticipating the movements of others and working in remarkable coordination to keep the unloading process running smoothly. What looks effortless in this timelapse is anything but. Just like an F1 pit crew, that level of precision doesn't happen by accident. It's the result of years of experience, focus, trust, and teamwork. To our forklift drivers, thank you for the expertise and pride you bring to Stanislaus every day. You make a demanding job look easy, and your work deserves the spotlight! updates.text: Our Fresh Pack tomato season wrapped up about a week ago. As the dust settles, I keep coming back to the reason we do what we do: you, the restaurateurs who count on the products we make. This year's pack ran from mid-July through the end of September. We harvest during the "Heart of the Season," when tomatoes are at their peak flavor and color. From choosing the right harvest time for each variety to moving with precision in the cannery, every decision was made with our customers in mind. We know the high standards you set for yourselves, and we are committed to producing and delivering tomato products that meet those expectations. The Fresh Pack tomato season is a true team effort. Through the summer heat and long hours, our team stayed focused on one goal: harvesting tomatoes at peak freshness and capturing their vibrant red color, fresh aroma, and vine-ripened flavor in every can. Thank you for trusting us to be part of your success. We are proud of the work accomplished this season, and even as we take a moment to reflect, we are already looking ahead to next year's harvest. Until next time, Tom Cortopassi

updates.text: Fall Harvest is Almost Here! Before the first olives make their way to the mill, there's something just as important to bring together, our team! Our seasonal and year-round employees recently came together for Fall Harvest orientation, reconnecting with familiar faces, welcoming teammates, and spending time at the mill and in the olive groves as we prepare for another harvest season. For many of our employees, this isn't their first Fall Harvest. They return season after season, bringing experience, knowledge, and pride in what they do. Some even go straight from tomato Fresh Pack to olive harvest, bringing their dedication from one harvest to the next! There's something exciting about seeing everyone come together again, knowing that soon the mill will be busy turning freshly harvested olives into the olive oil Corto is known for. To our Corto team, we're excited to have you back and grateful for the dedication you bring to every harvest.
