updates.text: There’s something special about getting to share Stanislaus with the people who support us outside of work. During our Family Tours, employees had the opportunity to bring a family member or friend along for a guided look through the plant. Our guests got to follow the tomato journey from start to finish, experience Fresh Pack up close, and see a little of what we do every day. But these tours are about more than showing our families where we work. Their support helps us do what we do, especially during Fresh Pack, and giving them a glimpse into something they’re a part of in their own way makes the experience that much more meaningful. After the tour, everyone gathered in the Cucina for a meal together and a chance to talk about everything they had just seen. To all the family members and friends who joined us, thank you for supporting our employees and for being part of the Stanislaus story, too. updates.text: Tomatoes are still flowing. 🍅 For roughly 70 days, our cannery runs around the clock as tomatoes move from the field to the can during our Fresh Pack season. We’re still flowing.

updates.text_html:
Tomatoes are still flowing. 🍅

For roughly 70 days, our cannery runs around the clock as tomatoes move from the field to the can during our Fresh Pack season. It’s a time at our company that is built on endurance. The kind of perseverance that asks you to keep showing up, shift after shift, day after day.

Our chefs and restaurateurs understand that rhythm. They know the work is a marathon, not a sprint, and their dedication to the craft inspires us to keep moving forward and bring our best energy to work every day.

The season isn’t over yet. We’re still flowing.

updates.text: Next Stop: The Can! During Fresh Pack, our tomatoes go on quite the journey through the plant. We’ve shared a few stops along the way, and now we’re following them to our Filler Seamers. This is where our tomatoes make their way into the can. Across our Filler Seamers, team members keep an eye on proper fill levels as cans move through this part of the process before they are closed and continue on to their next stop. When you work in one area of the plant, you don't always get to see every step our tomatoes take along the way. From the field to sorting and now into the can, each stop has a team of people helping move Fresh Pack forward. These are just a few of the many team members working at our Filler Seamers this Fresh Pack. Thank you to everyone behind this step of the journey! #SFPLife #CortoLife #StanislausandCortoLife #StanislausTomatoes #FamilyOwnedandOperated #CaliforniaTomatoes #CaliforniaGrown #StanislausFamily #Modesto #ModestoJobs #Careers #Agriculture #Cortooliveoil #EmployeeSpotlight #TeamStanislaus #BehindTheScenes #MeetOurTeam #Stanislaus #WorkFamily #OurPeople #StanislausStories #EmployeeExcellence

updates.text: At Casey’s, great customer service is about more than completing a transaction. It's about creating meaningful connections that make guests feel welcomed, valued, and appreciated every time they visit. Recently, guests took the time to recognize two team members who exemplify that commitment to service: Charles from our Mount Enterprise, Texas store and Delanoe from one of our Oklahoma City stores. One guest shared that whenever Charles is working, they know their visit will be a great one. From remembering names and favorite orders to greeting guests with a smile, Charles creates memorable experiences that make guests feel more like family than customers. Another guest reached out to recognize Delanoe for the way he consistently treats everyone with calm, respect, and dignity. Whether it's a regular guest, a first-time visitor, or someone having a tough day, he makes people feel seen, heard, and valued. Every guest interaction is an opportunity to make a lasting impression, and that's exactly what Charles and Delanoe do each day. Through their dedication to serving others and creating welcoming experiences, they help turn everyday visits into meaningful connections. Charles and Delanoe, thank you for showing what outstanding service looks like and for making such a positive impact on our guests. We're proud to have you on the Casey's team. 👇 Help us celebrate Charles, Delanoe, and the many Casey's team members who create memorable experiences for our guests every day in the comments! #CaseysCARES #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys #TeamCaseys #CustomerServiceWeek

updates.text: As we celebrate National 4-H Week, we're proud to continue our partnership with the National 4-H Council , helping young people build the confidence, leadership, and life skills they need to become #4HBeyondReady . Across Casey's 19-state footprint, nearly 3 million active 4-H members are gaining hands-on experiences that develop communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills while preparing them for future success. We invite our guests to join us in supporting the next generation of leaders by: 🍀 Rounding up in-store purchases through October 11 🍀 Adding a donation to online orders through October 31 🍀 Purchasing participating Pringles products, with contributions generated through qualifying purchases Casey's will match guest donations up to $150,000, and Pringles will contribute up to $20,000. Together, we're creating more opportunities for youth across Casey's Country. We're also bringing learning to life this fall through eight interactive events with local 4-H members, providing hands-on experiences focused on retail careers, teamwork, and workplace skills. Thank you to our guests, team members, partners, and the entire 4-H community for helping young people discover their potential and prepare for bright futures. #National4HWeek #4HBeyondReady #CaseysCountry #ItsNotCrazyItsCaseys

linkedin_company.about: ABOUT LITTLE CAESARS® Little Caesars, the Best Value in Pizza*, was founded by Mike and Marian Ilitch as a single, family-owned restaurant in 1959 and is headquartered in downtown Detroit, Michigan. It is the third-largest pizza chain in the world, with restaurants in each of the 50 U.S. states and 31 countries and territories. Known for its HOT-N-READY® pizza, Crazy Puffs®, and famed Crazy Bread®, Little Caesars uses quality ingredients, like fresh, never-frozen mozzarella and Muenster cheese and sauce made from fresh-packed, vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. The brand is known for innovation and is home to the exclusive Pizza Portal® pickup, a heated, self-service mobile order pickup station. Little Caesars is also the Official Pizza Sponsor of the NFL. A high-growth company with over 65 years in the $150 billion worldwide pizza industry, Little Caesars continually looks for franchisee candidates to join the team in markets worldwide. In addition to providing the opportunity for entrepreneurial independence in a franchise system, Little Caesars offers a simple operating system, a reputation for taste and value, and strong brand awareness with one of the most recognized characters in the country, Little Caesar. Little Caesars is proud to be part of the Ilitch Companies family of businesses. For more, visit LittleCaesars.com and follow Little Caesars on TikTok, Instagram, and X. *Limited to top 4 national pizza chains

ABOUT LITTLE CAESARS®  

Little Caesars, the Best Value in Pizza*, was founded by Mike and Marian Ilitch as a single, family-owned restaurant in 1959 and is headquartered in downtown Detroit, Michigan. It is the third-largest pizza chain in the world, with restaurants in each of the 50 U.S. states and 31 countries and territories. 
 
Known for its HOT-N-READY® pizza, Crazy Puffs®, and famed Crazy Bread®, Little Caesars uses quality ingredients, like fresh, never-frozen mozzarella and Muenster cheese and sauce made from fresh-packed, vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. The brand is known for innovation and is home to the exclusive Pizza Portal® pickup, a heated, self-service mobile order pickup station. Little Caesars is also the Official Pizza Sponsor of the NFL. 
 
A high-growth company with over 65 years in the $150 billion worldwide pizza industry, Little Caesars continually looks for franchisee candidates to join the team in markets worldwide. In addition to providing the opportunity for entrepreneurial independence in a franchise system, Little Caesars offers a simple operating system, a reputation for taste and value, and strong brand awareness with one of the most recognized characters in the country, Little Caesar. Little Caesars is proud to be part of the Ilitch Companies family of businesses.
 
For more, visit LittleCaesars.com and follow Little Caesars on TikTok, Instagram, and X.
 
*Limited to top 4 national pizza chains

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby

updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

locations: Chicago, Illinois, US
linkedin_company.about: A TRADITION OF QUALITY for FIVE GENERATIONS. "Give the people what they want." Saverio (Sam) Rosati Nearly a century ago these were the simple words Sam Rosati lived by; little did he know this humble philosophy helped shape the foundation on which Rosati’s Pizza was built. Sam’s father began the family’s rich tradition of serving delicious Italian food to customers in his New York restaurant back in the late 1890’s. After the turn of the century, the family moved to Chicago and opened yet another fine ltalian restaurant featuring “Italian Style Pizza”, a tasty appetizer consisting of homemade tomato sauce served on a crispy piece of bread. In 1927, following in his father’s footsteps, Sam opened his own Italian restaurant in downtown Chicago. When Sam retired, his sons were ready to continue the family tradition. The year was 1964 and pizza in America had evolved and was starting to take off. The first Rosati’s Pizza opened its doors in a suburb of Chicago. In 1970, Rick Rosati, great grandson of Fred Sr., continued the family tradition and opened his own Rosati’s Pizza in Arlington Heights, Illinois. By 1978, a total of ten individual Rosati family members owned Rosati’s Pizza locations. In 1979 the family decided to expand the business and began franchising the Rosati’s Pizza concept. In 1996 Sam Rosati, great great grandson of Fred Sr. opened his first Rosati’s Pizza location in Belvidere, Illinois marking the fifth generation of Rosati family members serving delicious Italian food. Other locations soon followed and Rosati’s Pizza was on the map.

updates.text: So we're back from NACS 2026, and honestly, we were surprised by what we heard on the show floor. It wasn't the sound of pitching, buzzwords, or typical conference chatter. It was the hum of skepticism. Customers had more questions this year than we've ever experienced before. Not because innovation has stalled, but because the stakes feel higher. AI was at the center of many of those conversations. Retailers recognize the opportunity, just as they once recognized the value of SEO. They know it has the potential to drive discovery, efficiency, and growth. What they're still trying to understand is how to capture that value without introducing unnecessary risk. One concern came up repeatedly: Will adding new value cost us the value we've already built? It's a challenge we understand because it's one we face ourselves. Large organizations can't afford to disrupt operations, customer experiences, or business continuity in pursuit of the next trend. That's why we've designed our solutions around a simple belief: innovation shouldn't require a tradeoff. Retailers shouldn't have to choose between what's working today and what will help them compete tomorrow. If you're asking the same questions, let's talk. Our team works with retailers every day to navigate these decisions and identify opportunities that support innovation without disrupting the experiences, operations, and outcomes that already drive success. Book a conversation with our team here: https://lnkd.in/gvFfcYyH

updates.text: Throughout history, every breakthrough has arrived with the same promise: Electricity. The internet. Mobile. Cloud. And now, AI. Each changed the world. But none created value simply because someone bought it. The winners weren't the organizations that adopted the technology first. They were the organizations that understood why they were adopting it. That's what stood out in Nick and Andy's conversation at NACS. Before AI. Before automation. Before modernization. Comes insight. What problem are you solving? What friction are you removing? What customer need are you addressing? Because ROI isn't just Return on Investment. It's the Result of Insight. Technology can accelerate almost anything. The question is whether it's accelerating a clear strategy or simply speeding up confusion. The investment comes after the insight. Not before it. updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: Phil Mauter has been promoted to President, QualServ North America! Yea! In this role, Phil will lead the QualServ North American strategy and oversee the day-to-day operations of all business functions. He is committed to elevating the customer experience while scaling the outstanding QS solutions and services. You can read his announcement here: https://lnkd.in/ec-79V9q Phil joined QualServ in 2021 as VP of operations, then was named General Manager in early 2025. While QS operations have benefitted from his business expertise, Team QualServ knows him as a trusted leader, problem solver, and head cheerleader. He has built a loyal employee base and a positive, can-do culture throughout the organization that strongly resonates with all in the QS orbit. Culture is important to Phil, at work and outside of it. A competitor at heart, Phil often challenges himself by powerlifting and loves to pack up his Jeep for some off-roading, or visiting a calm, cool stream for fly fishing. A Chicago native, Phil’s career has taken him all over the U.S. and world, including a stint in China. Exploring the globe reflects his personal life as well. Phil and his wife, Mindy, love to travel and daughters Amanda and Brianna are often along for the adventure. The stamps in their passports include Italy, the Netherlands, and Belgium with Spain next on their bucket list. When travelling they make it a point to always seek out local cuisine and the oldest pubs to experience the true roots of culture and history at any location. There is a “little girl,” who can do no wrong in the eyes of this powerlifter and off roader, a miniature Dachshund named Eleanor, who is known to be a bit spoiled by her parents. Phil, just reading about you motivates us. You’ve truly built an exceptional team at QualServ who are inspired to serve our customers at the highest level. We know the sky is the limit in your new role! Thanks for spreading good vibes wherever you go!! Congratulations Phil!! #middleby #teammiddleby

updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. Thank you to: Jack Altman , Jason M. Lemkin , Alex Bard , Dylan Field , Fidji Simo , Max Mullen , Shalini Rao , Alex Kurland , Naval Ravikant, Jonathan Neman , Claire Hughes Johnson , Dharmesh Shah , Cory Levy , John Andrew Entwistle, Andrew Steele , Joshua Browder , Sean Rad , Scott Belsky , Brett Schulman , Mike Vichich , Andy Pforzheimer , Harris Pollack , Stephen Kerns, Kimbal Musk , Max Altman , Ben Braverman , Geoff Donaker , Nick Bunick , Alexis Ohanian Sr. , Kipp Bodnar , Ankur Nagpal , Henry Schuck , Parker Conrad , Justin Mateen , Marcus Lemonis , Shaan Puri , Sam Parr , Tanay Tandon , Josh R. on, Josh R. , Immad Akhund , Garrett Langley , Guillermo Rauch . Owner exists to close the gap between small businesses and huge corporations. We’re starting with restaurant owners. They represent the American dream. 80% start as cooks or servers, then become first-time business owners. But they’re forced to compete with massive corporations, which spend billions on tech & marketing and hire entire teams of experts. We don't want local businesses to get crushed. Owner gives AI superpowers to small businesses, doing work they could never afford before, so they can do more than compete. They can win.

That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? It’s a front-row-seat to a movement that Owner is building - over 100 million guests that we’ve been able to bring to small businesses across the country. I really believe local business owners are the most inspiring people on earth, and it’s a privilege to build for them. Today we celebrate a fun milestone, and then we get right back to building for these amazing entrepreneurs. If you want to come build AI for (not against) people - we’re hiring. updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. Authors Haochen W. , Yi H. , and Ryan Xie share the engineering behind this deployment. The work was also presented at the ICML 2026 RLxF workshop. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

updates.text: DoorDash 🤝 Dispatch Goods 🤝 The Story of Stuff Project We ran a really special pilot in City of Half Moon Bay this year: a dozen restaurants swapped single-use containers for ones that get washed, sanitized, returned, and reused. Thousands fewer containers ended up in the trash. The program’s still running, and we’re still tuning it. But reusable packaging is new enough that half the work is just explaining what it is! Thanks Story of Stuff for helping with that. I hope it gets other cities and restaurants excited to try it too.

From neighborhood institutions to local favorites putting their own spin on a classic, meet the pizza spots customers are loving across America. Full list in the comments.

It was real work with real outcomes, backed by a rotation manager and a team invested in his growth. crunchbase.full_description:
ChowNow is an ordering platform dedicated to helping local restaurants grow and compete in a sustainable way. ChowNow helps local restaurants thrive. By helping diners discover the restaurants' delicious creations and helping restaurants connect with customers. ChowNow powers branded online ordering systems for independent restaurants via the restaurants’ own websites, on Facebook and Google pages, through ChowNow-created apps, and via ChowNow’s website, while also providing the restaurant partners key customer insights and marketing support.

The company does its services for a reasonable monthly fee, without the predatory third-party commissions charged by competitors. It also enables diners to connect with independent restaurants in communities to order takeout and in some cases delivery, in a way that’s sustainable and fair to restaurants.

ChowNow was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Playa Vista, California.

crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. Thank you to: Jack Altman , Jason M. Lemkin , Alex Bard , Dylan Field , Fidji Simo , Max Mullen , Shalini Rao , Alex Kurland , Naval Ravikant, Jonathan Neman , Claire Hughes Johnson , Dharmesh Shah , Cory Levy , John Andrew Entwistle, Andrew Steele , Joshua Browder , Sean Rad , Scott Belsky , Brett Schulman , Mike Vichich , Andy Pforzheimer , Harris Pollack , Stephen Kerns, Kimbal Musk , Max Altman , Ben Braverman , Geoff Donaker , Nick Bunick , Alexis Ohanian Sr. , Kipp Bodnar , Ankur Nagpal , Henry Schuck , Parker Conrad , Justin Mateen , Marcus Lemonis , Shaan Puri , Sam Parr , Tanay Tandon , Josh R. on, Josh R. , Immad Akhund , Garrett Langley , Guillermo Rauch . Dean Bloembergen , the team, and I are deeply grateful for everyone who has supported us, including those not tagged here. Owner exists to close the gap between small businesses and huge corporations. We’re starting with restaurant owners. They represent the American dream. 80% start as cooks or servers, then become first-time business owners. But they’re forced to compete with massive corporations, which spend billions on tech & marketing and hire entire teams of experts. We don't want local businesses to get crushed. Owner gives AI superpowers to small businesses, doing work they could never afford before, so they can do more than compete. They can win.

updates.text: So excited to share that Owner.com has closed a $240M Series D led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a $2.3B valuation. Everyone is debating how many jobs AI can cut. That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? I eat at Ashley’s Cafe (pictured) multiple times a week, and seeing the impact of our technology on Ashley’s business has been pure joy. It’s a front-row-seat to a movement that Owner is building - over 100 million guests that we’ve been able to bring to small businesses across the country. I really believe local business owners are the most inspiring people on earth, and it’s a privilege to build for them. Today we celebrate a fun milestone, and then we get right back to building for these amazing entrepreneurs. If you want to come build AI for (not against) people - we’re hiring. Careers page in the comments.

updates.text: We are pleased to announce that our Growth Equity team has led a $240 million financing round in Owner, an AI-native software company building the operations platform for every local business. Owner provides small businesses, starting with restaurants, with access to AI-powered technology and automation capabilities that have historically been accessible only to larger enterprises, helping local business owners manage and grow more efficiently. This investment will help support Owner's continued product innovation and expansion as it scales across the restaurant industry and extends its offerings to new geographies and additional local business categories. Learn more in the press release: http://ms.spr.ly/6046au7Sp

updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
We’ve grown to become the largest family-operated broadline food service distributor in North America by upholding the same business approach since 1897—being passionately committed to the people we serve. We believe in the power of good food—to bring people together and make moments special. Every product, every order, and every decision we make is inspired by the people on the other side of the plate.

We distribute to foodservice operators throughout the Midwest, Northeast, Southeast  and Southwest regions of the U.S. and coast to coast in Canada. 

Our company also operates more than 170 Gordon Food Service Stores, which are open to the public and provide the benefits of restaurant-quality products and friendly, knowledgeable service. Gordon Food Service Stores do not charge a membership fee. 

Gordon Food Service Stores are the primary supplier for many small foodservice operators, including: restaurants, churches, daycare providers, caterers, event planners, and other small businesses. 

We offer a broad range of employment opportunities throughout our corporate offices, distribution centers, and retail stores. We have a strong commitment to our employees and foster an environment that promotes internal growth, training, and career development opportunities. 

Gordon Food Service is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any person on the basis of age, sex, race, religion, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

updates.text: Meet the new SpotOn Handheld, built to handle real restaurant conditions: → all the taps (99.99% card-reading reliability) → all the turns (30% faster than our last) → all the drops (from five feet up, over and over again) → all the splashes and dunks (survives 30 minutes in three feet of water) And we made this film to prove it. Everything you see (and hear) is the real deal. The score is built entirely from the sounds of a working restaurant. The ticket printer became a synth. The fryer became a cymbal. Card taps and clanking dishes became the drums. And we dropped, dunked, and splashed the Handheld right along with it. Available now. updates.text: "It doesn't matter if we have two tables or 20. Crush it. Create something for a guest. They're gonna remember that forever." That's the standard at Port Union, a modern American restaurant in Chicago's Wicker Park from Chef Rodolfo Cuadros. Switching to a new POS wasn't an easy sell for the team. After a long time on one system, the comfort zone was real. SpotOn’s support is what won them over. With brunch about to launch and a whole new menu to build, one call to SpotOn got this answer: "Send me the menu and I'll do it for you." A simple tool to drive reviews mattered too, especially for a new restaurant still building its reputation. With SpotOn Mobile Pay & Review, guests leave a review right as they pay. That helps search visibility and builds trust with the next guest. Hit play for the full story 👇 #ShiftStories #RestaurantTech #RestaurantOwner #Hospitality #ChicagoRestaurants

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

SpotOn’s mission is to give small and midsize businesses a fighting chance, providing innovative software and payment solutions, supported by local and personal service, and delivered at a fair price. A leader in fully integrated restaurant management systems and small business technology, SpotOn offers end-to-end solutions which include marketing, website development, reservations, online ordering, appointments, eCommerce, digital loyalty, review management, as well as retail and restaurant point-of-sale (POS) solutions.

Doron Friedman, Matt Hyman, and Zach Hyman co-founded SpotOn in 2017 and its headquarters is located in San Francisco, California.

products_and_services.product_description: A cloud-based point-of-sale and restaurant management system for processing payments, managing menus and tables, handling orders, and viewing sales and labor reports.
Integrated payment processing for in-person, online, virtual-terminal, and invoicing transactions through SpotOn’s restaurant and small-business systems.
A commission-free online ordering and delivery solution that connects restaurant websites, guest ordering apps, delivery services, menus, payments, and the SpotOn POS.
A POS-integrated labor management platform for scheduling, labor forecasting, employee coordination, tip management, and payroll preparation.
Proprietary restaurant POS hardware including countertop stations, handheld POS devices, guest-facing displays, card readers, printers, cash drawers, and connectivity equipment.
A restaurant reservation and front-of-house management system for online bookings, waitlists, table layouts, guest information, reminders, and POS synchronization.

updates.text: We’ve brought reinforcement learning into DoorDash’s real-time dispatch system to improve batching efficiency while maintaining delivery quality. Trained offline on delayed marketplace outcomes, our RL policy adjusts dispatch objective weights for each merchant. Our existing optimizer handles feasibility and operational constraints. Authors Haochen W. , Yi H. , and Ryan Xie share the engineering behind this deployment. The work was also presented at the ICML 2026 RLxF workshop. updates.text: How do you scale real-time dispatch when demand can exceed processing capacity by nearly 4x? DoorDash engineers rearchitected our dispatch platform from a centralized execution model into a distributed, horizontally scalable system designed for real-time logistics optimization. The new architecture delivers 10x greater throughput, keeps dispatch fast and predictable at peak volume, and creates a foundation for more advanced ML and reinforcement learning in the dispatch loop. In this engineering deep dive, we share how we approached distributed compute, hierarchical decomposition, shadow testing, and production rollout for one of DoorDash’s most latency-sensitive systems. Read the full post: https://lnkd.in/gCaqbmVs

updates.text: DoorDash 🤝 Dispatch Goods 🤝 The Story of Stuff Project We ran a really special pilot in City of Half Moon Bay this year: a dozen restaurants swapped single-use containers for ones that get washed, sanitized, returned, and reused. Thousands fewer containers ended up in the trash. The program’s still running, and we’re still tuning it. But reusable packaging is new enough that half the work is just explaining what it is! Thanks Story of Stuff for helping with that. I hope it gets other cities and restaurants excited to try it too.

And because everyone has an opinion when it comes to pizza, we dug into the data: - Nearly 30 million pizza orders were placed on DoorDash in 2025 - Pepperoni remains America’s most-ordered topping - Orders with caramelized onions and meatballs grew more than 120% year-over-year - Pineapple was ordered more often than olives, bacon, chicken or ham - New York-style was the fastest-growing major pizza style, up more than 80% year-over-year From neighborhood institutions to local favorites putting their own spin on a classic, meet the pizza spots customers are loving across America. Full list in the comments.

updates.text_html:
October is National Pizza Month and we’re celebrating some of the local pizzerias customers love most with our list of 2026 Top Pizza Spots.

And because everyone has an opinion when it comes to pizza, we dug into the data:
- Nearly 30 million pizza orders were placed on DoorDash in 2025
- Pepperoni remains America’s most-ordered topping
- Orders with caramelized onions and meatballs grew more than 120% year-over-year
- Pineapple was ordered more often than olives, bacon, chicken or ham
- New York-style was the fastest-growing major pizza style, up more than 80% year-over-year

From neighborhood institutions to local favorites putting their own spin on a classic, meet the pizza spots customers are loving across America. Full list in the comments.

updates.text: Grubhub is proud to be recognized with the UserTesting Illumi Award for Emerging Innovator — and it came out of one of the biggest moments of our year. We recently made a bold move: removing delivery and service fees on restaurant orders over $50, supported by a campaign during the Big Game. As soon as the campaign launched, we ran three parallel research studies to capture real-time customer reactions. Within 48 hours, we had clear feedback. Customers were excited about the offer, but we identified opportunities to make the experience even stronger. Teams across the business moved quickly to update parts of the app and campaign creative while the campaign was still live. That fast feedback loop helped us improve the customer experience during a high-visibility moment — driving stronger AOV, better brand perception, and a campaign that delivered on its promise. The combination of customer insight, speed, and cross-functional execution helped turn a bold idea into meaningful business impact.

updates.text: Grubhub is proud to be recognized with the UserTesting Illumi Award for Emerging Innovator — and it came out of one of the biggest moments of our year. We recently made a bold move: removing delivery and service fees on restaurant orders over $50, supported by a campaign during the Big Game. As soon as the campaign launched, we ran three parallel research studies to capture real-time customer reactions. Within 48 hours, we had clear feedback. Customers were excited about the offer, but we identified opportunities to make the experience even stronger. Teams across the business moved quickly to update parts of the app and campaign creative while the campaign was still live. That fast feedback loop helped us improve the customer experience during a high-visibility moment — driving stronger AOV, better brand perception, and a campaign that delivered on its promise. The combination of customer insight, speed, and cross-functional execution helped turn a bold idea into meaningful business impact.

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." What that looks like on site: 💻 Intuitive tech that speeds ordering and payments so lines keep moving ✅ Orders right, right on time - even at peak hours 👥 A SpotOn team behind the scenes supporting restaurant vendors between rushes For the restaurants serving there, it's a chance to put their food in front of thousands of new guests. The tech's job is to stay out of the way so the food gets the attention. Watch the full interview 👇 #RestaurantTech #FoodFestival #Hospitality #RestaurantOwner #YesChefFoodFestival

updates.text: A POS without built-in text marketing is like a margarita without tequila. It's basically just a glass full of lime juice and salt. Long gone are the days when a restaurant POS was a sleek cash register. Nearly every customer interaction passes through a modern POS in some form, accumulating a continuous record of guest behavior. When guest communication tools like text marketing are built in to that environment to create a unified marketing engine, marketing messages can be defined by what guests have actually done rather than by static assumptions. If marketing tools need to be bolted on to that environment...lime juice and salt. And did you know that text messages have a 95-99% read rate? For more delicious stats and more about how a modern POS can take advantage of customer behavior data to drive growth, check out this article on SourceForge .

updates.text: Is it time to renew your POS contract? Before you do, here are a few questions worth asking. Does your POS scale? Your system should grow with you — not force you to rebuild menus and workflows every time you open a new store. Does your POS improve accuracy? Does it handle complex modifiers, a high volume of online orders, delivery, and driver dispatch without slowing you down or causing mistakes? Does your POS integrate? Is your team drowning in tablets? If everything lives in separate systems, that’s a workaround that doesn’t really work. Does your POS give you visibility? Can you see at-a-glance what’s happening across all of your stores and can you trust the numbers you’re seeing? Does your POS make you more visible? The customer data YOU ALREADY HAVE should flow seamlessly into a complete marketing and loyalty system. If you answered “no” to any of these questions, your POS isn’t a partner — it’s a problem, and it may be time to consider a refresh. Looking for a real POS partner? HungerRush is the POS partner behind every great guest experience. Get in touch.

updates.text: "A cheese may disappoint. It may be dull, it may be naive, it may be oversophisticated. Yet it remains cheese, milk's leap toward immortality." — Clifton Fadiman If you believe you are what you eat, then National Grilled Cheese Day is the perfect moment to shave off (...or unwrap...) a slice of immortality, melt it between two pieces of bread, and digest the divine. And tomato soup? Like Batman and Robin, Lucy and Ethel, Mario and Luigi, Frodo and Samwise, Han and Chewy, Michael and Dwight, Penny and Brain, Wayne and Garth, Rumi Mira Zoey and Bobby, The Dude and Walter, Pooh and Piglet, Jay and Silent Bob, Fry and Bender, or Wallace and Gromit ( — who were, yes, highly attuned to the lunar immortality of cheese)... While not officially "required" for a proper National Grilled Cheese Day celebration, that steady bowl of tomato soup is the classic lawful-good force multiplier. The OG 10xer. And is now a good time to talk about sourdough being bread's own leap toward immortality as well? Making a grilled cheese on sourdough and dipping it in tomato soup is basically like discovering Mario's infinite lives staircase. If you're reading this on April 12th, today is the day to make an Artemis-like leap toward your own immortality. Looking for other days to celebrate your favorite foods? updates.text: "My mule don't like people laughin'. Gets the crazy notion that people are laughin' at him." Burritos are no laughing matter....especially on NATIONAL BURRITO DAY! The word "burrito" means "little donkey" in Spanish, and while the origins of that name are long debated, there's no doubt that the tightly wrapped bundle of goodness does resemble the bedrolls carried by mules and donkeys in the desert-rambling days of yore. The burrito traces its origins to northern Mexican cooking. They were likely born in Sonora, a wheat-growing region where flour tortillas were the default, and were smaller than the overstuffed, foil-wrapped cathedral of fillings that emerged in San Francisco's Mission District in the 1960s. These days you can tell a burrito by its regional dialect. In Tucson, it is a "burro" and filled with machaca. In Texas, it rolls up at high noon, smothered in enchilada sauce, squinting a challenge for you to quick draw your fork. In New Mexico, you might be asked, "red or green?" In San Diego, there might be shrimp in it. In San Francisco, it is nearly the size of an actual donkey. Rice? No rice? Just veggies? Mushrooms? Salmon?!? Like many dishes we have come to wrap our arms around, the burrito is no longer just one thing. The large flour tortilla is a canvas upon which cooks of different cultures and different cities have been painting for over a century. And while we may laugh together over our burritos, we at HungerRush strongly recommend not laughing at them. Because while you might understand that we were just playin' around, the burrito just doesn't get it. If you are a slinger of burritos, today is your day! Looking for more food holidays to celebrate? We have you covered. We put together a comprehensive National Food Day Calendar worth bookmarking: https://hubs.li/Q049swH00

updates.text: This year Middleby completed its evolution to a standalone commercial foodservice company. While all looked seamless and easy when we made our corresponding announcements, behind the scenes there was a lot of critical heavy lifting to get us there, especially from our financial team. Our Chief Financial Officer Brittany Cerwin ensured all went smoothly in these two major transactions. Promoted earlier this year to CFO, Britt was responsible for leading the financial aspects of the Midera spin off into its own public company and managing the majority sale of our residential business. Her efforts were (and still are) key in strategically positioning Middleby where it is today and for future success. Britt was recently a guest on the CFO Thought Leader podcast to discuss her career path, and why Middleby was a fit for her 15 years ago and today. She discusses the tremendous efforts the Middleby finance department took on over the past year and where Middleby is headed in its new focused strategy. Being a team player we are sharing this photo from the 2026 Women’s Foodservice Forum Leadership Development Conference where Britt is pictured on the lower left. Thanks Britt, for taking the time to share your experience and wisdom. We can all learn from you. You can listen to the podcast here: https://lnkd.in/gvUGuAQD #middleby #middlebycommercial #podcast

updates.text: We are excited to announce that Rachel Mago has been promoted to Senior Vice President of Global Sales and Marketing at Taylor Company! In this expanded role, Rachel will assume responsibility for the sales teams in Europe, APAC, and other global service and sales groups. Rachel has a vast knowledge base, endless enthusiasm, and has successfully built deep connections and trust with Taylor partners and customers. One could say that Rachel was destined to work at Taylor. Growing up in the Pacific Northwest, her first job was at the only custard shop in Washington State! That’s not to say she took a direct line to Taylor, though. A Spanish major in college, Rachel moved to Spain to teach English. Returning home and teaching high school Spanish for a year prompted her to explore a career shift to sales. Rest assured, her Spanish fluency is in use and a definite asset to her current global role. Growing up in the PNW fostered her sense of adventure and love of the outdoors, which has led to several foreign hiking adventures with her husband, Johnny. Check out this cool photo of the pair in Iceland! She always up for travel and adding stamps to her passport. At her Chicago home, Rachel enjoys experimenting with recipes, discovering new restaurants, and tackling the most intricate Legos. Of course, she visits her family in the PNW as much as possible. Congratulations, Rachel, on your promotion. We sure hope that custard shop can see you now! Read Rachel’s announcement here: https://lnkd.in/gp7-dQTS #middleby #teammiddleby #thisismiddleby

updates.text: Thousands of guests. Dozens of restaurant vendors. One day to get it right. That's Yes Chef Food Festival in New York, where SpotOn was the official restaurant technology partner. We asked NYC food creator Alyssa La Spisa (The Recommendista on those other platforms 😉 ) to cover the festival for us, and she started with founder Jack Goldburg what it takes to run an event at this scale. His answer comes down to speed. "You don't want the lines to be long." crunchbase.full_description:
Papa Gino's is a web and mobile-based online food ordering platform that provides a wide range of authentic Italian taste pizzas for individuals.

Papa Gino's uses ingredients such as locally-milled hard winter wheat flour, water, yeast, salt, and oil to make pizzas and the specially crafted tomato sauce is made from vine-ripened California crushed tomatoes. Their signature blend of three premium cheeses for an authentic pizza is also used in the process. It offers its users with catering and delivery services as well as gluten free food for a healthy lifestyle. The company allows its users to send personalized eGift cards that individuals can select the layout of the card as well.

Papa Gino's was launched in 1961 by Michael Valerio and the company is based in the United States.

updates.text: There's more to every nut than meets the eye. This National Nut Day, we want to highlight the powerhouse that is the peanut. The journey of a peanut begins long before it reaches consumers. Unlike many crops, peanuts grow underground, where the developing pods mature beneath the soil after flowering above ground. From planting and harvesting to shelling, sorting, and processing, every peanut passes through numerous stages before reaching kitchens around the world. Few foods are as versatile as the peanut. Found in snacks, meals, desserts, and food products enjoyed worldwide, peanuts have become a staple ingredient across generations and cultures. Research has highlighted the wide range of nutritional compounds found in peanuts and the many ways they are used throughout the food industry. While they may be small, peanuts have a big story to tell. Today, we're celebrating the journey of this nut and the many people who help bring it from the field to consumers' tables every day.

linkedin_company.about: For over 100 years, Shamrock Foods Company has worked to ensure people come first – our 5,000+ associates, our customers, and the families we serve across the nation. A privately held, family-owned and -operated Forbes 500 company, Shamrock is an innovator in the food industry and has been since its founding in Arizona in 1922. Shamrock specializes in the manufacturing and distribution of quality food and food-related products through a family of companies, including Shamrock Foods foodservice distribution and Shamrock Farms dairy manufacturing, among others. Now led by the third generation of McClelland family leadership, Shamrock’s success is built upon three unwavering principles set forth by our founder, W.T. McClelland: An unwavering commitment to quality people, products, and service; innovation in everything we do; and commitment to the communities we are privileged to serve. Our unique company culture is guided by the motto to “treat associates as family, and customers and suppliers as friends.” Learn more about our products, philosophy, and current job openings at https://jobs.shamrockfoods.com.

updates.text: Arizona’s Hometown Dairy We're excited to kick off another season of the Shamrock Farms Farm Tour! As a family-owned company with more than 100 years rooted in dairy farming, we're proud to welcome thousands of students, families and community members each year to experience agriculture firsthand. Since opening our farm to the public in 2005, we've welcomed more than 150,000 visitors to learn how we care for our cows and where the pure, fresh milk in Shamrock Farms' delicious dairy products comes from. Located in Stanfield, Arizona, our milk travels less than an hour to our Phoenix production facility. It's a local farm-to-table story we're proud to share. Ready to see it for yourself? crunchbase.full_description:
Shamrock’s rich heritage began when W.T. McClelland (Mr. Mac), son of an Irish farmer, immigrated to the U.S. and bought a small dairy business in 1922 to serve a handful of customers in the Tucson area. His wife, Sara Winifred (Winnie) became the bookkeeper and christened the new business Shamrock Dairy. Together, Mr. Mac and Winnie forged an American success story.

After World War II, Shamrock Dairy built a processing plant in Phoenix and launched continuous expansion programs in both facility development and product line. Over the years, the product line has emerged to include frozen foods, fresh fruits and vegetables, meats, fish and institutional foodservice supplies and equipment.

Today, Shamrock Foods Company is the umbrella for Shamrock Farms, the largest dairy in the Southwest, and Shamrock Foods, a nationally-ranked foodservice distributor. Now headquartered in Phoenix, Shamrock sends refrigerated trucks to 9 other states from distribution centers in Phoenix, Arizona, Commerce City (Denver), Colorado and Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Eastvale, California.

updates.text: We were proud to join Northside Economic Opportunity Network (NEON) for its 20th Anniversary Celebration and be among the inaugural recipients of its Angel Awards, recognizing the companies and civic leaders whose partnership and investment have helped advance NEON’s mission to build wealth for low- to moderate-income entrepreneurs in North Minneapolis. Since 2016, General Mills has supported NEON through philanthropy, food-industry expertise and GoodWorks pro-bono projects, where our employees lend their skills and knowledge to help local business owners grow their operations. This support contributes to NEON’s work through programs like its Food Business Incubator and Collective Kitchens, which help food entrepreneurs access the resources they need to grow. We’re grateful to celebrate this milestone alongside NEON’s entrepreneurs, team, community partners and fellow supporters — and a special thank you to our General Mills Community Impact team for the leadership and dedication they bring to this work and to the North Minneapolis community. #GStandsForGood #CommunityImpact #Philanthropy

updates.text: This morning, General Mills’ board of directors announced that Dana McNabb, current chief operating officer, will become our next CEO, succeeding Jeff Harmening, who will become executive chair of the board of directors, effective January 1, 2027. Dana has made significant contributions across her 27 years at General Mills, having led in senior positions across the company and around the world. As current COO, she leads all four operating segments and key functions, with a focus on our consumers and delivering growth. She is a proven, results-driven leader with a deep understanding of our business, our brands and our industry. We’re incredibly grateful to Jeff for his 32 years of impact at General Mills and the strong foundation he laid for our next chapter. Learn more here: https://lnkd.in/e7uW3tyu

updates.text: September was full of moments that brought our people and communities together. 💙 As part of Familia Heritage Month, employees volunteered with CLUES (Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio), to put together school-supply kits for local students. We also celebrated 20 years of the Mill City Farmers Market, where General Mills has been a founding funder and longtime supporter. At our World Headquarters, employees, families and friends laced up for our annual Run of the Mills, while current and former Pillsbury colleagues came together for the Funster event to share stories and celebrate the brand’s legacy. Meanwhile, the Edgard & Cooper team brought sustainability and a shared love of pets to life at Upcycled & Unleashed, where adoptable pups took the runway in upcycled designs. We also connected with fellow Minnesota leaders at the Minnesota Business Partnership event to talk about the future of our state. From giving back to celebrating the connections that bring us together, these are a few of the moments that made September special. #MillsMonthlyMoments #GeneralMillsLife

updates.text: As we continue to pursue our long-term ambition of engineering trailblazing cooking product, we are proud to announce a new chapter in our leadership. To steer our 10-year strategy and next phase of global growth, we are thrilled to welcome former Volvo Cars CEO and Dyson CEO Jim Rowan , as our new Chair of the Board, effective 1st August 2026. Jim brings decades of international leadership from some of the world’s most innovative, design-led businesses. Throughout his career, he has successfully scaled premium, engineering-led consumer brands across complex global markets. He joins the Board alongside formalised Non-Executive Directors, Ruth Chandler (Board Advisor at Skyscanner and executive coach) and Scott Maguire (President and Chief Operating Officer of On). Together, they bring extensive global experience across innovation, people and commercial success. Darina Garland , Co-Founder of Ooni, shared: “Since the early days of Ooni we made the strategic decision to have a board of advisors, to bring together world-class experience that would challenge, support and steer us into the next level. Today we are so excited to bring this group of global stars into Ooni. We leaned into our value of ambition and had a rigorous process to find these board advisors and our new Chair. Jim is an exceptional leader, and we’re delighted to have him as Chair.” Jim succeeds Paul Ross who is stepping down after eight years in the position. During his tenure, Paul has played an important role in guiding growth and development, leaving a strong foundation for the future. We are immensely grateful for everything he has done for the business. #Ooni #Leadership #ExecutiveLeadership #BoardOfDirectors

updates.text: Film photography is more than 150 years old, yet modern technology has allowed it to thrive to this day. Sound familiar? For more than a century, our cooperative has been built and strengthened by the hard work of generations of member-owners. No matter the challenge, we continue to adapt to meet the needs of modern agriculture. The beauty of film photography is its ability to preserve a moment while reminding us of the story behind it. This National Farmer's Day, we're celebrating what it means to be Rooted In Tomorrow through a unique lens: specifically, the lens of a Houghton Ensign-Cupid film camera that's just one year younger than our 105-year-old cooperative. Take a look at two modern member farms captured through a piece of history and see how the cooperative model continues to connect the past, present and future of agriculture. https://spr.ly/6045BHBLmD

updates.text: Film photography -- an art form that’s more than 150 years old -- has been able to evolve and adapt, enabling it to thrive in a modern era. Land O'Lakes, Inc. has lasted more than 100 years because of the durability of the cooperative model, the resiliency of our member-owners and their willingness to evolve and adapt. With traditions rooted in generations of family farming, they’re able to augment age-old farming methods with cutting-edge technology to keep up with the demands of a modern, global food system. “I think of it often when I’m working in the field. I know that field has been worked by someone in my family for the last 150 years, and I’ve got a grandkid riding with me in the tractor. That’s what American agriculture is all about. It’s more than an occupation. It’s a lifestyle and commitment to feeding the planet.” Sift through more photos of a modern farm captured through a 100-year-old camera right here: https://lnkd.in/gSYAWabz

We got to work in 2005, sending text message orders to printers—two years before the iPhone would change the world. While the hospitality industry is still in the early innings of its digital transformation, we remain committed over two decades later to helping restaurants scale online ordering and delivery, make data-driven business decisions, and personalize the guest experience on- and off-premise. As a leading restaurant technology provider, we reach more than 100 million connected guests across approximately 90,000 locations, processing more than 3.5 million orders per day on average. With integrations to over 400 technology partners, our customers can build digital experiences with the largest and most flexible restaurant commerce ecosystem on the market. Over 800 restaurant brands trust Olo to grow their sales, do more with less, and make every guest feel like a regular.

updates.text: It’s a momentous week for Share Our Strength’s No Kid Hungry campaign thanks to Olo CEO Noah Glass ushering corporate philanthropy into the 21st century. Olo announced the Olo App, giving customers a smarter way to order from their favorite restaurants. Launching with more than 250 national and regional restaurant brands - and with new brands joining the app daily - the Olo App allows customers to browse, order and reorder from the restaurants they love and pay the prices they expect, without menu item markups. The Olo App also makes it easy for customers to support No Kid Hungry during checkout. Customers ordering through the Olo App can round up their purchase to the nearest dollar to benefit No Kid Hungry’s effort to end childhood hunger in the United States. Consumer round-ups for good causes have long existed but the new Olo App brings the practice to scale in a new and unprecedented way to which nothing else compares. But this way of thinking is not new to Noah. Just listen to our podcast conversation to learn the deep roots of Noah’s social entrepreneurship and business savvy. https://lnkd.in/gGFdQfgA And by all means, download the new app! https://lnkd.in/g86a5j4g Thank you Noah Glass , Justin Capozzo , and the entire amazing team at Olo . You can learn more about other social innovations by subscribing for free to my weekly Substack column https://lnkd.in/enmJmCk6 (I donate all funds from paid subscriptions to support our work or other nonprofits.) #NoKidHungry #hunger #philanthropy #corporate#philanthropy #socialentrepreneurship #innovation #technology #restaurants #culinary #hospitality #hospitalityatscale

updates.text: I used the Olo app for the first time tonight and since everybody on planet earth feels the need to give their opinion on a company trying new things, I figured I’d join the crowd 🤣. There’s clearly something here. A marketplace style platform that doesn’t silo the customer into one single delivery service is good for users, and it’s good for restaurants. It means the cheapest delivery possible for the restaurant, and the fastest food possible for the customer. Win win. I’ve heard a lot of chatter around how this impacts restaurants and competing technology platforms, but I haven’t heard much about how it impacts the end user. Isn’t that who we should all be trying to help at the end of the day? Now obviously, there are going to be holes in the product on day one. As with any new product, you have to feel out your users and mold to features they’re asking for. That will come with time and if Noah Glass has shown us anything, it’s that his team will figure it out. That said, there are some features I already really enjoy. The live delivery screen is what I would consider “delightful”. It’s easy to understand and gives me all of the information I’m looking for without overloading my screen. One thing I think we all need to remember is that helping end customers helps restaurants. If a platform can deliver a better customer experience, the user will associate that experience with the brand, not only the platform. I’m excited to see where Olo takes the product next. And a reminder to some of the harsher critics out there, building things in this industry is hard. We should be supporting and learning from each other because the more we do, the better products our customers will get to enjoy. #RestaurantTech
