updates.text: 48 hours ago, we launched the Olo App. Since then, I’ve read every comment, article, and DM. I’ve answered as many questions as I can. Here are the four I see most: “Isn’t this just another third-party marketplace?” No. It’s a network, not a marketplace, for good reason. Every order hits the restaurant’s kitchen exactly like a first-party order with zero commission. The brand keeps the guest relationship and the data. The Olo App brings restaurants together as a coalition. “Will people really download another app?” 40 million guests already have an Olo Account. Sign in with your email or mobile number, and your favorite brands, order history, delivery addresses, and payment details come with you. We built this for the big middle: guests who love variety and don’t want to pay 15-30% more for it. “Isn’t the 5% fee just a commission by another name?” No. The guest pays 5% on top of the product subtotal. The restaurant pays zero commission and keeps the full profit of a first-party order. We show the fee at the top of the menu and again at checkout. Want the absolute lowest price? Order direct from the brand—we tell you that in the fee breakdown at checkout. “Who delivers?” More than two dozen delivery service providers through Olo Dispatch. We built delivery-as-a-service over a decade ago and have scaled it ever since. Those years also gave us answers to the hard questions on driver accountability, handoffs, and reconciliation. The Olo App is not an all-encompassing solution today. Circle back with us in 2030. We have big plans we’re already working toward. Until then: feedback and iteration. Miles to go before we sleep! 🚀

updates.text: YESTERDAY we launched the OLO APP and you can download it now!! https://lnkd.in/gQY7tTAd For years restaurant brands have been (rightfully) pissed about the math on third-party marketplaces. The commissions eat the margin, someone else owns the guest, and the data never comes back to you. Consumers, on the other hand, haven't been pissed enough paying these huge premiums over actual menu prices, but they're catching on. In a year where AI changes what’s possible every day, I present something simpler: a restaurant ordering app that shifts the economics back toward you and the actual restaurants you love. Someone had to change the paradigm (s/o red rising lol) because the existing battlefield was screwing over everyone. Instead of an algorithm floating an ad to the top for a restaurant 10 miles away, how about a map that shows you local favorites that have pickup or delivery available down the road. That's a better experience for everyone involved, especially the food that's traveling, and it's more sustainable too. With 15-30% lower costs for the consumer. 15-30% lower costs!! linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
Olo was born out of a simple idea: What if you could order and pay for a coffee from your phone and have it ready upon arrival at the cafe? We got to work in 2005, sending text message orders to printers—two years before the iPhone would change the world.

While the hospitality industry is still in the early innings of its digital transformation, we remain committed over two decades later to helping restaurants scale online ordering and delivery, make data-driven business decisions, and personalize the guest experience on- and off-premise.

As a leading restaurant technology provider, we reach more than 100 million connected guests across approximately 90,000 locations, processing more than 3.5 million orders per day on average.

With integrations to over 400 technology partners, our customers can build digital experiences with the largest and most flexible restaurant commerce ecosystem on the market.

Over 800 restaurant brands trust Olo to grow their sales, do more with less, and make every guest feel like a regular.

updates.text: From leading Consumer FP&A to owning financial forecasting for all consumer and revenue-generating business segments at Yelp, Abby's scope at Yelp has grown quickly since joining in 2022. During her time here, she also welcomed two children and says the support from her team made all the difference. "I felt massively supported by my team, whether they were in the same stage of life or not, and knew that I'd be able to continue to grow my career here." And when asked why she continues to choose Yelp every day? "Yelp in general is full of really smart, motivated people who aren't willing to just sit and ride with the status quo. updates.text: Mikayla joined Yelp in 2017 as her first job out of college. After a year as an Account Executive, she moved into Local Sales leadership, where she earned President's Club twice and Quarterly Top 10 Manager ten times over six years. Almost a year later, she's still here and says it's the most she's grown both professionally and personally. She compares sales to marathon training: you put in the work every day without immediately seeing results, you can't let one tough day define you, and so much of it comes down to mindset and continuing to show up. crunchbase.full_description:
Blaze Pizza leads in the fast-casual artisan pizza category that uses an assembly line format to create pizzas at lightning fast speed.

Each Blaze Pizza restaurant makes its own dough from scratch using a recipe that requires a 24-hour fermentation period to produce its signature light-as-air, crisp crust. Guests watch as each perfectly proofed dough ball is pressed into a generous 12-inch crust. Pizzas are made in front of the customer using an assembly line format and are ready in two minutes. Blaze Pizza's menu also features signature salads, fresh lemonades, craft beer and wine and house-made S'more Pies, and also offers gluten-free dough and vegan cheese.

updates.text: Growth starts with people. In the latest episode of Food for Thought, Jane Wakely , Chief Consumer and Marketing Officer and Chief Growth Officer, International Foods at PepsiCo, shares what it takes to build enduring brands and drive growth in a world where consumer behavior is evolving faster than ever. From human insight and creativity to cultural relevance and commercial impact, great marketers do more than build brands. They architect growth. At PepsiCo, that means meeting people where they are, showing up in the moments that matter, and creating meaningful connections through the brands they love. One key takeaway from Jane: human-centricity will continue to matter most. And for the next generation of marketers, don't chase fads. Create trends.

linkedin_company.unformatted_about:
PepsiCo is a playground for curious people. We invite thinkers, doers, and changemakers to champion innovation, take calculated risks, and challenge the status quo. From executives to team members on the front lines, we’re excited about the future. We take chances. Together, we dare to make the world a better place.
 
Our associates are the magic ingredient. Each of them plays an integral role in helping create deep connections between people and our products. Think about your last group celebration: Chances are, one of our iconic brands was by your side. At PepsiCo, you’re invited to be a part of a global team of innovators who make, move, and sell these products—which are enjoyed by more than 1 billion people a day.
 
A career at PepsiCo means working in a culture where everyone’s welcome. Here, you can dare to be yourself. No matter who you are or where you’re from, you can influence the people around you and the world at large. By showing up, you’ll have the opportunity to learn, develop and grow your skills for the future. Our supportive teams can fuel your professional goals to make a global impact on people and the planet. 

Join us. Dare for Better.

linkedin_company.about: Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together. So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality through Afterpay, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next-generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale. Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business and helping sellers worldwide do the same. Square is part of Block, Inc. (NYSE: SQ), a global technology company with a focus on financial services.

updates.text: Great full-service restaurants are hospitality businesses first. For our latest campaign, the most compelling story we could tell was already happening inside these restaurants. Rather than tell it ourselves, we let their words and experiences lead. We partnered with three of LA's most iconic full-service restaurants: Ètra, Bar Étoile, and Stir Crazy. These are restaurants the hospitality industry looks to, places that have helped shape what modern full-service looks like. We went in without a script and asked them one question: what does it take to run a great restaurant? Those conversations became our latest film - a story about the business of hospitality, told by the people living it every day. Thanks to Evan Algorri , Andrew Lawson , Jill Bernheimer , Julian Kurland , and Mackenzie Hoffman for sharing their stories.

updates.text: Our SVP of Software Engineering, Ramakrishnan Jayaraman , was featured in Food & Wine on how AI is shaping restaurant menu pricing. A few lines made the article. Here’s more of how we think about it. Ram’s point: what AI changes is precision and scale. A model can see how guests respond to each item at each store. Most people assume that it only pushes prices up. It doesn’t. A good model also finds where visits are slipping and recommends a lower price or a value bundle to bring guests back. That’s different from dynamic pricing, where prices change by time of day. Ram calls that a separate approach, with much higher risk to guest trust. Three things we’d add: 1. 𝐀 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐢𝐟𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐣𝐨𝐛𝐬. For example, a model might show that a combo is underperforming in 40 stores. A person decides what to do. Brands should record both: what the system recommended and what the operator chose. That record is how you explain a price to a guest, a franchisee, or a regulator. 2. 𝐌𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐯𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐚𝐬 𝐰𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐚𝐬 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧. As Ram put it, if guests feel pricing is working against them, they visit less, and the margin gain disappears. Counting orders is easy. Knowing whether the same guest came back is harder, especially when they order in the app one week and at the counter the next. Guests who sign in to loyalty or redeem an offer tied to their account can be recognized across app, web, kiosk, and at the counter. They’re only part of the guest base, but they show which way visits are moving. The more guests a brand can recognize, the clearer the picture. 3. 𝐀𝐈 𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐡𝐞𝐜𝐤 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐜𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 Recommendation engines change what guests see, not what they pay. Suggesting a side that pairs with an order, or featuring what’s selling at a given store, lifts the average check without touching the menu price. That’s the idea behind our AI-powered Recommender. Today, the clearest win for AI pricing is finding the stores and guests where a targeted value offer brings visits back. Operators, where do you draw the line between a pricing recommendation and a pricing decision? Full Food & Wine piece in the comments. #RestaurantTech #AI #QSR #Foodservice #RestaurantIndustry

updates.text: Kyle McPhee started at Papa Murphy's International 's at 18, making $6 an hour. Twenty-five years later, he's the chain's largest owner in Utah with 15 locations –– plus two more in Wyoming –– and the eighth-largest brand owner in the country. This month, he opened his newest store in Eagle Mountain with a new business partner: his 20-year-old son, Aydon. What makes his operation work: 140 employees, mostly teens in their first jobs, with a low turnover rate. His approach is simple -- "I just manage the way I would want to be treated." McPhee's stores are embedded in their communities. They sponsor elementary school spirit nights, provide pizzas to local charter schools, support the Oakley Rodeo, and contribute to employees' own sports fundraisers. Now a second generation of employees is walking through his doors -- the kids of former workers are asking to be hired. "I always joke that they keep me young," he said. Full story from the Salt Lake Business Journal. https://lnkd.in/g9uiWMF6

updates.text: Securing Uber reaches far beyond the app on your phone. 3 months into the role, Philip Martin , our Chief Information Security Officer, shares 3 things that have stood out 👇 🌐 The range of problems to solve "Most people know Uber through rides or delivery. Since joining, I’ve gotten a much deeper appreciation for the range of problems behind that experience: identity, payments, infrastructure, AI, and an increasingly connected physical world. If you like working across disciplines, there’s an extraordinary amount to dig into here." 🤖 The chance to rethink security with AI "What’s exciting here is that we get to work on both sides of AI: helping Uber use it responsibly, and using it to make security itself better. That creates an opportunity to rethink how we identify risk, investigate threats, and respond, not just make the same processes a little faster." 💚 The impact of security here is unusually tangible "Our work connects directly to people’s everyday lives. Protecting this platform means protecting the trust of someone getting home, a courier making a delivery, or a driver earning a living. The scale is impressive; the human connection is what makes it meaningful." #WhatMovesUs

updates.text: Great to welcome Greg Brockman to Uber HQ this week! We’ve partnered with OpenAI for several years, and it’s exciting to see how far AI has come and what it makes possible for our business. Following a 1,000-person pilot, we’re rolling out ChatGPT Work from OpenAI for Business to every Uber employee, giving teams new ways to solve problems, simplify complex work, and get more done. We’re already seeing the impact. Earlier this year, we introduced AI pods, pairing AI engineers with teams across Uber to rethink how work gets done. One team reduced the time needed for a capital allocation process spanning 150 cities from 15 hours to just 30 minutes. That’s the promise of applied AI: combining powerful technology with our people’s expertise to find better ways of working and make a real impact across our business. At Uber, we’re always looking for ways to build, learn, and improve. We’re excited to bring these tools to more of our teams and see what they do with them.

updates.text: Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico, a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas. 2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança. 3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente. 4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias. 5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema. Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução. 7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais. 8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas. 9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos. 10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗
updates.title: Silvia Penna
updates.text_html:
Essa semana completei 10 anos de Uber. 

Essa viagem começou na operação de campo em Belo Horizonte, em 2016, até assumir a cadeira de Diretora-Geral no Brasil. Ao fazer a transição da linha de frente da execução para o desenho estratégico,  a principal certeza que carrego é que liderar é um aprendizado diário. 

Para celebrar esse marco, decidi compartilhar 10 coisas que aprendi – e desaprendi – nesse período: 

1. A rua ensina o que os relatórios não mostram. Ter começado com a "barriga no balcão" me ensinou que as decisões precisam funcionar no cotidiano real das pessoas.

2. Vulnerabilidade é sinal de coragem. Aprendi que ser transparente, autêntica e vulnerável constrói confiança.

3. A melhor tecnologia é aquela que "desaparece". A tecnologia mais impactante é aquela que se torna invisível na experiência do cliente.

4. Ideias valem mais do que a hierarquia. A cultura organizacional acelera a experiência quando valorizamos a diversidade de repertório e as boas ideias.

5. Nosso cliente é um ecossistema.  Precisamos gerar valor para motoristas e passageiros. A equação mágica está no equilíbrio dessa dinâmica. 

6. A estratégia é só o começo. O verdadeiro desafio está em transformá-la em execução.

7. A inovação ganha força no contexto local. Os melhores produtos nascem da união entre escala global e entendimento das necessidades locais.

8. Diversidade não é símbolo, é qualidade de decisão. Ampliar a presença feminina em cargos de liderança é melhorar a nossa leitura do mundo para criar produtos mais aderentes à vida das pessoas.

9. A maternidade e a liderança se potencializam. Viver a minha licença-maternidade de forma integral após assumir o cargo me ensinou a importância de formar times autônomos.

10. Esteja 100% presente. O equilíbrio se mede em intencionalidade. Estar 100% focada quando estou com o meu filho me traz a clareza mental necessária para exercer uma liderança com mais empatia, escuta e assertividade ao retornar ao trabalho. 

Conectar milhões de pessoas todos os dias é um desafio enorme e um privilégio sem tamanho. Muito obrigada aos parceiros, aos usuários e a todo o brilhante time da Uber que faz essa viagem cinco estrelas acontecer todos os dias. 🚀🚗

updates.text: Owner’s Head of AI Developer Experience, Max Schwenk , writes about tsrs: a Rust port of TypeScript’s typechecker that cut our monorepo’s typecheck from 80 seconds to 7 seconds. Cloudflare and VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare) are taking over tsrs as part of Oxc, in close collaboration with the TypeScript team. Coding agents wrote tsrs. In our codebase, it was 9.8× faster and used 6.6× less memory than Typescript 7.0 Previously, even with 36 GiB of memory, engineers couldn't run several agents in parallel without risking their machine locking up. We came up with mitigations, none of which seemed like a long-term scalable solution. tsrs allows us to run more agents working in parallel on our laptops and in our cloud sandboxes. For Owner, these typecheck and lint changes are projected to save hundreds of thousands of dollars a year. Across large TypeScript codebases, that could add up to hundreds of millions over time. How tsrs came together: https://lnkd.in/gNJ4RTEP

updates.text: I've joined Owner as Chief Revenue Officer. I've spent my career thinking about what makes a company worth building, and for me, it always starts with the customer. Local business owners are some of the most inspiring people there are. They took a chance on a dream, they serve their communities, and they are trying to build something that lasts. They deserve the benefits of scale and technology, and for too long, technology has failed to serve them. That is what drew me to Owner. Restaurants, where we are starting, are a massive market, and the problem Owner solves is both simple to say and very hard to do. Systematic growth for local businesses. More traffic, more conversion, more repeat customers. What also drew me in is how Owner builds. There is a real difference between a traditional software company sprinkling in AI so it can call itself an AI company and a company that is genuinely AI-native. Owner is the second kind. I have been blown away by our product velocity. The average engineer here is 400% more productive than they were even back in November of 2025, and we have pulled half of our 2027 roadmap forward into today. That creates a rare and exciting set of go-to-market problems. The question is not "when will the product ship and how do we sell it?" It is "how do we build a go-to-market system that can absorb this pace of innovation and transmit that value to the customer as fast as we create it?" There is no playbook for that. And that is exactly what makes this such an extraordinary time to build at Owner. I'm grateful for the opportunity to build with the incredible team here. The passion, energy, and talent in this organization are truly unique, and it's a privilege to build alongside them. A special thanks to Adam Guild and Rob Lehman for their partnership through the process and their trust in me. We are hiring across the go-to-market organization. Check out the roles, and let us know if you want to be part of a truly extraordinary company. Link in the comments.

updates.text: Owner has raised $240M, reached a $2.3B valuation, and crossed $100M ARR. Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the round, joined by Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, & Jack Altman. The world is racing to build AI to replace people’s jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: To do the jobs for small business owners they’ve never been able to afford. I started building what would become Owner at 17, to help my mom. We've now helped thousands of local business owners like her. This year alone, more than $1 billion dollars will be made by local restaurant owners using Owner. We wouldn’t be here without our team, investors, and earliest supporters. Thank you to: Jack Altman , Jason M. Lemkin , Alex Bard , Dylan Field , Fidji Simo , Max Mullen , Shalini Rao , Alex Kurland , Naval Ravikant, Jonathan Neman , Claire Hughes Johnson , Dharmesh Shah , Cory Levy , John Andrew Entwistle, Andrew Steele , Joshua Browder , Sean Rad , Scott Belsky , Brett Schulman , Mike Vichich , Andy Pforzheimer , Harris Pollack , Stephen Kerns, Kimbal Musk , Max Altman , Ben Braverman , Geoff Donaker , Nick Bunick , Alexis Ohanian Sr. , Kipp Bodnar , Ankur Nagpal , Henry Schuck , Parker Conrad , Justin Mateen , Marcus Lemonis , Shaan Puri , Sam Parr , Tanay Tandon , Josh R. on, Josh R. , Immad Akhund , Garrett Langley , Guillermo Rauch . Dean Bloembergen , the team, and I are deeply grateful for everyone who has supported us, including those not tagged here. Owner exists to close the gap between small businesses and huge corporations. We’re starting with restaurant owners. They represent the American dream. 80% start as cooks or servers, then become first-time business owners. But they’re forced to compete with massive corporations, which spend billions on tech & marketing and hire entire teams of experts. We don't want local businesses to get crushed. Owner gives AI superpowers to small businesses, doing work they could never afford before, so they can do more than compete. They can win.

updates.text: So excited to share that Owner.com has closed a $240M Series D led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a $2.3B valuation. Everyone is debating how many jobs AI can cut. That’s why it has been so motivating to spend every day asking a very different question: how we can use AI to help independent business owners grow and create jobs? I eat at Ashley’s Cafe (pictured) multiple times a week, and seeing the impact of our technology on Ashley’s business has been pure joy. It’s a front-row-seat to a movement that Owner is building - over 100 million guests that we’ve been able to bring to small businesses across the country. I really believe local business owners are the most inspiring people on earth, and it’s a privilege to build for them. Today we celebrate a fun milestone, and then we get right back to building for these amazing entrepreneurs. If you want to come build AI for (not against) people - we’re hiring. Careers page in the comments.

Owner provides small businesses, starting with restaurants, with access to AI-powered technology and automation capabilities that have historically been accessible only to larger enterprises, helping local business owners manage and grow more efficiently. updates.text: Excited to share I've joined Owner.com as Chief Talent Officer! Across my time building teams, one thing has been constant: it all comes down to exceptional people with big ambitions. So when thinking about my next chapter, I looked for three things. #1 - A mission I'd be proud of. So much of AI today lives on screens, chatbots, copilots, tools for people who already work in tech. Owner is bringing AI to the real world. The taqueria on your corner. The family pizza shop. The physical spaces where people actually gather, eat, and live. These owners are experts at their craft, but they're competing against chains with entire technology teams. Owner puts that same firepower in their hands, so they can stay competitive and succeed. #2 - A massive opportunity. Local business is one of the largest and most human parts of the economy, and it's been severely underserved. AI will change that, and will shape what our neighborhoods and main streets look like for decades. Owner is building tools that raise a business owner's odds of success. Starting with restaurants, and eventually every local business. #3 - People I'd be lucky to work with. Adam Guild and Dean have built a company centered on exceptional talent, anchored by a value that immediately struck me: "Bring good energy." Every conversation with Rob , Quenton , Lauren , William , Katie , Darrin , Wyatt and the team confirmed it. These are people you want to spend long hours and late nights with. They obsess over customers, move with urgency, and hold an exceptionally high bar I'm excited to protect and raise. Grateful to everyone over the years who have shaped how I think about talent. And to the Ownerds who've been so welcoming, we are building something epic! Of course, we're hiring. Come build with us!

crunchbase.full_description:
ChowNow is an ordering platform dedicated to helping local restaurants grow and compete in a sustainable way. ChowNow helps local restaurants thrive. By helping diners discover the restaurants' delicious creations and helping restaurants connect with customers. ChowNow powers branded online ordering systems for independent restaurants via the restaurants’ own websites, on Facebook and Google pages, through ChowNow-created apps, and via ChowNow’s website, while also providing the restaurant partners key customer insights and marketing support.

The company does its services for a reasonable monthly fee, without the predatory third-party commissions charged by competitors. It also enables diners to connect with independent restaurants in communities to order takeout and in some cases delivery, in a way that’s sustainable and fair to restaurants.

ChowNow was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in Playa Vista, California.
